1.name: ScadAnnotation
1.documentation:
Concrete Annotation for OpenSCAD-oriented member and facet directives in MachineBlocks.
preferredAlias is scad. Authoring documents bind xmlns:scad to this FQN.

Directives:
• Property (name="*") — member QNames such as <properties><scad:value/> (catalog metadata)
• Value (name="value") — PropertyDefinition value-field facets nested under a property
  (<myProp><scad:value>…</scad:value></myProp>) — not a member scad:myProp
• Document (name="document") — scad:document prose facets
• Summary (name="summary") — scad:summary prose facets
• Examples (name="examples") — scad:examples containers (independent OpenSCAD sample sets)
• Example (name="example") — scad:example sibling under canonical <examples> (1:1 pair)

Parent context disambiguates <scad:value>: under <properties> → Property member;
nested under a property element → Value facet. Parent context for <scad:example>:
direct child of <examples> → Example facet entry (sibling of <example>).
Orthogonal to Definition — does not alter MBEnum or StructuralDefinition shape; it
formalizes the annotation namespace those QNames resolve through.

2.fqnText: com machineblocks bml annotation ScadAnnotation Document
2.name: Document
2.documentation:
Element directive scad:document — OpenSCAD-specific document prose facet.
Does not satisfy the required default-namespace documentation slot on Definitions.
2.idea: An OpenSCAD document prose facet directive

3.fqnText: com machineblocks bml annotation ScadAnnotation Example
3.name: Example
3.documentation:
Element directive scad:example — OpenSCAD body as a sibling of canonical
<example> under the same <examples> container. Requires title (match the paired
BML example). Typically language="OpenSCAD" with CDATA body. Prefer over a parallel
scad:examples list when the sample is a paired render of the same usage.
3.idea: An OpenSCAD example entry facet directive

4.fqnText: com machineblocks bml annotation ScadAnnotation Examples
4.name: Examples
4.documentation:
Element directive scad:examples — OpenSCAD-specific examples container for
independent sample sets (no 1:1 BML pair). Holds <example> entries (typically
language="OpenSCAD") beside the canonical default-namespace <examples> aggregation.
Prefer scad:example as a sibling of <example> under the same <examples> when
BML and SCAD bodies are one logical pair. Does not replace canonical examples.
4.idea: An OpenSCAD examples container facet directive

5.fqnText: com machineblocks bml annotation ScadAnnotation Property
5.name: Property
5.documentation:
Property-shaped member directive (name="*") under scad. Authoring QNames such
as <properties><scad:value/></properties> are property members in this
annotation namespace — catalog metadata for SCAD render (e.g. MBEnum), not Definition
meta-model types and not nested value facets.
5.idea: An OpenSCAD property member annotation directive

6.fqnText: com machineblocks bml annotation ScadAnnotation Summary
6.name: Summary
6.documentation:
Element directive scad:summary — OpenSCAD-specific summary prose facet.
Does not satisfy the required default-namespace summary slot on Definitions.
6.idea: An OpenSCAD summary prose facet directive

7.fqnText: com machineblocks bml annotation ScadAnnotation Value
7.name: Value
7.documentation:
Element directive for nested scad:value under a property declaration —
multiplies that property's value field along the scad Annotation axis. Same property
identity (e.g. myProp); not member scad:myProp and not top-level catalog scad:value.
Example: <holeDiameter><value>1.6</value><scad:value>1.6</scad:value></holeDiameter>.
7.idea: An OpenSCAD property value-field facet directive

9.name: StandardPresets
9.documentation:
Named property presets for the MachineBlocks Standard brick — sizes, colors, and
composite combinations for Customizer and basePresets references.

17.name: Block
17.documentation:
MachineBlocks domain base Block. Carries presets aggregation and basePresets
association for domain-specific preset resolution. Preset merge is compiler logic; Customizer
output is render-target logic.

18.name: CompositeBlock
18.documentation:
Composable MachineBlocks Block with default _parts aggregation. _parts holds
placed block instances (direction, offset, appliedPresets) or child blocks for SCAD
composition.
18.idea: A Block made of child Blocks

19.name: NativeBlock
19.documentation:
Final leaf Block mapped directly to SCAD mb_block() — the native geometry primitive
at render time. Uses children aggregation for mb_block() sub-geometry instead of _parts.

Sole SSOT for MachineBlocks (MB) native parameters: names, types, documentation, defaults,
and scad:value live only here. Markdown, YAML (09_mbom_properties.yml, 09_api_parameters.yml),
and scad-lib docs must follow this file — align to it or link only; never redefine the inventory.

Type shapes SSOT: com.machineblocks.bml.type.* (Library.bml membership). Extend types there;
do not invent parallel type tables in Markdown/YAML.

20.name: Set
20.documentation:
Abstract composable Block for LEGO-style Sets — block palette, placed instances,
and assembly order. Top-level catalog unit in MachineBlocks.

21.name: Step
21.documentation:
Framework Block defining one assembly instruction step. Document order in _steps
defines build order.

22.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept Architecture
22.name: Architecture
22.documentation:
MachineBlocks follows a layered architecture:

MBML / BML (authoring)
  ↓ parse (@blockml/parser)
Urmodell — Canonical BOM (immutable; MBOM is the MachineBlocks specialization)
  ↓ Stage 2 — Validator (pragmatic fork; resolve only)
  ↓ Stage 3 — Render Target (reference: OpenSCAD)
STL / 3MF (or other target artifacts)

MBML is the declarative authoring format for blocks, sets, and related MachineBlocks
documents. Authors describe typed, parameterized elements without knowledge of any
render target. XML is the sole BML serialization for V1 and V2.

MBOM is the renderer-independent domain model layered on BOM Core — not a second SSOT.
The BOM Compiler parses BML into an immutable Urmodell (Canonical BOM); MBOM extends that
graph with MachineBlocks types, NativeBlock parameters, and SCAD conventions.
Validation operates on the lossless BOM (Stage 2 pragmatic fork). Composition expansion,
expression evaluation, and target emit are Stage 3 — the renderer chooses Urmodell,
the default pragmatic model, or its own forks.

A render target serializes that model into a concrete output language. The MachineBlocks V3
SCAD library is the reference render target: OpenSCAD files that OpenSCAD turns into STL or
3MF. MBOM/BOM is canonical; SCAD is a serialization — not the other way around.

Core principle: one native geometry primitive (NativeBlock → mb_block()) with a large
parameter space (SSOT: NativeBlock.bml). Complexity comes from parameter combinations,
composition of multiple blocks, and nesting — not from many unrelated primitives.
22.idea: A guide to the MachineBlocks layered architecture

23.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept CompositionConcepts
23.name: CompositionConcepts
23.documentation:
Composition builds larger objects from multiple blocks that share one spatial contract.

Flat composition places sibling blocks in a shared parent. Nested composition places child
blocks inside a parent; configuration propagates from parent to children unless overridden.

A composite wrapper typically hides its own body and studs (base=false, studs=false) and sets
size to the outer bounding box of its parts. Placement of each part uses direction, offset,
and alignment relative to the parent origin (alignChildren).

In MBOM, composition fills aggregations (for example _parts on CompositeBlock). There is no
separate Placement meta-block — placement is properties on the placed instances. There is also
no MBOM “assembly mode” property: unassembled / assembled / merged are SCAD preview/print
helpers (for example mb_assembly), not domain model concepts — see scad:ModulePatterns /
scad-lib docs when targeting OpenSCAD.

Calibration at internal contacts often uses a tiny namespaced baseAdjustment overlap so parts
fuse cleanly when boolean-merged at render time. Derived outer size can be computed from part
sizes, directions, and offsets when no explicit shared size exists.
23.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks composition and assembly

24.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept DecisionFramework
24.name: DecisionFramework
24.documentation:
Do not start with parameters — start with intent. Three decision layers apply whether authoring
in MBML or targeting SCAD:

1. Semantic Intent — what is this block for?
2. Pattern Selection — how is it structured?
3. Parameter Realization — how is it built?

Intent order: Semantic Mode (purpose, structure, printability) is primary. Output Mode chooses
LEGO-like (playful, looser) versus Device (functional, strict printability). Design Mode
(appearance) is secondary and never overrides purpose.

Shared pattern inventory (aligned with AuthoringPatterns / ModulePatterns / ScadDecisionRules):
1. Primitive Wrapper — thin pass-through around native geometry / mb_block()
2. Semantic / Simple Block — named type or module with a focused surface; one native leaf
3. Composite Block — multi-body (MBML _parts / SCAD children); Set is a Composite specialization
4. Helper / Form — shared geometry helpers, not content products (primarily SCAD)
When in doubt, choose Composite.

Capability boundary of a single native geometry call: classic bricks and plates, slopes and
bevels (may be combined in one call — V3; V2 forbade slope+bevel together), rounds, recess,
studs, simple cutouts, and similar single-body forms. L/T/cross shapes, Z-brackets, side
panels, cable channels, bent liftarms, multi-line text, and multi-body carriers require
composition.

Cross-cutting rules: design in west-local face semantics; prefer direction over free rotation;
keep calibration adjustments out of instance settings when they belong in config. In MBML/BOM
author Face (and Direction / Align) as enum member ids (XNeg, XPos, …) — not SCAD face strings;
SCAD literals ("x-", "x+", …) are emit-only (see TransformationConcepts / scad:ScadDecisionRules).

Draft note — Decision Knowledge package (planned): grow this into a structured collection
(best practices, antipatterns, pattern choices, boundaries, rules) under
com.machineblocks.bml.decision.* — not under documentation.*. Own knowledge branch types
(e.g. Practice, Antipattern, DecisionRule, PatternChoice) with typed relations to
NativeBlock / CompositeBlock / examples. Migrate this block and scad:ScadDecisionRules into
that package; keep documentation.concept|mbml|scad as reading guides that only cross-link in.
24.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks decision layers

25.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept GeometryConcepts
25.name: GeometryConcepts
25.documentation:
Core geometry parameters modify the block shape inside the bounding box defined by size:

size — integer grid extent; the spatial contract of the block.
sizeMod — semantic per-side modification that keeps the brick structurally intact.
slope — height change per side; positive slopes the top, negative creates inverted bottom
  slopes. Does not change footprint.
bevel — footprint change by shifting top corners in XY; produces wedge shapes. Does not change
  height. Wedges are not a separate primitive — they emerge from bevel.
baseCrop — hard cut or extension per face (FaceMapXYZ); does not preserve grid compatibility,
  walls, or structural features; does not change bounding box or positioning. Same behaviour as
  V2 crop, renamed in V3. Prefer sizeMod over baseCrop when the brick should remain
  structurally intact.

cutouts — aggregation of NativeBlock instances (NativeBlock[]), not a property and not a SCAD
settings-array shape. Each cutout is a full NativeBlock limited to shape-determining parameters
(size, offset, bevel, slope, rounding, …). The volume is boolean-subtracted from the body;
structural features (walls, recess, tongue) are ignored by the subtraction. SCAD emit form of
cutouts is a serialization concern — see scad:TypesAndSerialization.

Parameter names, types, and defaults are defined on NativeBlock — do not treat external YAML or
Markdown tables as authoritative.
25.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks shape modification concepts

26.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept Introduction
26.name: Introduction
26.documentation:
MachineBlocks is a parametric system for generating LEGO-compatible 3D blocks. Primary use is
3D printing (STL / 3MF); the same geometry model also supports general 3D modeling workflows.

The system is a foundation for modular, printable machines: bricks, panels, enclosures, and
functional assemblies built from typed, parameterized blocks.

MachineBlocks is a domain on top of BlockML. Authoring uses MBML (MachineBlocks Markup
Language). The canonical representation is MBOM (MachineBlocks Object Model). Render targets —
OpenSCAD is the reference — serialize MBOM into target-specific output. Direct OpenSCAD Block
Files remain supported as an advanced and legacy authoring path.

27.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept StatusConvention
27.name: StatusConvention
27.documentation:
Maturity is expressed with Status Block references — not free strings or boolean flags.

Core status blocks (package org.blockml.bml.status.*):
Stable — implemented, tested, and mapping complete; reliable behaviour (implicit default).
Draft — definition exists; implementation or mapping incomplete, untested, or
  intentionally divergent; may change.
Stub — placeholder; shape declared, behaviour not yet specified; validates OK;
  renderer may stub/log or abort.
Deprecated — retained for compatibility; do not use in new work.

Default is Stable. Status inherits downward; authors declare status only when diverging from
the inherited effective status.

At <status> and bml:status reference sites, unqualified names resolve to
org.blockml.bml.status.* — bare names are correct there
(e.g. <status>Draft</status>, bml:status="Deprecated").
Explicit prefixes or FQNs remain valid everywhere (status:Draft ≡ Draft at those sites).
Bare status names are invalid outside specialized status reference sites.

SCAD implementation status and MBOM mapping status may differ independently for the same
parameter or type. Use Draft with an explicit note when they are misaligned.
27.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks status Block references

28.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept StructureSystems
28.name: StructureSystems
28.documentation:
Structure parameters add physical function inside the same bounding box that size defines.
Geometry shapes the volume; structure makes it printable and connectable.

Four structure systems:

1. Body — base toggles the solid body. base=false hides the body while bounding box and
   alignment stay unchanged (useful for composite wrappers and stud-only layers).
2. Underside — baseCutoutType selects None / Standard / Studs / Groove (enum member ids).
   baseWallGaps (WallGap[]) open passages through underside walls for crossing geometry.
3. Enclosure — recess and recessWallThickness carve an interior; recessWallGaps
   (RecessWallGap[]) open walls. RecessWallGap extends WallGap with padStart / padEnd
   (default Auto) for tongue/groove-aware end insets. Do not use wall thickness 0 to create
   openings — use gaps.
4. Connection — continuous tongue-and-groove versus discrete connectors for segmented or
   angled joints.

Studs sit on the top grid. studBaseOverlap (mbu) sinks studs into the top surface; 0 is valid
when base=false but studs still render.
28.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks structure systems

29.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept TransformationConcepts
29.name: TransformationConcepts
29.documentation:
Geometry and children are built first in local space, then transformed together. After the
local build, the effective order is:

direction → align → rotationOffset → rotation → rotationOffsetRevert → offset

direction — semantic 90° grid orientation (West / North / East / South). At North and South,
size X and Y swap for placement; face semantics stay west-local for authoring.
Prefer direction over free rotation whenever the intent is grid-aligned reorientation.
SCAD serialize literals (scad:value): west / north / east / south.

align — Start / Center / End relative to the reference bounding box (studs, slope, bevel, and
baseCrop do not change the align box). Scalar Align may broadcast, or AxisXYZ(Align) sets each
axis. alignChildren sets the parent origin used by children (default Start on all axes).
SCAD serialize literals (scad:value): start / center / end.

rotation — free rotation after alignment; not grid-safe; last resort.
rotationOffset — optional pivot for rotation; may be reverted after rotation.
offset — final placement translation only.

Face identifiers in MBML/BOM are enum member ids (XNeg, XPos, YNeg, YPos, ZNeg, ZPos) —
not integers and not authored as SCAD face strings. The SCAD literals "x-", "x+", … live on
Face as scad:value and are emit-only. Same pattern for Direction and Align.
29.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks transformation concepts

30.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation concept UnitsAndGrid
30.name: UnitsAndGrid
30.documentation:
MachineBlocks sizes the world in a unit stack:

mm → mbu → grid → block geometry

unitMbuToMm (default 1.6) is the millimetre length of one mbu (MachineBlocks Unit).
unitGridToMbu is SizeXYZ (default {x: 5, y: 5, z: 2}): mbu per grid step on each axis for a
1×1 plate. At defaults that is 8×8×3.2 mm. A size of [1, 1, 1] is therefore a plate — not a
cube. The default XY-to-Z grid ratio is 2.5:1; cube-like blocks need Z ≈ 2.5× the XY grid
extent (for example [2, 2, 5] → 16×16×16 mm). X and Y may differ (unitGridToMbu is full XYZ).

Absolute size along an axis is
size[axis] × unitGridToMbu[axis] × unitMbuToMm × scale.

The bounding box is defined exclusively by size. Other parameters change visible geometry
inside that box; they do not redefine the spatial contract.

Geometry parameters use mbu or grid units. Calibration adjustments (for example baseAdjustment)
use absolute millimetres and must not scale with the global scale factor.
30.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks units and the grid

31.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation mbml AuthoringPatterns
31.name: AuthoringPatterns
31.documentation:
MBML authoring mirrors the shared pattern inventory (DecisionFramework / ModulePatterns):

1. Primitive Wrapper / Native leaf — lowers to NativeBlock parameters. One body, one spatial
contract. Custom brick types typically extend CompositeBlock or Block and lower to NativeBlock
instances — NativeBlock itself is final and cannot be a baseType.

2. Simple semantic Block — named domain type with defaults and a focused parameter surface;
still one native geometry realization at the leaf.

3. Composite Block — _parts (or nested children) for L/T/cross shapes, enclosures, channels,
and multi-body devices. Parent size is the outer bbox; parts carry direction and offset.
Set is a Composite specialization: palette in presets, placed instances in _parts, optional
ordered _steps for assembly instructions.

4. Helper / Form — shared geometry helpers, not content products. Primarily a SCAD Block File
concern (see ModulePatterns / ScadDecisionRules); rarely published as an MBML product Block.

Decision rule: if a single native call cannot express the topology without breaking the
capability boundary, author a Composite Block. Prefer composition over baseCrop and over mixing
incompatible shape modifiers in one leaf.
31.idea: A guide to MBML authoring patterns

32.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation mbml DomainModel
32.name: DomainModel
32.documentation:
MachineBlocks domain types under com.machineblocks.bml.core:

Block — abstract domain base (baseType Entity). Carries name, presets aggregation, and
basePresets association.
CompositeBlock — Block with default _parts aggregation for child block instances.
NativeBlock — final leaf geometry Block. Maps 1:1 to the native geometry primitive at render
  time. SSOT for all native MachineBlocks parameters. Uses children for nested native geometry
  instead of _parts. Must not be used as baseType for custom Block definitions.
Set — CompositeBlock for LEGO-style builds: palette via presets, placed instances in _parts,
  assembly order in _steps.
Step — final assembly instruction Block. baseType is org.blockml.bml.core.Block (framework
  Block), not mbcore:Block / Entity — a sibling outside the Entity → mbcore:Block tree.
  part association references a placed _parts instance by bml:id; document order in _steps is
  build order.

Hierarchy: Entity → mbcore:Block → CompositeBlock → Set. NativeBlock is a final sibling under
mbcore:Block. Step sits on org.blockml.bml.core.Block → Step.

Class identity is the Block FQN. Instance identity inside composition uses bml:id (nested paths
use ::). There is no separate Placement type — direction, offset, and related placement data
live on the placed instances.
32.idea: A guide to the MachineBlocks domain Block hierarchy

33.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation mbml MbmlOverview
33.name: MbmlOverview
33.documentation:
MBML (MachineBlocks Markup Language) is the declarative authoring format for MachineBlocks.
It is BML specialized for the MachineBlocks domain: blocks, sets, presets, and composition
described as typed XML without OpenSCAD knowledge. XML is the sole BML serialization for
V1 and V2.

The BOM Compiler parses BML into an immutable Urmodell (Canonical BOM). MBOM is the
MachineBlocks domain specialization of that model — types, NativeBlock parameters, and
domain block kinds — not a separate compiler product. Render targets interpret the BOM/MBOM
graph (Urmodell, pragmatic fork, or their own forks); they do not redefine the domain model.

Authoring flow: write .bml sources → parse to Urmodell → validate (Stage 2) → render with a
registered target (reference: machineblocks-v3-scad). Direct .scad Block Files bypass
MBML/MBOM and remain an advanced path; prefer MBML for new domain content.
33.idea: A guide to MBML authoring in MachineBlocks

34.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation mbml TypeSystem
34.name: TypeSystem
34.documentation:
MachineBlocks domain ValueTypes live in com.machineblocks.bml.type.*. They are the SSOT for
type shapes used by NativeBlock properties and other domain members. Do not redefine types from
Markdown or YAML.

Categories (illustrative — see package members for the full inventory):

Atomic enums — Axis, Face, Direction, Align, StudType, HoleType, Gender, and related.
Axis containers — AxisXY(T), AxisXYZ(T), AxisAB(T) for per-axis values.
Face / side maps — FaceMapXY, FaceMapXYZ, CornerMap, Per-side and hole-edge maps.
Size and offset — SizeXYZ, SizeXY, SizeAB, OffsetXYZ, OffsetXY, OffsetAB, RotationXYZ.
Domain compounds — Connector, ScrewHole, WallGap / RecessWallGap, Port, Grille, SelectiveGrid,
  rounding maps, quality profiles, PCB types.

Naming uses XYZ / XY / AB axis keys — not 3D / 2D labels.

MBOM values are canonical. Render targets serialize those values (for SCAD mappings see the
SCAD TypesAndSerialization documentation). NativeBlock property type attributes reference these
types directly.
34.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks domain types

35.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation scad BlockFileStructure
35.name: BlockFileStructure
35.documentation:
A Block Module is the reusable OpenSCAD module that calls mb_block() (directly or indirectly).
Naming: mb__<package>__<Class> with package segments separated by double underscores
(example: mb__com__machineblocks__scad__examples__Cross).

MachineBlocks 1:1 SCAD convention — Manifestation FQN: replace the reserved definition segment
bml with scad in the Definition FQN. Definition com.machineblocks.bml.examples.Cross maps to
Manifestation com.machineblocks.scad.examples.Cross → file under
scad-lib/blocks/com/machineblocks/scad/examples/Cross.scad and module
mb__com__machineblocks__scad__examples__Cross. Header FQN on the .scad file is the Manifestation
FQN; the BML Definition FQN remains the Idea identity in MBOM. Other targets may use another
segment (e.g. cadq) the same way. This replace rule applies only to 1:1 Block→file projects —
not a BlockML platform requirement.

Signature is always (config, settings).

A Block File is a self-contained .scad file: Block Module plus customizer variables and a main
module call. Mandatory section order, each marked with a /* Section Name */ comment:

Mandatory Header
Imports
Customization
Main Module Call
Main Module Definition
Optional Sub Modules
Optional Helper Modules
Optional Global Functions

Header first line inside the comment must be exactly: MachineBlocks.com Block File.
Required fields: Name, Filename, FQN. Copyright, license, and visit lines are optional.

Imports: use the library block.scad; include mb_config.scad. Inside modules, always pass the
config parameter — do not rely on globals for config.

Customization uses OpenSCAD Customizer tabs and annotations. Hidden section may only bridge
customizer variables into module arguments — no internal module computations and no
mb_param_*() calls at file scope.
35.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks V3 Block File structure

36.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation scad LegacyConversion
36.name: LegacyConversion
36.documentation:
Status: Draft — primary V2→V3 path is documented from the Cross Plate reference pair
(V2 machineblock script below vs V3 Composite Block File
com.machineblocks.bml.examples.Cross). Edge cases and automated converter coverage remain
incomplete.

Module naming generations:
v1: block() — earliest; no nesting
v2: machineblock() — direct parameter style (file-scope script)
v3: mb_block() / mb__…() — config/settings Block Module (current)

Primary supported path: machineblock() (V2) → mb_block() or composite V3 Block Files.
V1 block() may be attempted when parameters look familiar, but always warn that nesting is
unsupported and manual testing is required.

Conversion steps:
1. Create V3 Block File structure (mandatory header, imports, customizer, main call, module)
   and mb__<package>__<Class> naming (e.g. mb__com__machineblocks__scad__examples__Cross).
   Replace V2 import paths
   (machineblocks/lib/block.scad, machineblocks/config/config.scad) with project-relative
   lib/block.scad and config/mb_config.scad.
2. Replace machineblock(a=…) with mb_block(config, settings=[["a", …]]); use string face ids.
   Pass the shared config object — do not re-pass unitMbuToMm / unitGridToMbu / scale /
   *Adjustment into every call (V2 names were unitMbu / unitGrid).
3. Remove the entire [Override Config] tab: overrideConfig, all *_ovr customizer variables,
   Hidden ternaries that select ovr vs global, and deprecated *RoundingResolution parameters.
   Calibration and quality live in mb_config / config profiles only.
4. Wrap all geometry in a Block Module; read native params via mb_param_* and custom params
   via mb_param. Build a sharedSettings array once; concat per-child overrides.
5. Multiple machineblock() calls inside union() → one wrapper
   mb_block(base=false, studs=false, size=outer) with children() — Composite pattern.
6. Child align="ccs" with center-relative offsets: either set alignChildren on the wrapper and
   keep center math, or (preferred in Cross V3) switch children to start-aligned offsets and
   drop ccs — recalculate offset as […, brickOffset, …] without the -0.5*(parent-child) term.
7. Keep split customizer UI vars; only bridge them through the main settings list. Hidden must
   not call getters or hold module-only computations.

Cross-specific mappings (V2 → V3), learned from the reference pair:
• baseWallGapsX = [[offset, 2, length]] on the X-arm brick →
  baseWallGaps = [["y", offset, length]] (face string; side code 2 = both sides collapses to one
  V3 face entry for this pattern — split to two face entries when walls must differ).
• baseWallGapsY = [[offset, 2, length]] on the Y-arm brick →
  baseWallGaps = [["x", offset, length]].
• studShift string enum "none"|"x"|"y"|"xy" → boolean / SelectiveGrid form (Cross V3: false for
  "none"); do not pass the V2 string through unchanged.
• Customizer baseReliefCut* → settings keys reliefCut / reliefCutHeight / reliefCutThickness
  (getters mb_param_reliefCut*).
• studBaseOverlap is V3-native; omit on convert unless the V2 file already exposed an equivalent.
• Clamp child sizes/offsets with min(...) so customizer values cannot exceed the outer size.
• Do not copy V2 default sizes blindly — Cross V3 uses different product defaults ([4,4,3] vs
  V2 [3,3,1]); preserve author intent, not legacy demo numbers, unless converting that exact file.

Hidden section: customizer bridge only — no getters, no unitMbuToMm/unitGridToMbu/scale
globals. Retrieve unitMbuToMm, unitGridToMbu, and scale via mb_param_* inside the module when
needed. Native parameter inventory for getters: NativeBlock (not legacy YAML).
36.idea: A guide to converting V2 machineblock() files to V3

37.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation scad MbBlockApi
37.name: MbBlockApi
37.documentation:
mb_block() is the single public native geometry module of the MachineBlocks V3 SCAD library.
All printable leaf geometry goes through it — complexity is parameters, composition, and nesting.

Public signature:
mb_block(config = undef, settings = undef)

config and settings are optional arrays of [key, value] pairs (pseudo-maps). Resolution order
for each parameter: settings → config → default. Merge helpers combine layers; never read the
arrays by hand inside Block Modules.

Parameter access rule (mandatory inside every Block Module):

• Native — every property declared on com.machineblocks.bml.core.NativeBlock is a native
  parameter. In SCAD it MUST be read via its dedicated getter:
  mb_param_[propertyName](config, settings)
  optional third argument: block-specific default override.
  Example: size → mb_param_size(config, settings)

• Custom — any other parameter (module-specific, not a NativeBlock property) MUST be read via
  the generic getter:
  mb_param(config, settings, "name", default)
  Example: brick1SizeY → mb_param(config, settings, "brick1SizeY", 2)

Never invent mb_param_* for custom names. Never use mb_param() for NativeBlock properties.
Never access config/settings arrays directly.

Reference: com.machineblocks.bml.examples.Cross (Cross.scad) shows both sides in one module —
native getters for size, studs, baseColor, … and mb_param() for brick1SizeY, brick2SizeX,
brick1OffsetY, brick2OffsetX.

config carries environment, calibration, and shared profile values. settings carry instance
overrides for one call. Calibration adjustments belong in config profiles — not as routine
settings on content blocks.

Parameter inventory, types, defaults, and documentation are defined on NativeBlock — that Block
is the SSOT. SCAD docs explain the call model; they do not redefine the parameter set.
37.idea: A guide to the mb_block() public API

38.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation scad ModulePatterns
38.name: ModulePatterns
38.documentation:
Four production Block Module patterns appear in the V3 SCAD library (same inventory as
DecisionFramework / AuthoringPatterns):

Pattern 1 — Primitive Wrapper: thin module that calls mb_block() with a curated default
settings surface (pass-through / minimal logic).

Pattern 2 — Simple / Semantic Block: named module with getters, block-specific defaults, and
a focused customizer; still one mb_block() realization at the leaf. Example: Standard brick
(com.machineblocks.bml.bricks.Standard) — every NativeBlock property via mb_param_*.

Pattern 3 — Composite Block: outer mb_block(base=false, studs=false) with size = outer bbox;
children() hold parts with direction/offset. Examples: Cross, Frame.

Pattern 4 — Helper / Form: shared geometry helpers used by other modules, not end-user content
products.

Parameter access inside every pattern: NativeBlock properties → mb_param_[propertyName]();
all other parameters → mb_param(). Cross.scad is the reference for both in one module
(native: size, studs, …; custom: brick1SizeY, brick2SizeX, brick1OffsetY, brick2OffsetX).

Structural composites often realize Panel, Corner Panel, Channel, and Enclosure intents.
Connection uses tongue-and-groove or discrete connectors — see StructureSystems for concepts.

Full Block File examples below are complete OpenSCAD sources (not snippets). Prefer these over
inventing new file layouts. Helper / Form examples are not embedded here — follow library
helper modules when extending shared geometry.
38.idea: A guide to MachineBlocks SCAD Block Module patterns

39.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation scad ScadDecisionRules
39.name: ScadDecisionRules
39.documentation:
Direct SCAD generation follows the same three layers as the concept DecisionFramework
(Intent → Pattern → Parameters). This block states SCAD-specific constraints.

Pattern choice for Block Modules:
1. Primitive Wrapper — thin module around mb_block() with defaults
2. Semantic / Simple Block — named module, getters, focused customizer
3. Composite Block — wrapper mb_block(base=false, studs=false) with children
4. Helper / Form — shared geometry helpers, not content products
When in doubt, choose Composite.

Single mb_block() whitelist (examples): classic bricks/plates; slope and/or bevel (combinable
in V3 — V2 disallowed both in one call); round forms; recess; studs; simple cutouts;
single-line top text; PCB cavities; straight liftarms.

Requires Composite (blacklist for one call): L/T/cross; Z-brackets; side panels; cable
channels; bent liftarms; carriers; multi-line text; multi-body devices.

Device rules: walls/corners/channels as composites; lids as separate blocks; inner cavities
often baseCutoutType=none.

Implementation rules: design west-local; prefer direction over rotation; no calibration
adjustments in routine settings; NativeBlock properties always via mb_param_[propertyName](),
all other parameters via mb_param() (see MbBlockApi; Cross.scad demonstrates both); in SCAD
settings/config use Face scad:value strings ("x-", "x+", …) — MBML/BOM still authors enum
member ids; no globals inside modules; Hidden section is customizer bridge only.
39.idea: A guide to SCAD authoring decision rules

40.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation scad ScadRenderTarget
40.name: ScadRenderTarget
40.documentation:
OpenSCAD is the reference MachineBlocks render target. It is not the canonical representation
of blocks — MBOM is. The SCAD target serializes MBOM into MachineBlocks V3 .scad files that
OpenSCAD renders to STL or 3MF.

The target registers as machineblocks-v3-scad. V1 handles two base domain kinds:
Block (and descendants that lower to block modules) via a block processor, and Set via a set
processor (STEPS and view submodules).

MachineBlocks World convention: leaf NativeBlock ↔ mb_block(); composition becomes a nested
mb_block() tree; domain types lower to mb_block() settings. Other BlockML render targets may
emit entirely different shapes — this mapping is MachineBlocks-specific.

For 1:1 Block→file emit, Manifestation packages replace definition segment bml with scad
(com.machineblocks.bml.X → com.machineblocks.scad.X for path and mb__ module names). See
BlockFileStructure. Other targets may choose a different segment; this is not a platform rule.

Direct authoring of V3 Block Files (hand-written or AI-generated) remains supported and bypasses
MBML/MBOM. As MBML matures, that path becomes advanced/legacy for domain content.
40.idea: A guide to the MachineBlocks OpenSCAD render target

41.fqnText: com machineblocks bml documentation scad TypesAndSerialization
41.name: TypesAndSerialization
41.documentation:
Status: Draft — MBOM type shapes are defined in com.machineblocks.bml.type.*; SCAD serialization
rules continue to be validated against the V3 library. Prefer BML type definitions over
Markdown/YAML for shapes; this block summarizes the serialization strategy only.

Strategy: take the canonical MBOM value → validate → normalize → emit the shortest valid SCAD
form → wrap as ["paramName", value] in settings/config.

Typical SCAD forms (details live on the type Blocks):
AxisXYZ — scalar, [xy, z], or [x, y, z]
AxisXY — scalar or [x, y]
Per-side-4 — scalar, [x, y], or four-value array
FaceVector6 — always six values
FaceMap — [["face", value], …] (optional namespaced keys)
SelectiveGrid — [base, [[rect], value], …] or a scalar broadcast

Do not design MBOM around SCAD arrays. Design SCAD arrays as serialization of MBOM.
41.idea: A guide to MBOM type serialization for SCAD

80.name: Library
80.documentation:
Publishable MachineBlocks root library (com.machineblocks.bml.Library). Exports shared domain

exclusively by this file's blocks list — not by directory layout.

81.name: README
81.documentation:
README block for the MachineBlocks root library (com.machineblocks.bml.Library).
Start with references marked relation=ReadFirst — curated documentation in mental learning
order across concept (renderer-agnostic), mbml (authoring), and scad (OpenSCAD render target).
Library.bml points here via the required readMe aggregation (<mb:README />).

82.name: Align
82.documentation:
Enum ValueType for start / center / end alignment on MachineBlocks bricks.
Extends MBEnum(Text). BOM property values store only the member id (Start / Center / End)
plus this EnumType; scad:value holds the SCAD serialization literal.

Usage contrast — scalar Align may be broadcast, or expanded with an axis map:
  NativeBlock.align / alignChildren → Align | AxisXYZ(Align)  (brick world axes X/Y/Z)
  Port.align (face-local)           → Align | AxisAB(Align)   (face plane A/B = XY|XZ|YZ)
AxisXYZ vs AxisAB are not interchangeable: XYZ is placement in brick space; AB is
in-plane on a directed face.

83.name: Auto

84.name: Axis

85.name: AxisAB
85.documentation:
Struct ValueType for component-keyed { a, b }. Extends MultiAxis(N).
AB names an abstract face-local plane that resolves to XY, XZ, or YZ depending on context —
not a fixed world-axis pair like AxisXY. World / brick axes use XY / XYZ; face-local
in-plane values use AB — see docs/04_types.md (XY / XYZ / AB). Inherits the MultiAxis N
parameter for a. B is a separate generic (defaultType N) so the b component may differ from
a — e.g. AxisAB(Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY), Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitZ)) when the plane mixes
XY and Z scales. Bare AxisAB / AxisAB(T) binds B to N as dimensionless Decimal; no default
grid unit, because no single GridUnitXY / GridUnitZ applies to every AB plane. N and B are
any ValueType.
85.idea: A value pair along A and B

86.name: AxisXY
86.documentation:
Struct ValueType for axis-keyed { x, y }. Extends MultiAxis(N).
N is any ValueType (default Decimal) — numbers, structs, enums, etc. Bare AxisXY is Decimal
(dimensionless). Supply a unit via N — e.g. AxisXY(Decimal(unit:Millimeter)) or
AxisXY(Integer(mbunit:MBU)).
86.idea: A value pair along X and Y

87.name: AxisXYZ
87.documentation:
Struct ValueType for axis-keyed { x, y, z }. Extends AxisXY(N) and adds z.
Inherits x and y typed as N. Z is a separate generic (defaultType N) so the Z component may
differ from X/Y — e.g. AxisXYZ(Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY), Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitZ)).
Bare AxisXYZ / AxisXYZ(T) binds Z to the same effective type as N. N and Z are any ValueType
(default Decimal).
87.idea: A value triple along X, Y, and Z

88.name: BaseCutout

89.name: BaseRoundingMap
89.documentation:
Closed AxisXYZ(Decimal | RadiusAB | CornerMap(Decimal | RadiusAB)) for body corner rounding on
all three brick axes. Not re-opened as a generic. Inherits x, y, z; each axis holds a
CornerMap of unitless Decimal or RadiusAB (axis context supplies XY vs Z scale). SCAD
serializes as the nested AxisXYZ / CornerMap form. Used by NativeBlock.baseRoundingRadius
as the expanded alternative beside a bare Decimal broadcast.
89.idea: A per-axis corner rounding map for the brick body

90.name: Bevel
90.documentation:
Closed CornerMap(OffsetXY) for wedge bevels on the horizontal (Z-face)
plane only — not a multi-axis map like BaseRoundingMap. Not re-opened as a generic.
Inherits sw, nw, ne, se; each corner is an OffsetXY displacement in GridUnitXY (OffsetXY
default). World XY via OffsetXY (not AxisAB) is intentional: the plane is fixed to the
brick Z-face. SCAD serializes as a 4-element array of [x, y] pairs. Used by
NativeBlock.bevel; the resulting shape is intersected with the bounding box and may
combine with slope.
90.idea: A corner bevel displacement map on the horizontal plane

91.name: Connector
91.documentation:
Struct ValueType for a triangular side connector placement
{ face, axis, gender, align, padStart, padEnd }. Used by NativeBlock.connectors as
Boolean.False | Connector[]. padStart / padEnd skip connector slots at the start and end
along the face — important when joining bricks of different sizes.
91.idea: A side connector on a directed face

92.name: CornerMap
92.documentation:
Struct ValueType for a corner-keyed map { sw, nw, ne, se } in the local brick
frame. The four corners may lie on any local plane (XY, XZ, or YZ) — the plane is not part of
the type. Generic T is the per-corner value type — any ValueType; no defaultType — bind T
explicitly, e.g. CornerMap(Boolean) or CornerMap(Decimal(unit:Millimeter)). Short keys map to
south-west / north-west / north-east / south-east.
92.idea: A value map on the four corners

93.name: Direction

94.name: Face
94.idea: A directed face on a brick

95.name: FaceAxisXY
95.documentation:
Enum ValueType for XY-directed faces (x- / x+ / y- / y+), single axes (x / y),
and the combined XY plane on MachineBlocks bricks. Extends MBEnum(Text). BOM property values
store only the member id plus this EnumType; scad:value holds the SCAD serialization literal.
95.idea: An XY face, axis, or both axes

96.name: FaceMapXY
96.documentation:
Struct ValueType for a sparse face map on the four lateral faces
{ xNeg, xPos, yNeg, yPos }. Generic T is the per-face value type — e.g.
FaceMapXY(Decimal(unit:Millimeter)). FaceMapXYZ extends this type and adds zNeg / zPos
(generic Z, defaultType T). Keys are signed-axis faces (not min/max ranges); SCAD literals
remain x- / x+ via Face / scad:value. Named FaceMapXY (not FaceMap2D).
96.idea: A face-keyed value map on X and Y

97.name: FaceMapXYZ
97.documentation:
Struct ValueType for a sparse face map on all six faces
{ xNeg, xPos, yNeg, yPos, zNeg, zPos }. Extends FaceMapXY(T) and adds zNeg / zPos
typed as Z. Z defaults to T (declaration-order sibling default) so FaceMapXYZ(T) keeps one
binding; supply both when Z faces differ — e.g.
FaceMapXYZ(Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY), Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitZ)).
Preferred type for NativeBlock face maps with Z (baseAdjustment, sizeMod, …). Lateral-only
maps use FaceMapXY. Named FaceMapXYZ (not FaceMap3D).
97.idea: A face-keyed value map on X, Y, and Z

98.name: Gender

99.name: Grille
99.documentation:
Enum ValueType for grille bar orientation on MachineBlocks bricks.
Extends MBEnum(Text). Members X / Y set bar direction; None disables the grille.
BOM property values store only the member id plus this EnumType; scad:value holds the
SCAD serialization literal.

100.name: HoleEdgeMap
100.documentation:
Closed AxisXYZ(HoleEdgeMode | HoleEdgePair) for Technic hole edge modes on
X, Y, and Z hole directions. Not re-opened as a generic. Inherits x, y, z; each component is
either a scalar HoleEdgeMode or a HoleEdgePair for the two companion edges. SCAD serializes
as a 3-element array (1/2/3-value rules apply at the property). Used by
NativeBlock.holeXYZEdgeMode.

101.name: HoleEdgeMode
101.documentation:
Enum ValueType for how hole-edge treatment applies along an edge —
none / start / end / all. Extends MBEnum(Text). BOM property values store only the member id
(None / Start / End / All) plus this EnumType; scad:value holds the SCAD serialization
literal.

102.name: HoleEdgePair
102.documentation:
Closed AxisAB(HoleEdgeMode) for one hole-axis entry's inner two companion
edges — e.g. X-holes use [Y-edge, Z-edge]. Not re-opened as a generic. Inherits a and b;
SCAD serializes as a 2-element array of HoleEdgeMode literals (none / start / end / all).
Used inside HoleEdgeMap and as a top-level alternative on NativeBlock.holeXYZEdgeMode.
102.idea: A hole-edge mode pair on two companion edges

103.name: HoleType
103.documentation:
Enum ValueType for LEGO Technic hole shapes on MachineBlocks bricks.
Extends MBEnum(Text). Pin is a round hole; Axle is a cross-shaped hole.
BOM property values store only the member id plus this EnumType; scad:value holds the
SCAD serialization literal.

104.name: Inherit
104.documentation:
Named Constant(Text) for the singleton value "Inherit". Use as a union
alternative — for example Inherit | Float — instead of writing Constant(Text){value: "Inherit"}
at every reference site. The external value is "Inherit" (identical to Text). Signals that a
property should take its effective value from the parent / surrounding context.

105.name: MBEnum
105.documentation:
Abstract base for MachineBlocks EnumTypes. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.EnumType
and declares catalog property scad:value : T — the SCAD serialization literal for each enum
member (annotation member QName under ScadAnnotation.Property, name="*"). This is a top-level
namespaced member on the enum type — not a PropertyDefinition value facet
(<myProp><scad:value>…</scad:value></myProp> uses Annotation.Value).
Concrete enums bind T (typically Text) and set scad:value on values composition members. BOM
property values still store only member id + EnumType; scad:value is catalog metadata looked
up at render time.
105.idea: A MachineBlocks enum with a SCAD serialization literal

106.name: MultiAxis
106.documentation:
Abstract StructType base for MachineBlocks axis-keyed maps (AxisXY, AxisXYZ).
Generic N (ValueType, default Decimal) is the per-axis value type on XY. AxisXYZ adds Z
(ValueType, defaultType N) so the Z component may differ. Units travel with N / Z —
e.g. AxisXY(Decimal(unit:Millimeter)), AxisXYZ(Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY), Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitZ)).
Bare MultiAxis / AxisXY / AxisXYZ resolve to Decimal (dimensionless).

107.name: None
107.documentation:
Named Constant(Text) for the singleton value "None". Use as a union
alternative — for example None | Float — instead of writing Constant(Text){value: "None"}
at every reference site. The external value is "None" (identical to Text). Distinct from
org.blockml.bml.unit.None (the dimensionless unit) — this type lives under
com.machineblocks.bml.type.

108.name: OffsetAB
108.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for an offset pair { a, b }. Extends AxisAB(N, B) —
inherits a (N) and b (B); adds offset / translation semantics (may be negative). When used as a
face-local offset, a and b are measured from the respective negative (-) sides of the face.
AB stands for a face-local plane that may be XY, XZ, or YZ depending on context (e.g. the
selected Face) — therefore bare OffsetAB defaults N to dimensionless Decimal and does not
bind a single grid unit such as GridUnitXY. A uniform GridUnitXY default (as on OffsetXY)
would be wrong whenever the plane includes Z (GridUnitZ). Bind units explicitly when known —
e.g. OffsetAB(Decimal(unit:Millimeter)) or OffsetAB(Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY),
Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitZ)). N and B are constrained to Number; B defaults to N.
108.idea: An offset along A and B

109.name: OffsetXY
109.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for an offset pair { x, y }. Extends AxisXY(N) —
inherits x and y; adds offset / translation semantics (may be negative). N is constrained to
Number (AxisXY remains ValueType-universal). Bare OffsetXY defaults N to
Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY). Override via N — e.g. OffsetXY(Decimal(unit:Millimeter)). Named
OffsetXY (not Offset2D) — MachineBlocks axis-keyed types use XY / XYZ, not 2D / 3D.
109.idea: An offset along X and Y

110.name: OffsetXYZ
110.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for an offset triple { x, y, z }. Extends AxisXYZ(N, Z) —
inherits x, y (N) and z (Z); adds offset / translation semantics (may be negative). N and Z are
constrained to Number. Bare OffsetXYZ defaults N to Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY) and Z to
Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitZ) — distinct plate-grid scales. Uniform override requires both
arguments — e.g. OffsetXYZ(Decimal(unit:Millimeter), Decimal(unit:Millimeter)). Named
OffsetXYZ (not Offset3D) — MachineBlocks axis-keyed types use XY / XYZ, not 2D / 3D.
110.idea: An offset along X, Y, and Z

111.name: PcbMountingType
111.documentation:
Enum ValueType for PCB mounting features on MachineBlocks bricks —
clips (clip-in frame) / sockets (screw sockets). Extends MBEnum(Text). BOM property
values store only the member id (Clips / Sockets) plus this EnumType; scad:value holds
the SCAD serialization literal. Used by NativeBlock.pcb as Boolean.False | PcbMountingType.

112.name: PcbSocket
112.documentation:
Struct ValueType for one PCB screw-socket center { x, y } in millimeters,
measured from the brick center. Maps 1:1 to the SCAD pcbSockets entry [x, y]. Used by
NativeBlock.pcbSockets as the list of individual sockets — distinct from NativeBlock.pcbOffset,
which offsets the entire PCB assembly. Diameter, height, and hole diameter stay on
NativeBlock.pcbSocket* (global).

113.name: PillarGapAutoConfig
113.documentation:
Struct ValueType for pillars="auto" layout: corner triangle leg length and
middle cross width (grid units). Used by NativeBlock.pillarGapAutoConfig — replaces the
V2 pair pillarGapCornerLength / pillarGapMiddle.

114.name: PlaneRoundingMap
114.documentation:
Closed CornerMap(Decimal(GridUnitXY) | RadiusAB(Decimal(GridUnitXY))) for
recess / tongue corner rounding on the horizontal (Z-face) plane only — not a full
AxisXYZ map like BaseRoundingMap. Not re-opened as a generic. Inherits sw, nw, ne, se;
each corner is a scalar GridUnitXY radius or a RadiusAB pair. SCAD serializes as the
CornerMap form. Used by NativeBlock.recessRoundingRadius and tongueRoundingRadius as the
expanded alternative beside Auto and bare Decimal(GridUnitXY).
114.idea: A corner rounding map on the horizontal plane

115.name: Port
115.documentation:
Struct ValueType for a face cutout port { face, align, offset, rotation, shapes,
depth }. Maps 1:1 to the SCAD ports tuple [face, anchor, offset, rotation, shapes, depth].
offset and depth are unitless — the face determines which grid/physical scale applies.
Used by NativeBlock.ports as Boolean.False | Port[].
115.idea: A face cutout port with shapes

116.fqnText: com machineblocks bml type Port PortCircleShapeSettings
116.name: PortCircleShapeSettings
116.documentation:
Circle typeData for a port shape — SCAD [diameter].
FQN: com.machineblocks.bml.type.Port.PortCircleShapeSettings.

117.fqnText: com machineblocks bml type Port PortRectShapeSettings
117.name: PortRectShapeSettings
117.documentation:
Rectangle typeData for a port shape — SCAD [[width, height], roundingRadius].
FQN: com.machineblocks.bml.type.Port.PortRectShapeSettings.

118.fqnText: com machineblocks bml type Port PortShape
118.name: PortShape
118.documentation:
Struct ValueType for one port shape { type, offset, rotation, setting }.
Maps 1:1 to the SCAD shape tuple [type, offset, rotation, typeData].
FQN: com.machineblocks.bml.type.Port.PortShape.
118.idea: A single shape within a port

119.fqnText: com machineblocks bml type Port PortShapeSettings
119.name: PortShapeSettings
119.documentation:
Abstract StructType base for port shape typeData. Extended by
PortCircleShapeSettings and PortRectShapeSettings.
FQN: com.machineblocks.bml.type.Port.PortShapeSettings.

120.name: PortShapeType

121.name: QualityPreset
121.documentation:
Enum ValueType for quality presets — preview / normal / print / render.
Extends MBEnum(Text). BOM property values store only the member id (Preview / Normal /
Print / Render) plus this EnumType; scad:value holds the SCAD serialization literal.
121.idea: A render or mesh quality preset

122.name: RadiusAB
122.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for a radius pair { a, b }. Extends AxisAB(N, B) —
inherits a (N) and b (B); adds radius / rounding semantics (non-negative extents). N and B are
constrained to Number. B defaults to N so bare RadiusAB / RadiusAB(T) binds both components to
the same effective type. Bare RadiusAB defaults N to Decimal (dimensionless). Override via N /
B — e.g. RadiusAB(Decimal(mbunit:MBU)) or RadiusAB(Decimal(unit:Millimeter),
Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitZ)).
122.idea: A radius pair along A and B

123.name: RecessWallGap
123.documentation:
Struct ValueType for a gap in a recess wall. Extends WallGap (face, pos, len)
with padStart and padEnd — how much the opening is reduced inward from each end along the
wall. Both default to Auto. Used where recess openings need tongue/groove-aware end insets
beyond a plain WallGap.
123.idea: A recess wall opening with end padding

124.name: RotationXY
124.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for a rotation pair { x, y } in degrees. Extends
AxisXY with N closed to Decimal(unit:Degree) — not re-opened as a generic. Rotation about
X and Y (degrees of arc). Named RotationXY (not Rotation2D) — MachineBlocks axis-keyed
types use XY / XYZ, not 2D / 3D.
124.idea: A rotation about X and Y in degrees

125.name: RotationXYZ
125.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for a rotation triple { x, y, z } in degrees. Extends
AxisXYZ with N closed to Decimal(unit:Degree); Z is omitted at the baseType application and
defaults to N (same degree type). Not re-opened as a generic. Named RotationXYZ (not
Rotation3D) — MachineBlocks axis-keyed types use XY / XYZ, not 2D / 3D.
125.idea: A rotation about X, Y, and Z in degrees

126.name: ScadQualityClassFactors
126.documentation:
Struct ValueType for OpenSCAD quality-class segment length multipliers
{ functional, visual, hidden }. Higher values reduce mesh quality and improve render
performance. Used by NativeBlock.scadQualityClassFactors.

127.name: ScadQualityClassMinSegments
127.documentation:
Struct ValueType for OpenSCAD quality-class minimum full-circle segment counts
{ functional, visual, hidden }. Prevents small radii from becoming overly coarse. Used by
NativeBlock.scadQualityClassMinSegments.

128.name: ScadQualityProfile
128.documentation:
Struct ValueType mapping each QualityPreset (preview / normal / print / render)
to a Profile of segment length (mm) and maximum segment count. Used by
NativeBlock.scadQualityProfile. Smaller length increases mesh quality; segments caps
full-circle resolution. Property names match the QualityPreset scad:value literals.
128.idea: A quality-preset map of SCAD mesh profiles

129.fqnText: com machineblocks bml type ScadQualityProfile Profile
129.name: Profile
129.documentation:
Struct ValueType for one quality level: target segment length in millimeters
and maximum segment count. FQN: com.machineblocks.bml.type.ScadQualityProfile.Profile.
129.idea: A SCAD mesh quality profile entry

130.name: ScrewHole
130.documentation:
Struct ValueType for a mounting screw hole
{ face, offset, diameter, depth, insetThickness, insetDepth }. Maps 1:1 to the SCAD
screwHoles tuple [face, position, diameter?, depth?, insetThickness?, insetDepth?].
offset is the face-local grid position (measured from the respective negative (-) sides).
diameter / depth / inset* use Auto to inherit NativeBlock.screwHole* defaults, or an explicit
Decimal(Millimeter) per-hole override. Used by NativeBlock.screwHoles as ScrewHole[].
130.idea: A screw hole on a directed face

131.name: SelectiveGrid
131.documentation:
Struct ValueType for one inclusive axis-aligned range on the plate grid with an
override value. Used as SelectiveGrid(T)[] on *Areas properties (e.g. studAreas) alongside a
Boolean default property (e.g. studs). Generic T is the cell value type — e.g.
SelectiveGrid(Boolean) or SelectiveGrid(Boolean | mbt:HoleType). Later entries win on overlap
(authoring order).

132.name: SizeAB
132.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for a size pair { a, b }. Extends AxisAB(N, B) —
inherits a (N) and b (B); adds size / extent semantics. N and B are constrained to Number.
B defaults to N so bare SizeAB / SizeAB(T) binds both to the same effective type. Bare SizeAB
defaults N to Decimal (dimensionless). Override via N / B — e.g. SizeAB(Decimal(unit:Millimeter)).
132.idea: A size pair along A and B

133.name: SizeXY
133.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for a size pair { x, y }. Extends AxisXY(N) —
inherits x and y; adds size semantics (extent / footprint). N is constrained to Number
(AxisXY remains ValueType-universal). Bare SizeXY defaults N to Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY).
Override via N — e.g. SizeXY(Decimal(unit:Millimeter)). Named SizeXY (not Size2D) —
MachineBlocks axis-keyed types use XY / XYZ, not 2D / 3D.
133.idea: A size along X and Y

134.name: SizeXYZ
134.documentation:
Semantic Struct ValueType for a size triple { x, y, z }. Extends AxisXYZ(N, Z) —
inherits x, y (N) and z (Z); adds size semantics (extent / brick footprint). N and Z are
constrained to Number. Bare SizeXYZ defaults N to Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitXY) and Z to
Decimal(mbunit:GridUnitZ) — distinct plate-grid scales. Uniform override requires both
arguments — e.g. SizeXYZ(Decimal(unit:Millimeter), Decimal(unit:Millimeter)). Named SizeXYZ
(not Size3D) — MachineBlocks axis-keyed types use XY / XYZ, not 2D / 3D.
134.idea: A size along X, Y, and Z

135.name: StudType
135.documentation:
Enum ValueType for stud variants on MachineBlocks bricks.
Extends MBEnum(Text). Solid is a massive stud; Hollow has a center hole.
BOM property values store only the member id plus this EnumType;
scad:value holds the SCAD serialization literal.

136.name: WallGap
136.documentation:
Struct ValueType for a gap in a base or recess wall. face selects an XY face,
axis, or both axes (FaceAxisXY); pos is the start along that wall in grid units; len is the
opening length in grid units. Used by NativeBlock.baseWallGaps and recessWallGaps as
WallGap[].
136.idea: A wall opening on a face or axis

137.name: GridUnitXY
137.documentation:
Plate-grid unit along X and Y. A 1×1 plate footprint is one GridUnitXY in each
horizontal axis. Size in mbu via unitGridToMbu.x / unitGridToMbu.y (default 5 mbu per
GridUnitXY). Distinct from GridUnitZ — vertical plate height uses a different mbu scale.

138.name: GridUnitZ
138.documentation:
Plate-grid unit along Z (stack height). One plate layer is one GridUnitZ.
Size in mbu via unitGridToMbu.z (default 2 mbu per GridUnitZ). Distinct from GridUnitXY —
horizontal footprint uses a different mbu scale.

139.name: MBU
139.documentation:
Base geometric unit of the MachineBlocks system. Idealized block geometry is
expressed in mbu; conversion to millimeters uses unitMbuToMm (default 1.6 mm per mbu).

140.name: BmlAnnotation
140.documentation:
Concrete Annotation for BlockML language directives. preferredAlias is bml. Authoring documents
bind xmlns:bml to this FQN. Directives control composition structure, instance identity, generic
binding, service beans, and serialization shape — they are not Block properties and not
Definition members.

Attribute directives: id, version, bean, scope, status, generics, each, if, unless, with, xml.
Element directives: container. Dual authoring (attribute or child element) is documented on
generics and xml.

The legacy schema URI http://blockml.org/schema/bml remains an XSD/catalog identifier only —
BML-semantic xmlns:bml must target this Annotation. XSD is not a standard feature;
xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default (doc:DocumentFormat).

141.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Bean
141.name: Bean
141.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:bean — registers the instance as a named service bean
for expression access via @beanName.

142.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Container
142.name: Container
142.documentation:
Element directive bml:container — virtual container that produces no Block
output but applies directives to a group of children.

143.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Each
143.name: Each
143.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:each — expands the element once per loop iteration
(numeric or collection). See doc:BmlDirectives.

144.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Generics
144.name: Generics
144.documentation:
Attribute or child-element directive bml:generics — binds open genericTypes
on a Block instance. Only on Block instances (composition children and instance aggregation
fill). Value is the parenthesized argument list from a baseType generic application — the
type name is omitted because the instance tag is the type. Parentheses are required.
Attribute form: bml:generics="(type:Integer)". Element form:
<bml:generics>(type:String, myns:MyBlock)</bml:generics>. Arguments are
TypeExpressions in declaration order. Authored args win; remaining parameters take
defaultType. Open generic instance without this directive → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE.
Placement elsewhere → BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED. Argument list incompatible with
the instance's open parameters → BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH. See doc:BmlDirectives
and doc:GenericsModel.

145.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Id
145.name: Id
145.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:id — instance identity within a composition tree.
Required when the instance is referenced or carries bml:each.

146.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation If
146.name: If
146.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:if — includes the element only when the expression
evaluates to true.

147.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Scope
147.name: Scope
147.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:scope — "local" or "context" for service bean
visibility. Default local when omitted.
147.idea: A service bean visibility scope directive

148.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Status
148.name: Status
148.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:status — shorthand status reference; unqualified
values resolve via org.blockml.bml.status.*.

149.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Unless
149.name: Unless
149.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:unless — includes the element only when the expression
evaluates to false. Negation of bml:if.

150.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Version
150.name: Version
150.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:version — optional exact-version assert when a
composition reference targets an external block type.
150.idea: An external type version pin directive

151.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation With
151.name: With
151.documentation:
Attribute directive bml:with — defines local variables visible within the
element and its descendants. See doc:BmlDirectives.

152.fqnText: org blockml bml annotation BmlAnnotation Xml
152.name: Xml

153.name: Action
153.documentation:
Action capability. Behaviour that neither consumes an external payload nor
produces one — a pure side effect or command (trigger, reset, refresh, invalidate).
Inherits _hasInput=false and _hasOutput=false; inputType and outputType are forbidden.

157.name: AggregationConstraint
157.documentation:
Abstract branch for constraints on Aggregation members. Generic T binds to the
effective AggregationDefinition. Valid only under an Aggregation's <constraints> container
(BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise).

158.name: AllowedChildType
158.documentation:
Aggregation-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective
AggregationDefinition. When validation is set, each composition child under the aggregation must
resolve to the given Block type FQN. Reference implementation for AggregationConstraint branch.
158.idea: A rule for allowed child types

159.name: AssociationConstraint
159.documentation:
Abstract branch for constraints on Association members. Generic T binds to the
effective AssociationDefinition. Valid only under an Association's <constraints> container
(BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise).

160.name: BlockConstraint
160.documentation:
Abstract branch for Block-level structural constraints. May express cross-member
rules (RequiresMember, MutuallyExclusive, …). Generic T binds to the effective
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition type of the enclosing Block (including
SubBlockDefinition, RootBlockDefinition, and EmbeddedBlockDefinition subtypes). Valid only under a Block's
<constraints> container (BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise).
160.idea: A rule for a whole Block

161.name: CapabilityConstraint
161.documentation:
Abstract branch for constraints on Capability members. Generic T binds to the
effective CapabilityDefinition. Valid only under a Capability's <constraints> container
(BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise).

162.name: Max
162.documentation:
Scalar constraint: T binds to the property type. Compatible with Integer, Float,
and Decimal properties. The value property must match T.
162.idea: An upper bound on a number

163.name: MaxItems
163.documentation: T binds to the property collection type (e.g. String[]). The value property is Integer — the maximum item count.
163.idea: An upper bound on item count

164.name: MaxLength
164.documentation: T binds to the property type for scalar String properties, or to the element type when the property is a collection (e.g. String[]). The value property is always Integer — the maximum length threshold.

165.name: MemberConstraint
165.documentation:
Abstract branch for member-level structural constraints. Generic T binds to the
effective MemberDefinition subtype of the embedding context. Specialized by PropertyConstraint,
AggregationConstraint, AssociationConstraint, and CapabilityConstraint.
165.idea: A rule for a Block member

166.name: Min
166.documentation:
Scalar constraint: T binds to the property type. Compatible with Integer, Float,
and Decimal properties. The value property must match T.
166.idea: A lower bound on a number

167.name: MinItems
167.documentation: T binds to the property collection type (e.g. String[]). The value property is Integer — the minimum item count.
167.idea: A lower bound on item count

168.name: MinLength
168.documentation: T binds to the property type for scalar String properties, or to the element type when the property is a collection (e.g. String[]). The value property is always Integer — the minimum length threshold.

169.name: MustBeReadOnly
169.documentation:
Property-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective PropertyDefinition.
When validation is set, the validator requires readOnly=true on the Property (authored or
derived). Reference implementation for PropertyConstraint branch.
169.idea: A rule that a Property is read-only

170.name: NoSelfReference
170.documentation:
Association-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective
AssociationDefinition. When validation is set, association targets must not reference the
enclosing Block's own type. Reference implementation for AssociationConstraint branch.

171.name: Pattern
171.documentation: T binds to org.blockml.bml.type.Text. The value property holds the regex pattern.

172.name: PropertyConstraint
172.documentation:
Abstract branch for constraints on Property definitions (not property values —
see ValueConstraint for value rules). Generic T binds to the effective PropertyDefinition of
the enclosing Property. Valid only under a Property's <constraints> container when the
constraint extends PropertyConstraint (not ValueConstraint).

173.name: RequiresImplementation
173.documentation:
Capability-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective
CapabilityDefinition. When validation is set, the Capability must declare an implementation
binding on concrete Blocks. Reference implementation for CapabilityConstraint branch.
173.idea: A rule that a Capability is implemented

174.name: RequiresMember
174.documentation:
Block-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective block definition type.
When validation is set, the validator requires a member with the given local name in the
effective member set of the Block. Reference implementation for BlockConstraint branch.
174.idea: A rule that a member must exist

175.name: StructuralConstraint
175.documentation:
Abstract branch for structural constraints on definition elements (Blocks and
members). Generic parameter T binds automatically to the effective definition type of the
embedding context at validate time. Separates definition-shape rules from value-level rules
(ValueConstraint).

176.name: ValueConstraint
176.documentation:
Abstract branch for value-level constraints. Generic parameter T binds automatically
to the effective ValueType of the enclosing Property at validate time — authors never specify T
in BML. Valid only under a Property member's <constraints> container
(BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise). Examples: Min, Max, Pattern, ValuePresent.
176.idea: A rule for a concrete value

177.name: ValuePresent
177.documentation:
Scalar constraint: T binds to the property type. The property value must be present
after all model resolution is complete — inheritance, contracts, default values, and instance
value binding. Only authored values count; expression evaluation does not satisfy ValuePresent
(Stage 2 does not evaluate expressions). Enforced by validateConstraints() at Stage 2 only when
validation references an understood Validation block (typically validation:Error). Declares no
own properties beyond the inherited validation reference.
177.idea: A rule that a value must be set

178.name: Alias
178.documentation:
Abstract branch marker for alias Entity instances in an aliases aggregation on
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition only (root blocks and Sub-Blocks). Domain libraries
define concrete alias blocks extending this branch for catalogue-controlled alternative names.
The core library provides org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextAlias for ad-hoc text names and
org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedAlias as the protected base for catalogue aliases whose members are
set on derived alias block definitions; comma-separated shorthand on <aliases> expands to
FreeTextAlias instances only. Not XML
namespace prefix aliases. Not search tags — use org.blockml.bml.core.Keyword branch for those.

179.name: Annotation
179.documentation:
Abstract branch for annotation namespaces. Every BML-semantic xmlns prefix must resolve to
either a Package (FQN prefix under which types live) or a concrete Annotation. Annotations are
orthogonal to the Definition meta-model (org.blockml.bml.definition.*): they do not describe
block structure, members, or constraints. They declare which directive QNames are legal under
a preferred authoring alias (e.g. bml, scad).

preferredAlias is authoring convention only — the BOM stores the Annotation FQN, never the
XML prefix. directives lists the concrete Directive kinds this annotation exposes.

Directive taxonomy (SubBlocks — not Definition member kinds):
• Directive — base; property name is the directive local name
• Member (name="*") — wildcard member directives under this namespace
  → Property · Aggregation · Association · Capability
• Element — element-form directives
  → Document (name="document") · Summary (name="summary") · Examples (name="examples")
    · Example (name="example") — sibling under StructuralDefinition examples container
    · Value (name="value") — PropertyDefinition value-field facets
• Attribute — attribute-form directives (id, with, each, …)

Naming overlap with Definition (Property, Aggregation, …) is classification of directive form
only — Annotation.Property is not def:PropertyDefinition. Annotation.Value facets nested under
a property declaration (e.g. <myProp><scad:value>…</scad:value></myProp>)
are not the same as a member QName <scad:value/> under <properties> — parent
context disambiguates.
179.idea: A declared annotation namespace with typed directives

180.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Aggregation
180.name: Aggregation
180.documentation:
Classifies annotation QNames as aggregation-shaped member directives
(name="*"). Orthogonal to org.blockml.bml.definition.AggregationDefinition.

181.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Association
181.name: Association
181.documentation:
Classifies annotation QNames as association-shaped member directives
(name="*"). Orthogonal to org.blockml.bml.definition.AssociationDefinition.

182.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Attribute
182.name: Attribute
182.documentation:
Directive that appears as an XML attribute under the annotation namespace
(e.g. bml:id, bml:each, bml:with). Concrete directives set name to the attribute local
name.

183.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Capability
183.name: Capability
183.documentation:
Classifies annotation QNames as capability-shaped member directives
(name="*"). Orthogonal to org.blockml.bml.core.Capability and
org.blockml.bml.definition.CapabilityDefinition.

184.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Directive
184.name: Directive
184.documentation:
Abstract base for all annotation directives. The name property is the
directive local name under the annotation namespace (e.g. id, with, document, examples,
example, value). Member directives fix name to "*"; Document, Summary, Examples, Example,
and Value fix document / summary / examples / example / value; Attribute and Element
concretes set an explicit local name.

185.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Document
185.name: Document
185.documentation:
Standard element directive for namespaced document prose facets. name is
fixed to "document" (e.g. scad:document). Distinct from the default-namespace
Definition property documentation — Annotation facets never satisfy required canonical
documentation slots.

186.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Element
186.name: Element
186.documentation:
Directive that appears as an XML element under the annotation namespace
(e.g. bml:container, scad:document, scad:examples, sibling scad:example, nested scad:value).
Concrete directives set name; Document, Summary, Examples, Example, and Value are standard
element kinds with fixed names.

187.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Example
187.name: Example
187.documentation:
Standard element directive for a target-language sample as a sibling of
StructuralDefinition.Example under the same <examples> container. name is fixed to
"example" (e.g. scad:example next to <example>). Parent context: direct child of
<examples> with an Annotation prefix → this Example facet entry; unprefixed
<example> → StructuralDefinition.Example. Same shape as a canonical example (required
title, optional language / snippet, CDATA body). Prefer this over a parallel scad:examples
container when BML and OpenSCAD bodies are one logical pair (match by title). Does not
replace canonical <example> entries.

188.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Examples
188.name: Examples
188.documentation:
Standard element directive for namespaced examples containers. name is fixed
to "examples" (e.g. scad:examples). Parallel to Document and Summary facets: the default-
namespace <examples> aggregation on StructuralDefinition remains the canonical slot;
Annotation-prefixed containers (scad:examples, …) hold independent facet-specific sample
sets and never replace the canonical examples aggregation. Prefer Annotation.Example
(scad:example sibling under the same <examples>) when a target-language sample pairs
1:1 with a canonical <example>.

189.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Member
189.name: Member
189.documentation:
Member-shaped directive under an annotation namespace. name is fixed to "*"
— the concrete local name comes from the authoring QName (e.g. scad:value). Specialized by
Property, Aggregation, Association, and Capability. Not a Definition member type.

190.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Property
190.name: Property
190.documentation:
Classifies annotation QNames as property-shaped member directives (name="*").
Orthogonal to org.blockml.bml.definition.PropertyDefinition.

191.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Summary
191.name: Summary
191.documentation:
Standard element directive for namespaced summary prose facets. name is
fixed to "summary" (e.g. scad:summary). Distinct from the default-namespace Definition
property summary.

192.fqnText: org blockml bml core Annotation Value
192.name: Value
192.documentation:
Standard element directive for namespaced PropertyDefinition value facets.
name is fixed to "value" (e.g. <myProp><scad:value>1.6</scad:value></myProp>).
Multiplies the value field of an existing property along the Annotation namespace axis —
same property identity (myProp), not a member QName scad:myProp and not a top-level
<properties><scad:value/></properties> member (that is Annotation.Property /
Member). Parent context disambiguates: nested under a property element → Value facet;
direct child of properties → Member when the Annotation declares Property (name="*").
Cross-namespace faceting is valid (for example <something:myProp><scad:value>…);
same-namespace self-faceting is forbidden (for example
<scad:value><scad:value>…). Canonical <value> remains the default-namespace
slot; facet values never replace it for BML semantics — renderers may prefer a matching
Annotation facet.

193.name: Block
193.documentation:
Root semantic unit of BlockML — the sole inheritance root for all Block definitions.
Every concept in the grammar is a Block: composable domain types, ValueTypes, Languages,
Status values, Constraints, Capabilities, Exceptions, Services, Libraries, and Definition meta-model
types. Unqualified name Block resolves to this type.

Role and constraints:
• Sole inheritance root — omits <baseType>; all other definitions must declare a non-empty parent FQN
• Abstract — not used directly as a composition instance type
• Further members defined by sub-types — Properties, Aggregations,
  Associations, and Capabilities via the baseType chain
• Composition instance identity uses bml:id and bml:version (not member attributes)
• Documentation prose language is Definition meta (def:BlockDefinition.language), not a
  member of this type — this document authors <language><English/></language> as the
  framework default for inheritance

Type reference rules:
• Aggregation member types may be any Block FQN
• Association member types must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[]
• Property and Capability payload types must resolve to a ValueType
• Capability throws lists Exception types via TypeReferenceEntity — not ValueType payloads
• Capability implementation language attributes reference org.blockml.bml.language.* — unqualified names permitted

Documentation model (on every root block definition — see def:BlockDefinition /
doc:DocumentationModel):
• Definition identity first — element type/name tag (preferred) or <name> / <type> /
  <baseType> (baseType omitted only here; dual format: doc:DocumentFormat)
• <is> — always required after identity; clear Urbild designation (what the Block semantically represents)
• <summary> — required when documentation is too long for a quick scan
• <language> — optional Definition meta; natural language for documentation prose
  (inherits from enclosing Library document, then this Block document's English default)
• <documentation> — always required; technical description; optional language
  attribute when prose deviates from effective block language
• <isNot> — required when confusion risk exists
• Optional extensions: <since>, <changelog>, <examples>, <references>
Omitted is or documentation → BML_MISSING_IS / BML_MISSING_DOCUMENTATION; missing isNot or
