summary when required → BML_MISSING_IS_NOT / BML_MISSING_SUMMARY (warning V1).

Serialization:
• bml:xml ${ bml:Self } — composable instances render under their declared type tag
  (for example <core:Block>, <myns:Wall>)
• Definition branch types describe block structure and carry their own bml:xml rules

194.name: BlockLibrary
194.documentation:
Abstract publishable library unit — groups exported Block and ValueType definitions,
optional legacy XSD schemas, dependencies on other libraries, and nested sub-libraries.
Replaces the legacy library.xml descriptor. XSD is not a standard feature
(doc:DocumentFormat).

Framework base type in org.blockml.bml.core — not exported via Library blocks.
Concrete Library.bml files inherit from BlockLibrary and declare aggregations explicitly.

Catalog aggregations are public and readOnly: foreign Blocks and tools may inspect a library
descriptor (e.g. list exports or dependencies) in expressions; only the Library definition
(and child overrides) may author the catalog. Instances must not rewrite these members.

Documentation prose language is Definition meta (def:BlockDefinition.language) on the Library
document — not a catalog aggregation. Exported blocks inherit that document language unless
they declare their own <language>.

Aggregations (each aggregation member is opened by name; none is default):
• readMe — required human/LLM reading entry (ReadMe block, 1..1)
• bootstrap — optional automation SPOE (Bootstrap block, 0..1)
• dependencies — other Library blocks this library depends on (typical: inner library
  depends on outer)
• subLibraries — nested child Library blocks grouped under this library
• schemas — optional legacy XSD paths as FilePathEntity instances; omitted by default
• blocks — exported Block and ValueType definitions (membership SSOT)

readMe and bootstrap hold TypeReferenceEntity children — empty QName sugar sets value to
that FQN. dependencies, subLibraries, and blocks use the same pattern. Optional bml:version on
sugar (or explicit TypeReferenceEntity) children is an exact-version assert against the
referenced type (value) — same semantics as external composition references; omitted → resolve
from TypeRegistry / library context; no match → BML_UNKNOWN_VERSION. schemas holds
FilePathEntity composition children; value is the relative .xsd path from the library package
root (directory containing Library.bml).

Concrete Library.bml <references> rule — at most two <see> entries:
1. Required: relation=ReadFirst targeting the same ReadMe named in readMe.
2. Optional: relation=ThenContinueWith targeting the Bootstrap named in bootstrap, only when
   bootstrap is present. Signals: after reading, continue by executing the automation SPOE.
No AuthoringGuide / DeepDive / Extends / SeeAlso (or other) entries on concrete Libraries —
those belong on documentation blocks, not on the catalog descriptor.

195.name: Bootstrap
195.documentation:
Abstract empty branch for Bootstrap blocks — the optional single point of entry
(SPOE) for automated startup: tasks, agents, CI pipelines, and similar process logic. Intentionally
empty — no properties or aggregations. Concrete subtypes add scenario-specific members when
needed.

Distinct from org.blockml.bml.core.ReadMe, which is the required human/LLM reading entry on a
Library (readMe aggregation). A Library may omit bootstrap (0..1) when it has no automated
startup SPOE; it must never declare more than one Bootstrap.

Human/LLM orientation (curated ReadFirst reading order, TaskIndex catalog) lives on ReadMe
blocks — not on Bootstrap.

196.name: Capability
196.documentation:
Capability branch of BlockML. Declares a capability type. Every capability may
carry an implementation whose language attribute references a Language FQN.

The implementation body is not restricted to a compiler-emit template. It may
describe intent (PseudoCode or a natural language), supply a companion template
for a renderer, or be a deterministic function a host toolchain evaluates.
Those readings coexist — doc:CapabilitySemantics.

Exception types a capability may raise are declared on
org.blockml.bml.definition.CapabilityDefinition.throws
(type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]) — not on this branch type.

197.name: Constraint
197.documentation:
Abstract universal root for all constraint types. Specialized by
org.blockml.bml.constraint.ValueConstraint (property value rules) and
org.blockml.bml.constraint.StructuralConstraint (definition-shape rules on Blocks and members).
Every concrete constraint extends one of the branch types; the <constraints> embedding
context determines the target and automatic generic binding — authors never specify target or
type arguments in BML. Constraints describe the condition only. Whether BlockML enforces a
constraint is controlled by the optional validation property, which references an
org.blockml.bml.core.Validation block. When validation is omitted, validateConstraints() does not
enforce the rule — the constraint remains metadata for renderers, editors, runtimes, and custom
validators. The constraint instance itself is still validated (type, properties, generic
binding, branch compatibility).

198.name: Definition
198.documentation:
Abstract identification marker for the Definition branch under org.blockml.bml.core.Block.
Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks. Any block whose baseType
chain includes org.blockml.bml.core.Definition is a Definition meta-model block
(org.blockml.bml.definition.*). Concrete grammar lives on subtypes such as
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition and org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition.

Used as a generic constraint and branch marker for definition-element references. Member path
ValueTypes (org.blockml.bml.type.MemberIdentifier and children) constrain D to
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition. Framework core branch types remain baseType markers;
domain interface-style type bounds use contracts and satisfiesTypeBound — see 17_type_system_bml.md.

199.name: Diagnostic
199.documentation:
Abstract branch for org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* blocks. Each concrete diagnostic
block documents one validator or parser code (for example BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE) with is, summary,
keywords, and references. Use relation=Resolves on <see> to link to a TaskGuide that
walks through the fix. Enables agents and humans to navigate from a reported error to a
procedural resolution path without searching documentation prose.

200.name: Documentation
200.documentation:
Abstract base for org.blockml.bml.documentation.* blocks — curated reading material that
explains BlockML concepts in mental learning order. Each concrete documentation block
carries is, documentation, and references; cross-links belong in references, not in
documentation prose. Listed via relation=ReadFirst on README and other ReadMe blocks.
Procedural how-to blocks extend org.blockml.bml.core.TaskGuide instead.

201.name: Entity
201.documentation:
Abstract branch for Entities — Blocks that represent instances with identity in
composition or aggregation. Domain blocks, built-in services, and PrimitiveEntity wrappers extend
Entity. Entity is not a ValueType; use Property with a ValueType for typed payloads.

202.name: Exception
202.documentation:
Abstract branch for exception types that a Capability may declare it can raise.

Corresponds to Java exception classes used in a method `throws` clause: the type is listed
on the Capability signature; instances carry a human-readable message.

Domain libraries define concrete exception types extending this branch (for example
`com.example.bml.FileNotFound`). Capability members list those types on
`org.blockml.bml.definition.CapabilityDefinition.throws` via
`type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]` — empty-QName sugar such as `<io:FileNotFound />`.

Distinct from `org.blockml.bml.core.Diagnostic`, which catalogues validator and parser codes
rather than Capability-thrown failures.

203.name: Group
203.documentation:
Abstract base type for groups — named categories that organize related elements
for editors and tooling. Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks.
Concrete group kinds extend this branch (e.g. org.blockml.bml.group.MemberGroup for Block
members, org.blockml.bml.group.BlockGroup for Blocks).

204.name: Keyword
204.documentation:
Abstract branch marker for keyword Entity instances in a keywords aggregation on
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition elements. Follows Everything-is-a-Block —
domain libraries define concrete keyword blocks extending this branch for controlled vocabulary
tags (for example org.example.keyword.Inheritance extending org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword).
The core library provides org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextKeyword for ad-hoc text tags and
org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword as the protected base for catalogue keywords whose members are
set on derived keyword block definitions; comma-separated shorthand on <keywords> expands
to FreeTextKeyword instances only — not to domain or FixedKeyword catalogue blocks.
Distinct from org.blockml.bml.core.Alias (alternative Block type names on BlockDefinition).

205.name: Language
205.documentation:
Language branch of BlockML. Declares an implementation language permitted on
Capability implementations (OpenSCAD, TypeScript, English, …). Natural languages for
documentation prose extend org.blockml.bml.language.NaturalLanguage; formal code and markup
languages extend ProgrammingLanguage and MarkupLanguage. ProgrammingLanguage and MarkupLanguage
declare optional generic L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content/text language of
formal bodies — omit L unless the content language must be declared.

206.name: Mapping
206.documentation:
Abstract branch for explicit value mapping between representations. Mapping is not a property
of StructType — it belongs at the site where a function-like representation is used.

Concrete mappings extend this branch and declare how authored syntax maps to BlockML types and
how BlockML types map to target-language signatures.

Component responsibilities:
• Parser — stores authored syntax only; no mapping in Canonical BOM
• Expression parser — AST with positional, named, object, and array literal arguments
• Validator — resolves capability, selects FunctionMapping, validates mapped input against
  inputType
• Renderer — may emit authored form, evaluate FunctionMapping, or interpret mapping for the
  target system; Canonical BOM stays unchanged

207.name: PrimitiveEntity
207.documentation:
Abstract generic Entity for primitive values that must appear as Block instances
inside a composition or aggregation. Follows the general generic resolution rule: T belongs
exclusively to this Block and is never inherited. Derived Blocks bind or forward T explicitly
through baseType (for example baseType = PrimitiveEntity(Integer) binds T = Integer and yields
value : Integer). On instances that member is authored as value="…" (or <value>…</value>
as the member itself) because the Property is named value — not because of the
PropertyDefinition value field. Do not wrap other instance Properties in <value>; see
doc:MemberAuthoring.

Cannot be instantiated directly — concrete specializations (IntegerEntity, TextEntity,
DecimalEntity, …) bind all generic parameters and become normal, instantiable Blocks.

Properties continue to store primitive values directly — PrimitiveEntity exists only when the
primitive value itself must become an Entity with identity, documentation, or metadata.
207.idea: A primitive value as an Entity

208.name: ReadMe
208.documentation:
Abstract branch for ReadMe blocks. A ReadMe declares where humans and LLMs start
reading a library — curated learning order, vocabulary, and orientation. Distinct from
org.blockml.bml.core.Bootstrap, which is the optional single point of entry (SPOE) for automated
startup (tasks, agents, CI pipelines).

org.blockml.bml.README is the standard ReadMe for the core library. Library descriptors point
here via the required readMe aggregation (1..1).

ReadMe blocks carry the normal documentation model (is, documentation, references). Curated
reading order is expressed via <references> with relation=ReadFirst; available task
catalog entries via relation=TaskIndex — not via separate aggregations on ReadMe itself. The
abstract base declares no members.

209.name: Relation
209.documentation:
Abstract branch for relation blocks on <see> entries in <references>.
Relation values are Block references following the Everything-is-a-Block principle.
Standard implementations live in org.blockml.bml.relation.*; domain libraries may define
additional relation blocks. Implicit default when omitted on <see>:
org.blockml.bml.relation.SeeAlso. Standard relations include ReadFirst (README learning path),
ReadNext (forward edge between documentation blocks), ThenContinueWith (Library bootstrap after
reading — TypeRelation(core:Bootstrap)), TaskIndex (task catalog), TaskStep and Prerequisite
(procedural guides), and Resolves (diagnostic to fix task). Unqualified names on relation=
resolve via implicit namespace org.blockml.bml.relation.*.

TypeRelation is the constrained subtype for relations that may only target see type= and whose
target must satisfy a generic Block branch T (default core:Block).

210.name: Status
210.documentation:
Abstract branch for status blocks. Status values are Block references following the
Everything-is-a-Block principle. Standard implementations live in org.blockml.bml.status.*;
domain libraries may define additional status blocks. Implicit default when omitted:
org.blockml.bml.status.Stable. Status is inherited downward — declare <status> or bml:status
only when deviating from the effective inherited status.

211.name: TaskGuide
211.documentation:
Abstract branch for org.blockml.bml.task.* blocks — step-by-step procedures
distinct from org.blockml.bml.documentation.* concept blocks. TaskGuide blocks carry the normal
documentation model (is, summary, keywords, documentation, references). Ordered procedure
steps use relation=TaskStep on <see> entries; prerequisites use relation=Prerequisite.
Task catalogs on README / ReadMe blocks list available tasks via relation=TaskIndex.
Tooling filters by relation to build learn paths (ReadFirst), task paths (TaskStep), or error
fix paths (Diagnostic blocks with relation=Resolves).

212.name: TypeRelation
212.documentation:
Abstract Relation subtype that may be used only on <see type="…"> entries —
never on instance, file, url, property, aggregation, association, or capability targets.

Generic T is the allowed target Block branch. The resolved type of see type= must satisfy
satisfiesTypeBound(resolve(type), T) — otherwise BML_TYPE_BOUND_NOT_SATISFIED. Default
T = core:Block — any Block type reference is allowed until a concrete subtype binds T more
narrowly (e.g. ThenContinueWith binds T = core:Bootstrap).

Plain Relation (SeeAlso, AuthoringGuide, …) remains unrestricted across target kinds.
TypeRelation is for relations whose semantics require a Block type identity target.

213.name: Unit
213.documentation:
Abstract Block branch for measurement units — a taxonomy/catalog like Language
or Status, not a ValueType. Unit blocks describe a unit of measure; they never store concrete
magnitudes and are not valid as Property type or Capability inputType/outputType. They appear
as generic type arguments on Number (and domain types such as MultiAxis) — e.g.
Decimal(unit:Millimeter), Float(unit:Degree). Standard implementations live in
org.blockml.bml.unit.*; domain libraries may define additional unit blocks.

214.name: Validation
214.documentation:
Abstract branch for validation semantics. A Validation block describes whether and
how BlockML itself should enforce an attached constraint. Constraints reference Validation via
the optional validation property on org.blockml.bml.core.Constraint. When validation is omitted,
the BlockML validator ignores the constraint — it remains metadata for renderers, editors,
runtimes, and custom validators. Standard implementations live in org.blockml.bml.validation.*;
domain libraries may define additional Validation blocks (for example
com.machineblocks.bml.validation.ManufacturingWarning). The BlockML validator only interprets
Validation types it understands; other tools may interpret additional Validation blocks.

215.name: ValueType
215.documentation:
ValueType branch of BlockML. Semantic unit for property and Capability types
(primitives, structs, enums). A ValueType never stores data — it describes the nature of a
value. All concrete values are stored exclusively in Properties. Only ValueTypes may appear as
property type or Capability inputType/outputType.

Top of the value assignability hierarchy — every PrimitiveType, StructType, EnumType, and
ConstantType is assignable to ValueType. With multiplicity, compatibility is evaluated against
the referenced element type: ValueType[] accepts zero or more values whose concrete ValueType is
assignable to ValueType, each element validated independently, so element types may differ
within one collection. See doc:TypeExpressions — Collection compatibility ·
Heterogeneous collections.

216.name: AggregationDefinition
216.documentation:
Describes a Block member representing an owned collection. Children are always
Block instances; the aggregation type attribute selects the payload type:

• Plain Block type (for example core:Block[], bricks:Brick[]) — composition ownership of those
  Block types. Children are Block instances: member values, nested aggregations filled without
  a composition wrapper, and bml:id. A child whose type still has open genericTypes after
  inheritance must bind them with bml:generics (attribute or child element; parenthesized
  TypeExpression list). Missing → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE. See doc:GenericsModel.
• TypeReferenceEntity application (for example type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Block)[]) —
  owned TypeReferenceEntity instances whose value holds an FQN / TypeExpression. Empty children
  whose element QName is not TypeReferenceEntity are syntactic sugar for
  <type:TypeReferenceEntity value="…QName…" /> (B/D bound by the aggregation type).

Rendered as a child element inside the aggregations container; the XML element name is the
aggregation name (bml:xml="${ #this.name }"). An optional XML prefix on the element name supplies
the member namespace — resolved via xmlns to BOM namespace; unprefixed elements use the default
namespace (empty string). Member identity is (resolvedNamespace, localName). Maps to BOM
AggregationDefinition (kind: "aggregation") with type expression, cardinality (from type
multiplicity), optional default flag, and optional nested composition template. Standalone
composition is never allowed — <composition> must be nested inside the aggregation member
(BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION). Scalar member fields (type, default) follow
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition placement rules — element preferred on aggregation
declarations. Structured composition remains a child element.
Composition instance ID reachability for bml:id references is controlled by this aggregation
member's visibility (inherited from org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition) — public
aggregations export ids for cross-document {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{id} references; protected
limits reach to the declaring Block and its child Blocks; private limits reach to the declaring
Block only. Service binding on composition children uses bml:bean and bml:scope on Block
instances — not aggregation member fields. Open generic children use bml:generics on the
instance — not aggregation member fields.

217.fqnText: org blockml bml definition AggregationDefinition Composition
217.name: Composition
217.documentation:
Describes the composition element on an aggregation member declaration only.
Rendered as composition with optional bml:with directives and a tree of composition child
nodes (Block instances and bml:container virtual containers). Not an instance wrapper —
nested Block instances in this tree fill their own aggregations directly, without a nested
composition element. Maps to BOM
CompositionTemplate { aggregationName (from enclosing aggregation member name), directives,
children }. Instance ID reachability is determined by the enclosing aggregation member's
visibility — not by attributes on the composition element. Standalone composition outside an
aggregation member element is invalid (BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION). Declared as the
composition property on org.blockml.bml.definition.AggregationDefinition.

218.name: AssociationDefinition
218.documentation:
Describes a Block member that connects instances to instances — non-owning model
links between concrete Block instances, without lifecycle ownership. Distinct from documentation
References (<see> on StructuralDefinition.references), which connect types to types or
types to instances for documentation only. Rendered as a child element inside the associations
container; the XML element name is the association name (bml:xml="${ #this.name }"). An optional
XML prefix on the element name supplies the member namespace — resolved via xmlns to BOM
namespace; unprefixed elements use the default namespace (empty string). Member identity is
(resolvedNamespace, localName). Maps to BOM AssociationDefinition (kind: "association") with
type (InstanceReference TypeExpression) and cardinality (from type multiplicity). Association
type must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[] with T extending core:Block — bare
Block FQNs (e.g. core:Block, bml:Self[]) are invalid. Instance values are authored on Block
instances as member attributes or elements (space-separated InstanceReference tokens, or
expressions). Associations do not own composition children. Scalar member field type follows
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition placement rules — element preferred on definitions,
attribute preferred on Block instances. Domain examples include basePresets on MachineBlocks
Block types (type InstanceReference(bml:Self)[]).

219.name: BlockDefinition
219.documentation:
Abstract meta-model base for all Block definition documents — root blocks,
Sub-Blocks, and embedded virtual files. Semantically a Class: declarative type shape without instance
state. Parsed into BomDocument.block and nested block definition trees. Generic type parameter B
binds this definition to the Block type it describes — conceptually BlockDefinition of
com.foo.Bar when B resolves to com.foo.Bar.

Declares identity first (name, type, baseType, version), then semantic and discovery fields
(is, isNot, aliases), generic parameters, contracts, and
member declaration containers (properties, aggregations, associations, capabilities). Inherits
summary and keywords aggregation (core.Keyword[]) from
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. isNot is block-level only; aliases aggregation
(core.Alias[]) lists domain Alias blocks or org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextAlias instances. Omitted when unnecessary. Type modifiers abstract and final are inherited from
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. Every definition element is addressable via
its canonical structural path within the Block FQN (for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width).
Member declaration order in BML is preserved in BOM and is significant for StructType
positional mapping and render targets.

Declares definition (meta-model role selector) and subBlocks (recursive nested type hierarchy).
Specialized as three sibling kinds that each override definition with a tighter TypeReference and
default: SubBlockDefinition (nested), RootBlockDefinition (document root + embeddedBlocks),
EmbeddedBlockDefinition (virtual .bml under root embeddedBlocks). Identity properties type and
baseType are TypeReference strings (not TypeReferenceEntity aggregations) — type names the Block
being declared; baseType carries the parent TypeExpression including generic applications. Other
type references (composition tags, member type attributes, contracts) accept FQN, xmlns QName,
context-bound unqualified fallback, or Sub-Block-relative names — all normalized to a canonical
FQN during resolution (BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE, BML_AMBIGUOUS_TYPE, BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX).
219.idea: The shape of a Block document

220.name: CapabilityDefinition
220.documentation:
Describes a Block member defining how the Block communicates. Rendered as a child
element inside the capabilities container; the XML element name is the capability name
(bml:xml="${ #this.name }"). An optional XML prefix on the element name supplies the member
namespace — resolved via xmlns to BOM namespace; unprefixed elements use the default namespace
(empty string). Member identity is (resolvedNamespace, localName).

Maps to BOM CapabilityDefinition (kind: "capability") with typeFqn, inputType, outputType,
optional throws, and optional implementation binding. Inbound requires inputType; Outbound
requires outputType; Transformation requires both; Action requires neither. inputType and
outputType use TypeExpression syntax and must resolve to ValueTypes.

throws lists Exception types this Capability may raise — the BlockML equivalent of a Java
method throws clause (type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]).

Scalar capability fields (type, inputType, outputType) follow
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition placement rules — element preferred on definitions,
attribute preferred on Block instances. Structured implementation remains a child element;
throws is an aggregation of TypeReferenceEntity children.

221.fqnText: org blockml bml definition CapabilityDefinition Implementation
221.name: Implementation
221.documentation:
Describes the implementation element on a capability member. Rendered as
implementation with a required language attribute referencing org.blockml.bml.language.*
and a CDATA source body. Maps to BOM ImplementationBlock { languageFqn, source,
embeddedExpressions }. Not a ValueType — structured metadata on the Entity branch. The
body may be intent, a companion template, or a host-evaluable function
(doc:CapabilitySemantics). Capability references inside the body use BML Embedded
Expression syntax (<$ … $>). Declared as the implementation property on
org.blockml.bml.definition.CapabilityDefinition.

222.name: ConstrainableDefinition
222.documentation:
Abstract base for Block and member definitions that support a <constraints>
container. The embedding context determines the constraint target and binds the generic type
parameter automatically — no target property in BML. Validator checks branch compatibility via
the constraint baseType chain (BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH). Constraint order in BML is
preserved in BOM. Target binding and generic resolution are not stored in the Canonical BOM.
222.idea: A definition that can carry Constraints

223.name: EmbeddedBlockDefinition
223.documentation:
Meta-model type for embedded Block documents — virtual .bml files inlined under
the document root's <embeddedBlocks> aggregation. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition (subBlocks, identity, members) and overrides
definition to default EmbeddedBlockDefinition.

Embedded blocks are full Block documents. Authoring is the same as the document root
(doc:DocumentFormat): preferred type tag (<acme:MyBlock>), legacy <block> plus
<type>. The resolved type is the FQN (not nested under the root) and must be fully
qualified. They may declare subBlocks and generics like any Block. They must
not declare <embeddedBlocks> — nesting is forbidden (BML_NESTED_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS). Only the
document root (RootBlockDefinition) may own embeddedBlocks; compose fat artifacts by listing
virtual files flat at the root (bundlers flatten nested packages when merging).

Within the BomDocument, each embedded FQN shadows the corresponding library or file-based
BlockDefinition. Duplicate FQNs among embeds → BML_DUPLICATE_EMBEDDED_BLOCK. Externally,
embeds are invisible.
223.idea: The shape of an embedded Block document

224.name: GenericTypeDefinition
224.documentation:
Declares one generic type parameter on a root Block definition. Rendered inside
the genericTypes container as an element whose local name is the parameter identifier (root
block only). Maps to BOM GenericType { name, baseType, defaultType? } — name is derived from
the XML element name, not from a child or attribute. The name is substituted in type references
within this Block (e.g. type="T" → GenericParameterReference). baseType is the FQN constraint —
each concrete type argument at reference sites (type applications and instance bml:generics)
must inherit from that branch (BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION on mismatch). Optional
defaultType supplies the binding when a generic application or bml:generics omits the
corresponding type argument: a concrete TypeExpression, or the name of an earlier sibling
generic parameter (declaration-order only; cycles and forward references forbidden). Must
satisfy baseType after resolution. See 17_type_system_bml.md — defaultType. Parameter name
must differ from the Block name and every Sub-Block name.

225.name: MemberDefinition
225.documentation:
Abstract base type for Block member declarations — properties, aggregations,
associations, and capabilities. Rendered as a child element inside the corresponding member
container on BlockDefinition; the XML element name is the member name (bml:xml="${ #this.name }").
An optional XML prefix on the element name supplies the member namespace — resolved via xmlns to
BOM namespace; unprefixed elements use the default namespace (empty string). Member identity is
(resolvedNamespace, normalizedLogicalName) — visibility prefixes (_ / __) are stripped from the
element localName before match or collision checks. Declaration properties abstract, final, and
override are local to each member declaration — not inherited. Only their semantic effects
propagate (implementation obligations, override prohibitions).

Member value placement (scalar members on PropertyDefinition, CapabilityDefinition, and shared
MemberDefinition fields):
• On member declarations (Block definition documents): each declaration field may render as a
  child element or as an attribute on the member element — both are valid; element form is
  preferred when serializing definitions (e.g. <type>Integer</type> over
  type="Integer"; <value>…</value> over value="…").
• On Block instances (composition): the member itself renders as an attribute or child element
  of the Block — both are valid; attribute form is preferred (e.g. width="50" over
  <width>50</width>). Do not wrap the payload in <value> or <composition>
  — those are PropertyDefinition / AggregationDefinition declaration fields only. Exception: a
  member whose name is value uses value="…" / <value> as the member itself. See
  doc:MemberAuthoring.
Structured children (constraints, groups, suggestions, composition, implementation) remain
elements.

Member declaration modes are orthogonal:
• new — introduces a new member; must not set override="true"
• override="true" — refines an inherited member of the same identity (namespace +
  normalizedLogicalName). Required on every local redeclaration that merges with an existing
  member from the baseType chain or from contracts[] — including contract member completion. Each
  redeclaration layer must set override="true" again — override is not inherited. Omission when a
  parent member exists → BML_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED. Visibility may widen on override (e.g. protected
  `_name` → public `name`); narrowing → BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING. Member-level bml:xml may change
  on the same override. Private members cannot be overridden → BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE.

Declaration properties abstract, final, and override are boolean properties local to the current
declaration (default false). They are never inherited; only semantic effects apply across layers:
- abstract="true" creates an implementation obligation for concrete descendants
- final="true" prevents redeclaration in child blocks (validator checks all declaring layers)
- override="true" confirms a deliberate redefinition of an inherited member

A locally concrete redeclaration (abstract=false, the default) with override="true" satisfies an
inherited implementation obligation when it is complete for the member kind (Property: type;
Aggregation: type; Association: type; Capability: type + implementation). To keep a member
abstract in a child block, explicitly declare abstract="true" on that redeclaration.

Maps to BOM MemberDefinitionBase fields shared by all member kinds — including visibility and
readOnly attributes, plus the groups aggregation (MemberGroup type references).

226.name: PropertyDefinition
226.documentation:
Describes a Block member that carries a scalar or structured value. Rendered as a
child element inside the properties container; the XML element name is the property name
(bml:xml="${ #this.name }"). An optional XML prefix on the element name supplies the member
namespace — for example ui5:width resolves via xmlns:ui5 to the canonical namespace stored in
BOM namespace; unprefixed elements belong to the default namespace (empty string). The prefix
itself is never stored. Member identity is (resolvedNamespace, localName). Maps to BOM
PropertyDefinition (kind: "property") with typeFqn, values[] (value-field entries with
namespace), optional groups (inherited from MemberDefinition), and optional constraints (via
ConstrainableDefinition) and suggestions. Convenience path value is the default-namespace entry.
Property type must resolve to a ValueType branch. Scalar member fields (type, value) follow
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition placement rules on the PropertyDefinition
declaration — element preferred on definitions. The value field is definition syntax only;
it is not a wrapper around a Property assignment on a domain Block instance. On instances the
Property is a Block attribute or the Property element's direct content
(myProperty="…" / <myProperty>…</myProperty>) — see doc:MemberAuthoring. Structured
children (groups, suggestions) remain elements. Every Property behaves as Optional — it has a
value or has no value; there is no null. Declaration order among properties is significant for
StructType positional mapping and Capability parameter order.

Value-field Annotation facets: nested under this property element, an Annotation-prefixed
value element (e.g. scad:value from Annotation.Value) multiplies the value field along the
Annotation namespace axis — same property identity, not a member QName and not scad:myProp.
Parent context disambiguates from top-level <properties><scad:value/> members.
See doc:AnnotationModel — Property value facets.

227.name: RootBlockDefinition
227.documentation:
Meta-model type for document-root block documents. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition, overrides definition (default RootBlockDefinition),
and adds the embeddedBlocks aggregation (Inline Library — virtual .bml files co-located in one
BomDocument). subBlocks is inherited from BlockDefinition.

The definition property defaults to org.blockml.bml.definition.RootBlockDefinition when
<definition> is omitted on the document root. Embedded entries use
org.blockml.bml.definition.EmbeddedBlockDefinition (see EmbeddedBlockDefinition) — they are not
RootBlockDefinition instances. Sub-Blocks use SubBlockDefinition — sibling specialization.

embeddedBlocks is allowed only on the document root. Each child is an EmbeddedBlockDefinition
(virtual file): own FQN from mandatory <type>, own members and subBlocks, no nested
embeddedBlocks. Nested embeds are forbidden (BML_NESTED_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS). Within this document,
embedded FQNs shadow library/file definitions; duplicate embed FQNs →
BML_DUPLICATE_EMBEDDED_BLOCK; externally embeds remain invisible.
227.idea: The shape of a root Block document

228.name: StructuralDefinition
228.documentation:
Abstract base type for BlockML structural definition elements. It provides the common
documentation model consisting of summaries[], keywords, groups, documentations[] (i18n via
language= and optional QName facets — facets are not for locales), version information, change
history, examples, and references, plus local declaration properties (abstract, final) for block
definitions. Concrete structural definition types inherit these members to describe themselves
consistently. Member declarations declare abstract, final, and override locally via
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition. BlockDefinition and MemberDefinition override
groups to narrow the Group branch (BlockGroup and MemberGroup respectively).

229.fqnText: org blockml bml definition StructuralDefinition Change
229.name: Change
229.documentation:
Describes a single changelog entry in a changelog container on any definition
element (block, property, aggregation, …). Rendered as a change element with a required
version attribute and a trimmed text body describing what changed. Maps to BOM
ChangelogEntry { version, text, languageFqn? }. Entries must be ordered chronologically by
version — oldest first (BML_CHANGELOG_VERSION_ORDER when out of order). Optional language
attribute overrides the effective natural language for this entry's text body.

230.fqnText: org blockml bml definition StructuralDefinition Documentation
230.name: Documentation
230.documentation:
Describes one documentation prose entry on any
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition (block, property, aggregation, …). Rendered
as a documentation element (optionally QName-prefixed for Annotation facets) with optional language
attribute and a trimmed text body. The body is Markdown(English) by default — see the
language and content properties for the content model and the CDATA serialization rules.
Authors may place multiple siblings: i18n via language=
(Markdown(NaturalLanguage) or a bare NaturalLanguage); facets via annotation element namespace
(e.g. scad:document from
Annotation.Document). Facet namespaces are Annotations, not locales. Maps to BOM documentations[] DocumentationProseEntry
{ namespace, text, languageFqn }. Identity (namespace, languageFqn) within documentations[] —
duplicate → BML_DUPLICATE_DOCUMENTATION. Declared as a repeatable property shape on
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition.

231.fqnText: org blockml bml definition StructuralDefinition Example
231.name: Example
231.documentation:
Describes one usage example in an examples container on any definition element
(block, property, aggregation, …). Rendered as an example element with a required title
attribute and a character-data body (bml:xml="text" — Text node or CDATA equally valid;
serializer chooses CDATA vs text per escape policy, 19 D8). The enclosing container may be
default-namespace <examples> or an Annotation facet (e.g. scad:examples). Paired
target-language samples use Annotation.Example as a sibling under the same <examples>
(e.g. scad:example with matching title) — preferred over a parallel scad:examples container.
Maps to BOM DocumentationExample { title, content, contentLanguageFqn?, namespace?, snippet }.
Empty body → BML_EXAMPLE_EMPTY_BODY. The title is always written in the effective natural
language of the enclosing block definition. An optional language attribute on the example
element references a Language FQN — implementation languages (OpenSCAD, TypeScript, …) for
code samples, or NaturalLanguage (English, German, …) for prose bodies. Optional snippet
marks illustrative fragments that are not complete / not to be syntax-checked.

232.fqnText: org blockml bml definition StructuralDefinition Reference
232.name: Reference
232.documentation:
Records a documentation link from the current definition to another Block type,
package, Block instance, definition element, repository markdown file, or external URL. References
connect types to types or types to instances for documentation purposes — they are not
instance-to-instance model links (those are Associations / AssociationDefinition). Rendered
as a see element inside the references container on any
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition (alongside changelog and examples). Maps to
BOM DocumentationReference { type?, package?, instance?, file?, url?, property?, aggregation?,
association?, capability?, relationFqn?, context, languageFqn? }. Optional relation attribute
references org.blockml.bml.relation.* — default org.blockml.bml.relation.SeeAlso when omitted.
Optional language attribute overrides the effective natural language for the relationship
text body.

Nine mutually exclusive target attributes (type, package, instance, file, url, property, aggregation,
association, capability) instead of one generic target. Type targets use TypeReference;
package targets use PackageReference; instance targets use InstanceReference; member targets
declare a concrete kind — property : PropertyReference, aggregation : AggregationReference,
association : AssociationReference, capability : CapabilityReference — and store the
canonical definition path in the BOM (for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width).
Split authoring type="com.foo.Bar" property="width" resolves to that path — type qualifies
the member name and is not stored as a separate type target. Split authoring
type="com.foo.Bar" instance="myId" resolves to com.foo.Bar::myId.
The attribute name encodes the target kind at the read site — see type (TypeReference),
see package (PackageReference), see instance (InstanceReference), see property
(PropertyReference), see file (repository documentation), see url (web address). Humans and
LLMs classify each reference from element shape alone without inferring kind from value
syntax. See 02_mbml.md — Associations vs References · references — Why separate target
attributes.

233.name: SubBlockDefinition
233.documentation:
Meta-model type for nested Sub-Block documents within a BomDocument. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition and overrides definition (default SubBlockDefinition).
Shared identity, members, and subBlocks are inherited from BlockDefinition — Sub-Block-specific
identity rules live here.

Block identity conventions for Sub-Blocks (see 02_mbml.md — Type References and Block Identity):
• Sub-Block: semantically nested type within the same BomDocument as the root block — does not
  open its own document or library scope. Analogous to a Java static nested class: may declare
  own <genericTypes>; does not see enclosing Block generics (forward with applications).
  Uses org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition
  as definition meta-model — default org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition when
  <definition> is omitted. name is the local identity (required) — preferred authoring:
  the element local name under <subBlocks> is the Sub-Block name (<MyBlock>);
  child <name> is then optional (doc:DocumentFormat). type is normally
  omitted and derived recursively from the immediate enclosing block as
  resolve(parent.type) + "." + name (BML_SUBBLOCK_TYPE_MISMATCH when an explicit type does not
  match). Sub-Blocks may declare further Sub-Blocks to any depth (for example
  com.foo.Vehicle.Engine.Cylinder). Unqualified nested names resolve enclosing-chain first
  (02_mbml.md — Unqualified nested type resolution). Sub-Blocks must not declare embeddedBlocks
  (BML_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS_ON_SUBBLOCK).

Root blocks use org.blockml.bml.definition.RootBlockDefinition; embedded virtual files use
org.blockml.bml.definition.EmbeddedBlockDefinition — sibling specializations of
BlockDefinition.
233.idea: The shape of a nested Sub-Block

234.name: BML_ABSTRACT_MEMBER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
234.documentation:
Implement with override="true" and a locally complete declaration (abstract defaults to false). To keep abstract, redeclare with abstract="true".
Emitted when a concrete Block still has an abstract member obligation from the inheritance/contract merge.

235.name: BML_AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_MAPPING
235.documentation:
Reserved: emitted when a call maps ambiguously under a custom FunctionMapping. Until custom
mappings ship, treat as reserved.
Reserved: emitted when a call maps ambiguously under a custom FunctionMapping.

236.name: BML_AMBIGUOUS_TYPE
236.documentation:
Emitted when an unqualified type name matches more than one candidate in nested or context-bound
resolution. Remedy: Qualify with xmlns QName, FQN, or Sub-Block-relative path. Grandchildren
are never unqualified.
Emitted when an unqualified type name matches more than one candidate in nested or context-bound resolution.

237.name: BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH
237.documentation:
Emitted when an explicit root name does not equal lastSegment(resolve(type)). Remedy: Root
design principle: type is canonical; name is a redundant short form of the last type segment.
Emitted when an explicit root name does not equal lastSegment(resolve(type)).

238.name: BML_CAPABILITY_LINK_MISMATCH
238.documentation:
Emitted when capability linking pairs incompatible Capability kinds or payloads. Remedy:
Use Outbound→Inbound (or valid Transformation pairing) with compatible inputType/outputType.
Emitted when capability linking pairs incompatible Capability kinds or payloads.

239.name: BML_CARDINALITY_VIOLATION
239.documentation:
Emitted when an aggregation child count or association InstanceReference token count violates
the type multiplicity. Remedy: Adjust the number of aggregation children or association pointer
tokens, or the member multiplicity. Association cardinality is limited to 0..1 and 0..n —
required-single notations (1..1, 1..n) are invalid on associations.
Emitted when an aggregation child count or association InstanceReference token count violates the type multiplicity.

240.name: BML_CHANGELOG_VERSION_ORDER
240.documentation:
Emitted when changelog entries are not in oldest-first version order. Remedy: Order <change>
entries ascending by version.
Emitted when changelog entries are not in oldest-first version order.

241.name: BML_CONSTANT_VALUE_MISMATCH
241.documentation:
Emitted when a value does not equal the configured Constant(T){value: …} literal after type
checks. Remedy: Use the exact singleton literal allowed by the Constant configuration.
Emitted when a value does not equal the configured Constant(T){value: …} literal after type checks.

242.name: BML_CONSTRAINT_INFORMATION
242.documentation:
Emitted when a constraint fails with validation=Information. Remedy: Informational only —
compilation continues.
Emitted when a constraint fails with validation=Information.

243.name: BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH
243.documentation:
Emitted when a Constraint branch is placed in an incompatible embedding context. Remedy:
Constraint generics are compiler-bound from context (Property → ValueType, Aggregation →
AggregationDefinition, …).
Emitted when a Constraint branch is placed in an incompatible embedding context.

244.name: BML_CONSTRAINT_TYPE_MISMATCH
244.documentation:
Emitted when constraint generic T is incompatible with the bound target type. Remedy: Choose
a constraint whose T binds from the embedding context type.
Emitted when constraint generic T is incompatible with the bound target type.

245.name: BML_CONSTRAINT_UNKNOWN
245.documentation:
Emitted when a constraint type is not in TypeRegistry or not a Constraint subtype. Remedy:
Export the constraint via Library.blocks and use a valid Constraint FQN.
Emitted when a constraint type is not in TypeRegistry or not a Constraint subtype.

246.name: BML_CONSTRAINT_VALUE_MISMATCH
246.documentation:
Emitted when a constraint instance property value is incompatible with bound T. Remedy: Fix
the constraint parameter value types (e.g. Min.value).
Emitted when a constraint instance property value is incompatible with bound T.

247.name: BML_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION
247.documentation:
Emitted when a constraint fails with validation=Error. Remedy: Change the authored value
or relax/remove the constraint.
Emitted when a constraint fails with validation=Error.

248.name: BML_CONSTRAINT_WARNING
248.documentation:
Emitted when a constraint fails with validation=Warning. Remedy: Warning only — compilation
continues unless elevated by policy.
Emitted when a constraint fails with validation=Warning.

249.name: BML_CONTRACT_MEMBER_KIND_MISMATCH
249.documentation:
Emitted when a contract member kind does not match the merging member kind. Remedy: Property
overrides property, aggregation overrides aggregation, etc.
Emitted when a contract member kind does not match the merging member kind.

250.name: BML_CONTRACT_NOT_ON_ROOT
250.documentation:
Emitted when <contracts> is declared on a Sub-Block or non-root definition. Remedy:
Contracts are root-block only.
Emitted when <contracts> is declared on a Sub-Block or non-root definition.

251.name: BML_DEFINITION_TYPE_MISMATCH
251.documentation:
Defaults: RootBlockDefinition, SubBlockDefinition, EmbeddedBlockDefinition. Unqualified names resolve via org.blockml.bml.definition.*.
Emitted when the definition meta-model type is incompatible with the block role (root / Sub-Block / embedded).

252.name: BML_DEPRECATED_MEMBER_NAMESPACE_ATTR
252.documentation:
Emitted when a legacy namespace= attribute appears on a member element. Remedy: Use XML element
QName / xmlns prefixes for member namespaces — no namespace attribute.
Emitted when a legacy namespace= attribute appears on a member element.

253.name: BML_DEPRECATED_TYPE
253.documentation:
Emitted when a referenced type is marked deprecated/status Deprecated. Remedy: Prefer the
replacement type; status may be warning-level depending on policy.
Emitted when a referenced type is marked deprecated/status Deprecated.

254.name: BML_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED
254.documentation:
Emitted when a bml: directive appears on an element where it is not permitted. Remedy: See
placement rules for each directive.
Emitted when a bml: directive appears on an element where it is not permitted.

255.name: BML_DUPLICATE_CONTRACT
255.documentation:
Emitted when the same contract FQN appears more than once in <contracts>. Remedy: List
each contract at most once.
Emitted when the same contract FQN appears more than once in <contracts>.

256.name: BML_DUPLICATE_DOCUMENTATION
256.documentation:
Emitted when documentation entries collide on (namespace, languageFqn). Remedy: Keep one
documentation entry per namespace/language pair.
Emitted when documentation entries collide on (namespace, languageFqn).

257.name: BML_DUPLICATE_EMBEDDED_BLOCK
257.documentation:
Emitted when two embedded Blocks in the same document share the same FQN. Remedy: Within
the BomDocument, embed FQNs must be unique. Externally, embeds remain invisible.
Emitted when two embedded Blocks in the same document share the same FQN.

258.name: BML_DUPLICATE_FUNCTION_PARAMETER
258.documentation:
Emitted when a named call argument is supplied more than once. Remedy: Each inputType field
may appear at most once in named form.
Emitted when a named call argument is supplied more than once.

259.name: BML_DUPLICATE_GENERIC
259.documentation:
Emitted when two genericTypes entries share the same parameter name. Remedy: Rename one parameter.
Emitted when two genericTypes entries share the same parameter name.

260.name: BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_NAME
260.documentation:
Emitted when two members share the same (namespace, normalizedLogicalName) identity. Remedy:
Rename one member or fix visibility-prefix duplicates.
Emitted when two members share the same (namespace, normalizedLogicalName) identity.

261.name: BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_VISIBILITY_VARIANT
261.documentation:
Collision checking uses normalizedLogicalName with visibility prefixes stripped. A logical member or Sub-Block exists exactly once with exactly one visibility.
Emitted when members or Sub-Blocks differ only by visibility prefix (myVar / _myVar / __myVar).

262.name: BML_DUPLICATE_PROPERTY_VALUE
262.documentation:
Emitted when property value facets collide on the same annotation namespace. Remedy: One
value entry per namespace; facets multiply along Annotation namespaces.
Emitted when property value facets collide on the same annotation namespace.

263.name: BML_DUPLICATE_SUMMARY
263.documentation:
Emitted when summary entries collide on (namespace, languageFqn). Remedy: Keep one summary
per namespace/language pair.
Emitted when summary entries collide on (namespace, languageFqn).

264.name: BML_DUPLICATE_TYPE_CONFIGURATION
264.documentation:
Emitted when the same configuration property is supplied twice in {...}. Remedy: Provide
each configuration key once.
Emitted when the same configuration property is supplied twice in {...}.

265.name: BML_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS_ON_SUBBLOCK
265.documentation:
Emitted when a Sub-Block declares embeddedBlocks — only the document root may own that aggregation.
Remedy: Sub-Blocks may nest subBlocks but must not declare embeddedBlocks. Flat root embeddedBlocks
compose fat artifacts.
Emitted when a Sub-Block declares embeddedBlocks — only the document root may own that aggregation.

266.name: BML_EXAMPLE_EMPTY_BODY
266.documentation:
Emitted when an example entry has an empty body. Remedy: Provide CDATA/text content for the
example.
Emitted when an example entry has an empty body.

267.name: BML_EXAMPLE_MISSING_TITLE
267.documentation:
Emitted when an example omits the required title. Remedy: Add title= on the example entry.
Emitted when an example omits the required title.

268.name: BML_EXAMPLE_UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE
268.documentation:
Emitted when example language= does not resolve to a Language block. Remedy: Use org.blockml.bml.language.*
(implementation dialect for CDATA).
Emitted when example language= does not resolve to a Language block.

269.name: BML_EXPR_BUILTIN_NOT_V1
269.documentation:
Emitted when a built-in outside the V1 supported set is called. Remedy: V1 includes a focused
#math / #numbers / #strings / #lists subset — see doc:Expressions V1 scope.
Emitted when a built-in outside the V1 supported set is called.

270.name: BML_EXPR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO
270.documentation:
Emitted for compile-time division by zero when both operands are literals. Only literal operand
cases are checked at validate time; runtime division remains renderer concern.
Emitted for compile-time division by zero when both operands are literals.

271.name: BML_EXPR_LINK_INVALID_SOURCE
271.documentation:
Emitted when @bean.capa (no parentheses) is used on a non-Outbound Capability. Remedy: Capability
linking without call parentheses requires an Outbound source.
Emitted when @bean.capa (no parentheses) is used on a non-Outbound Capability.

272.name: BML_EXPR_LINK_INVALID_TARGET
272.documentation:
Emitted when capability linking targets a Capability that is not Inbound. Remedy: Link targets
must be Inbound (or compatible Transformation pairing rules).
Emitted when capability linking targets a Capability that is not Inbound.

273.name: BML_EXPR_LINK_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH
273.documentation:
Emitted when linked Capabilities have incompatible inputType/outputType. Remedy: Ensure linked
Outbound/Inbound (or Transformation) payloads are compatible.
Emitted when linked Capabilities have incompatible inputType/outputType.

274.name: BML_EXPR_MODEL_NO_CONTEXT
274.documentation:
Emitted when a relative @model: path is used without a binding context. Remedy: Absolute
paths start with /. Relative paths require a nearest parent Model-bound Aggregation. V1 defers
model runtime.
Emitted when a relative @model: path is used without a binding context.

275.name: BML_EXPR_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_INTERPOLATION
275.documentation:
Emitted when a ${ } hole in interpolated Text uses a construct outside the Restricted Profile.
Holes allow property access, literals, + (Text / Number), #strings.*, and #math.* only.
Forbidden in holes: @model, @bean, Capability linking / own-calls, and bml:each / bml:with
variables. Remedy: keep the hole on the Restricted Profile, or author a whole-value
"${ expr }" ExpressionValue when the full language is required (doc:Expressions).
Emitted when an interpolation hole uses a construct outside the Restricted Profile.

276.name: BML_EXPR_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH
276.documentation:
Emitted when call syntax does not match declared inputType after FunctionMapping. Remedy:
Adjust positional/named/object-literal arguments to the Capability inputType shape.
Emitted when call syntax does not match declared inputType after FunctionMapping.

277.name: BML_EXPR_SYNTAX_ERROR
277.documentation:
Emitted when expression raw text fails to parse (parseExpression utility). Remedy: Check
${ } / <$ $> delimiters, quotes, operators, and balanced brackets. An unclosed ${ in
interpolated Text is this code. Nested embed delimiters are invalid.
Emitted when expression raw text fails to parse (parseExpression utility).

278.name: BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH
278.documentation:
Emitted when the expression result type is incompatible with the target member type, or when
interpolated Text holes are authored on a member that is not type:Text. Remedy: Align
operators/calls with the Property or Capability payload type after inference. Keep
interpolation on type:Text (or type:Text[] string leaves) — doc:Expressions.
Emitted when the expression result type is incompatible with the target member type.

279.name: BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_BEAN
279.documentation:
Emitted when @bean refers to a name not declared as a service bean Aggregation. Remedy: Register
the instance with bml:bean (and optional bml:scope). V1 defers bean execution.
Emitted when @bean refers to a name not declared as a service bean Aggregation.

280.name: BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN
280.documentation:
Emitted when #name is not a registered built-in service Capability. Remedy: Use documented
#math / #strings / #lists / #numbers / #bools names. Unknown or misspelled builtins fail
validation.
Emitted when #name is not a registered built-in service Capability.

281.name: BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY
281.documentation:
Emitted when an identifier is not found in scope, or index access is used on a StructType
field. Remedy: Property access is the outer Block instance (#this). this without # is a
member (#this.this), not the instance. StructType members are addressed by name (size.x),
not size[0]. See doc:Expressions.
Emitted when an identifier is not found in scope, or index access is used on a StructType field.

282.name: BML_EXPRESSION_TYPE_ERROR
282.documentation:
Legacy/alias style expression type error — prefer BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH where applicable.
Align expression result type with the target member type.
Legacy/alias style expression type error — prefer BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH where applicable.

283.name: BML_FINAL_BASE_TYPE
283.documentation:
final="true" on a block definition prevents other definitions from extending it. Choose a non-final base or unseal the parent if you control it.
Emitted when a Block uses a final type as baseType.

284.name: BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE
284.documentation:
final="true" seals a declaration. Private members are also non-overridable. Remove the override or change the parent declaration.
Emitted when a child attempts to override a final member, or to override a private member.

285.name: BML_FUNCTION_DUPLICATE_MAIN
285.documentation:
Emitted when an OpenSCAD utility implementation declares more than one main function matching
the Capability name. Remedy: Keep exactly one main function named like the Capability.
Emitted when an OpenSCAD utility implementation declares more than one main function matching the Capability name.

286.name: BML_FUNCTION_MISSING_MAIN
286.documentation:
Emitted when an OpenSCAD utility implementation lacks a main function matching the Capability
name. Remedy: Add function <capabilityName>(...) as the main entry.
Emitted when an OpenSCAD utility implementation lacks a main function matching the Capability name.

287.name: BML_FUNCTION_NO_RUNTIME_IMPL
287.documentation:
Emitted when a Capability requires a runtime implementation that is not provided for the
target. Remedy: Supply an implementation language/body supported by the renderer, or mark
appropriately.
Emitted when a Capability requires a runtime implementation that is not provided for the target.

288.name: BML_GENERIC_BLOCK_NAME_COLLISION
288.documentation:
Emitted when a genericTypes parameter name equals the declaring Block's name. Remedy: On
the same declaring Block, generic parameter names must not collide with the Block name or
a direct Sub-Block name.
Emitted when a genericTypes parameter name equals the declaring Block's name.

289.name: BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION
289.documentation:
Emitted when a type argument or defaultType fails the parameter's baseType via
satisfiesTypeBound — including arguments authored in a type application and in instance
bml:generics. Remedy: Union arguments must satisfy the bound per alternative.
Emitted when a type argument or defaultType fails the parameter's baseType via satisfiesTypeBound.

290.name: BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_CYCLE
290.documentation:
Emitted when defaultType bindings form a cycle. Remedy: Declaration-order sibling defaults
already prevent most cycles; this is defense in depth.
Emitted when defaultType bindings form a cycle.

291.name: BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_FORWARD_REF
291.documentation:
Emitted when defaultType names a later or unknown sibling generic parameter. Remedy: Sibling-parameter
defaults may reference only earlier parameters (declaration-order DAG).
Emitted when defaultType names a later or unknown sibling generic parameter.

292.name: BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_UNRESOLVED
292.documentation:
Emitted when a defaultType chain does not ground to a concrete TypeExpression. Remedy: Every
unbound parameter at a reference site must resolve via authored args or defaults.
Emitted when a defaultType chain does not ground to a concrete TypeExpression.

293.name: BML_GENERIC_SUBBLOCK_NAME_COLLISION
293.documentation:
Emitted when a genericTypes parameter name equals a direct Sub-Block local name on the same
Block. Remedy: Rename the generic parameter or the Sub-Block so nested unqualified resolution
remains unambiguous.
Emitted when a genericTypes parameter name equals a direct Sub-Block local name on the same Block.

294.name: BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH
294.documentation:
Emitted when bml:generics is present on a Block instance but the argument list is not compatible
with that instance's open genericTypes: the type has no open parameters, the argument count
does not match (including extra arguments), or the value is not a parenthesized list in the
same form as a baseType generic application. Remedy: Supply a parenthesized TypeExpression list
in declaration order that binds the open parameters, or omit the directive when none are open.
Argument values that fail the parameter baseType → BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION. A
required argument omitted with no defaultType → BML_MISSING_GENERIC_TYPE_ARGUMENT.
Ill-formed TypeExpression syntax → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE.
Emitted when bml:generics does not match the instance's open genericTypes.

295.name: BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED
295.documentation:
Emitted when bml:generics appears where it is not permitted. The directive is legal only on
Block instances (composition children and instance aggregation fill), as attribute
bml:generics="(…)" or child <bml:generics>(…)</bml:generics>. It is not allowed on
Block definitions, composition wrappers, bml:container, or member declarations. Remedy: Move
the directive onto the instance whose open genericTypes it binds, or remove it.
Emitted when bml:generics is authored anywhere other than a Block instance.

296.name: BML_IDENTITY_TYPE_CHILD_ELEMENT
296.documentation:
Emitted when type/baseType identity fields are authored as illegal child shapes. Remedy:
Author type/baseType as TypeReference text (element or attribute) per MemberDefinition placement.
Emitted when type/baseType identity fields are authored as illegal child shapes.

297.name: BML_IMPLEMENTATION_UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE
297.documentation:
Emitted when implementation language= does not resolve to org.blockml.bml.language.*. Remedy:
Use a Language FQN or unqualified name at the language attribute site.
Emitted when implementation language= does not resolve to org.blockml.bml.language.*.

298.name: BML_INVALID_BLOCK_NAME
298.documentation:
Emitted when <name> is not PascalCase letters-and-digits ([A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*). Remedy:
PascalCase keeps composition tags with xmlns prefixes unambiguous — member names use camelCase.
Emitted when <name> is not PascalCase letters-and-digits ([A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*).

299.name: BML_INVALID_DEFINITION_BRANCH
299.documentation:
Emitted when a definition meta-model type is used outside the Definition branch expectations.
Remedy: Use Root/Sub/Embedded/Member definition types appropriately.
Emitted when a definition meta-model type is used outside the Definition branch expectations.

300.name: BML_INVALID_EMBEDDED_EXPRESSION
300.documentation:
Emitted when an <$ $> region contains invalid BlockML Expression content. Remedy: Use
#this.capa(...), #built-ins, @bean calls, and the shared expression grammar inside embeds.
Emitted when an <$ $> region contains invalid BlockML Expression content.

301.name: BML_INVALID_NAMESPACE_TARGET
301.documentation:
Emitted when xmlns targets neither a Package nor an Annotation. Remedy: Bind prefixes to
package FQNs or Annotation FQNs only.
Emitted when xmlns targets neither a Package nor an Annotation.

302.name: BML_INVALID_PROPERTY
302.documentation:
Emitted when a property declaration or instance value is structurally invalid. Remedy: Check
property type, value placement, and facets.
Emitted when a property declaration or instance value is structurally invalid.

303.name: BML_INVALID_PROPERTY_TYPE
303.documentation:
Bare type sites (Property type, Capability inputType/outputType) require ValueTypes. Aggregation type may be any Block FQN. Association type must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[].
Emitted when a Property or Capability payload type does not resolve to a ValueType branch.

304.name: BML_INVALID_SINCE_VERSION
304.documentation:
Emitted when since is not a valid Version value. Remedy: Use org.blockml.bml.type.Version
format.
Emitted when since is not a valid Version value.

305.name: BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE
305.documentation:
Emitted when a TypeIdentifier, TypeReference, or TypeExpression cannot be parsed or is
ill-formed — including an ill-formed bml:generics value and ill-formed MemberIdentifier /
InstanceIdentifier path or id syntax. This is the syntax check shared by Identifier and
Reference, keyed off the declared ValueType of the field (not the field name). Fields
typed Identifier (and not a Reference subtype) stop here — an unknown but well-formed
name is valid. Fields typed Reference continue to existence checks (BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE,
BML_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY, BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF). Remedy: Fix
FQN/QName/generic/configuration/path syntax. Instance bml:generics requires a
parenthesized argument list in the same form as a TypeReference application.
Emitted when a TypeIdentifier, TypeReference, or TypeExpression cannot be parsed or is
ill-formed.

306.name: BML_INVALID_VALUE
306.documentation:
Emitted when authored property text fails the lexical parse for the declared PrimitiveType.
The Capability throws exception:InvalidValueException; the validator reports this Diagnostic.
Remedy: fix the literal to match the type's parseValue contract (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

Not used for TypeReference existence (BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE), instance existence
(BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF), type-instance configuration, or Property constraints.
Emitted when a host evaluates PrimitiveType.parseValue and the body throws InvalidValueException.

307.name: BML_LEGACY_TYPE_SOURCE
307.documentation:
Emitted when a type still comes from a legacy XSD/YAML source during migration. Remedy: Migrate
to BML TypeRegistry definitions.
Emitted when a type still comes from a legacy XSD/YAML source during migration.

308.name: BML_LIBRARY_NESTING_VIOLATION
308.documentation:
Typical pattern: inner lists outer in dependencies; outer lists inner in subLibraries. Membership is defined by Library.blocks.
Emitted when outer library blocks reference a Block exported only by an inner nested library incorrectly.

309.name: BML_MISSING_AGGREGATION_TYPE
309.documentation:
Emitted when a new aggregation declaration omits required type. Remedy: Provide type on new
aggregations; inherited overrides may omit unchanged type.
Emitted when a new aggregation declaration omits required type.

310.name: BML_MISSING_BASE_TYPE
310.documentation:
Emitted when a Block other than org.blockml.bml.core.Block omits baseType. Remedy: Single
inheritance is mandatory except on the sole root org.blockml.bml.core.Block.
Emitted when a Block other than org.blockml.bml.core.Block omits baseType.

311.name: BML_MISSING_BLOCK_TYPE
311.documentation:
On root blocks, type is the canonical identity. Preferred authoring: the document root tag
is the type. Legacy: child <type> under a <block> root (doc:DocumentFormat).
name is optional and must match lastSegment(resolve(type)) when present.
Emitted when the document-root Block supplies neither a type root tag nor a
type element.

312.name: BML_MISSING_CONSTANT_VALUE
312.documentation:
Emitted when Constant(T) omits required {value: …} configuration. Remedy: Write Constant(T){value:
…}.
Emitted when Constant(T) omits required {value: …} configuration.

313.name: BML_MISSING_DOCUMENTATION
313.documentation:
Emitted when a Block definition omits required default-namespace documentation. Remedy: Every
Block definition (root and Sub-Blocks) requires ≥1 default-namespace documentation entry.
Emitted when a Block definition omits required default-namespace documentation.

314.name: BML_MISSING_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE
314.documentation:
Type is required and fully qualified. Preferred authoring: the element tag is the type,
same as the document root. Legacy: child <type> under a <block> wrapper
(doc:DocumentFormat). FQN = resolve(type), not nested under the root.
Emitted when an embedded Block supplies neither a type tag nor a type child.

315.name: BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_MAPPING
315.documentation:
Reserved: emitted when an implementation requires a non-default FunctionMapping but none
is declared. Until custom mappings ship, treat as reserved. Default FunctionMapping covers
V1 built-ins.
Reserved: emitted when an implementation requires a non-default FunctionMapping but none is declared.

316.name: BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_PARAMETER
316.documentation:
Emitted when a required inputType field is absent after FunctionMapping. Remedy: Supply the
missing positional or named argument, or an object literal with all required fields.
Emitted when a required inputType field is absent after FunctionMapping.

317.name: BML_MISSING_GENERIC_TYPE_ARGUMENT
317.documentation:
Emitted when a generic application or instance bml:generics omits a required type argument with
no resolvable defaultType. Remedy: Supply the argument or declare defaultType. An entire missing
bml:generics on an open-generic instance is BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE, not this code.
Emitted when a generic application or bml:generics omits a required type argument with no resolvable defaultType.

318.name: BML_MISSING_ID
318.documentation:
Emitted when bml:id is required (referenced instance or bml:each) but absent. Remedy: Add
bml:id (literal or expression).
Emitted when bml:id is required (referenced instance or bml:each) but absent.

319.name: BML_MISSING_IMPLEMENTATION_LANGUAGE
319.documentation:
Emitted when <implementation> omits required language. Remedy: Set language to an org.blockml.bml.language.*
FQN.
Emitted when <implementation> omits required language.

320.name: BML_MISSING_IS
320.documentation:
Emitted when a Block definition omits the required is Urbild designation. Remedy: is is always
required after identity fields — a clear noun phrase for what the Block semantically represents.
Emitted when a Block definition omits the required is Urbild designation.

321.name: BML_MISSING_IS_NOT
321.documentation:
Warning/required when confusion risk exists and isNot is omitted on a Block. isNot is block-level
negative space for disambiguation. Missing when required → this code.
Warning/required when confusion risk exists and isNot is omitted on a Block.

322.name: BML_MISSING_SUBBLOCK_NAME
322.documentation:
Name is required as local identity. Preferred authoring: the element local name under
<subBlocks> is the Sub-Block name. Legacy: child <name> under a <block>
wrapper (doc:DocumentFormat). Type is normally derived.
Emitted when a Sub-Block supplies neither a name element tag nor a name child.

323.name: BML_MISSING_SUMMARY
323.documentation:
Warning when documentation is too long for a quick scan and default-namespace summary is
omitted. summary sits between is and documentation for LLM/human orientation.
Warning when documentation is too long for a quick scan and default-namespace summary is omitted.

324.name: BML_MISSING_VERSION
324.documentation:
Emitted when a Block has no effective version (own version and library.version both absent
for an exported block). Remedy: Framework convention: version often only on Library.bml for
org.blockml.bml.* exports.
Emitted when a Block has no effective version (own version and library.version both absent for an exported block).

325.name: BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS
325.documentation:
Emitted when a Capability/function call mixes positional and named arguments under default
FunctionMapping. Remedy: Use positional-only, named-only, or a single object literal — not
mixed forms.
Emitted when a Capability/function call mixes positional and named arguments under default FunctionMapping.

326.name: BML_MIXED_TYPE_CONFIGURATION
326.documentation:
Emitted when named and positional ValueType instance configuration are mixed in one {...}
block. Remedy: Use either named key: value pairs or positional values by property declaration
order — not both.
Emitted when named and positional ValueType instance configuration are mixed in one {...} block.

327.name: BML_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_COLLISION
327.documentation:
Emitted when the same prefix maps to conflicting namespaces when merging bindings (e.g. FatBlock).
Remedy: Align xmlns prefixes across the bundle.
Emitted when the same prefix maps to conflicting namespaces when merging bindings (e.g. FatBlock).

328.name: BML_NAMESPACE_UNBOUND
328.documentation:
Emitted when emit/QName mode needs a prefix for a namespace missing from authored bindings.
Remedy: Declare xmlns for that namespace; do not invent prefixes at emit time.
Emitted when emit/QName mode needs a prefix for a namespace missing from authored bindings.

329.name: BML_NATIVE_BLOCK_CUSTOM_PROPERTY
329.documentation:
Domain/policy: unexpected custom property on NativeBlock chain. Prefer declared NativeBlock
properties; domain-specific.
Domain/policy: unexpected custom property on NativeBlock chain.

330.name: BML_NESTED_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS
330.documentation:
Emitted when an embedded Block itself declares embeddedBlocks. Remedy: Compose artifacts
by listing virtual files flat at the root. Bundlers flatten when merging packages.
Emitted when an embedded Block itself declares embeddedBlocks.

331.name: BML_NO_TARGET
331.documentation:
Emitted when compilation is requested with no configured render target. Remedy: Configure
targets[] in bom.config / CLI.
Emitted when compilation is requested with no configured render target.

332.name: BML_NON_STATIC_INSTANCE_REF
332.documentation:
Emitted when a qualified instance reference requires a static literal bml:id but got a dynamic
id. Remedy: Use a literal static bml:id for cross-document {FQN}::{id} references.
Emitted when a qualified instance reference requires a static literal bml:id but got a dynamic id.

333.name: BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE
333.documentation:
Emitted when a Block instance whose type still has open genericTypes after inheritance is used
as an aggregation child (composition or instance fill) without bml:generics binding those
parameters. Remedy: Author bml:generics="(…)" or
<bml:generics>(…)</bml:generics> with a parenthesized TypeExpression list, or bind
the parameters on a derived type via baseType application. Parameters with resolvable
defaultType are not open. Abstract Blocks remain uninstantiable even with bml:generics.
Emitted when a Block instance whose type still has open genericTypes is aggregated without bml:generics.

334.name: BML_OUTSIDE_BML_NAMESPACE
334.documentation:
Emitted when a BML definition FQN does not reside under the domain's bml package (domain.bml.*).
Remedy: Every BlockML definition must live under <domain>.bml.* — e.g. org.blockml.bml.*,
com.machineblocks.bml.*.
Emitted when a BML definition FQN does not reside under the domain's bml package (domain.bml.*).

335.name: BML_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED
335.documentation:
Every redeclaration layer that merges with an inherited or contract member must set override="true" again — including contract completion. Override is not inherited.
Emitted when a local member redeclaration merges with a baseType or contracts member without override="true".

336.name: BML_OVERRIDE_WITHOUT_PARENT
336.documentation:
A genuinely new member must not set override="true". Check namespace + normalizedLogicalName identity and contract merge order.
Emitted when override="true" is set but no matching parent member exists in the baseType chain or contracts[].

337.name: BML_PREFER_CONSTANT_TYPE
337.documentation:
Warning: prefer Constant(T){value: …} over obsolete wrapper/literal union forms. Migrate
AutoOr/FalseOr/NoneOr and bare literal unions to Constant form.
Warning: prefer Constant(T){value: …} over obsolete wrapper/literal union forms.

338.name: BML_PREFER_TYPE_CONFIGURATION
338.documentation:
Warning: prefer ValueType {...} configuration over equivalent Constraints for type-intrinsic
thresholds. E.g. Text{maxLength: 100} instead of MaxLength constraint when intrinsic.
Warning: prefer ValueType {...} configuration over equivalent Constraints for type-intrinsic thresholds.

339.name: BML_PRESET_CYCLE
339.documentation:
Domain: preset references form a cycle. Break the preset dependency cycle in domain presets.
This diagnostic is emitted by domain validators; Core only catalogues the code.
Domain: preset references form a cycle.

340.name: BML_PRIVATE_MEMBER_ACCESS
340.documentation:
Private members (__name) are usable only within the declaring Block's definition — including instances of the declaring type in that same definition. Composition ownership does not lift private encapsulation of contained Sub-Block instances.
Emitted when a private member is read or set outside the Block definition that declares it.

341.name: BML_PRIVATE_SUBBLOCK_ACCESS
341.documentation:
Emitted when a private Sub-Block is referenced outside the immediately declaring Block definition.
Remedy: Private Sub-Blocks (__Name) follow the same access model as private members — declaring
Block only.
Emitted when a private Sub-Block is referenced outside the immediately declaring Block definition.

342.name: BML_PROPERTY_CYCLE
342.documentation:
Emitted when <value> expressions form a cyclic dependency among Properties. Remedy:
value expressions may reference own Block Properties and #built-ins only; resolve via topological
sort.
Emitted when <value> expressions form a cyclic dependency among Properties.

343.name: BML_PROTECTED_MEMBER_ACCESS
343.documentation:
Protected members (_name) allow access when C=D, C inherits from D, C is the immediate composition owner O, or C inherits from instance type I. Outer composition ancestors do not receive protected configuration access.
Emitted when a protected member is used outside declaring Block, inheritance, or immediate composition-owner context.

344.name: BML_PROTECTED_SUBBLOCK_ACCESS
344.documentation:
