Protected Sub-Blocks (_Name) are visible inside the enclosing Block definition and derived Blocks — not from arbitrary external documents.
Emitted when a protected Sub-Block is referenced outside the enclosing definition and its derived Blocks.

345.name: BML_READONLY_MEMBER_WRITE
345.documentation:
Definition authoring and child definition overrides may set readOnly member values/composition; instances must not. Expressions may still read subject to visibility.
Emitted when a Block instance sets a member whose effective definition has readOnly=true.

346.name: BML_REDUNDANT_AGGREGATION_TYPE
346.documentation:
Omit unchanged type on aggregation overrides. Declare type only when refining or replacing the inherited type. Authored redundant type is ignored.
Warning (V1): restating an identical type on an inherited aggregation override that only fills composition/metadata.

347.name: BML_REDUNDANT_STATUS
347.documentation:
Warning: explicit status duplicates the effective/default status unnecessarily. Omit redundant
status unless documenting intent.
Warning: explicit status duplicates the effective/default status unnecessarily.

348.name: BML_REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS_TARGET
348.documentation:
Emitted when a documentation <see> target is ambiguous. Remedy: Use exactly one target
kind or a disambiguating split form.
Emitted when a documentation <see> target is ambiguous.

349.name: BML_REFERENCE_MISSING_TARGET
349.documentation:
Emitted when a <see> entry has no target attribute. Remedy: Provide type, instance,
file, url, or member path target.
Emitted when a <see> entry has no target attribute.

350.name: BML_REFERENCE_UNKNOWN_MEMBER
350.documentation:
Emitted when a see member path (property/aggregation/…) cannot be resolved. Remedy: Fix the
canonical member path or owning type.
Emitted when a see member path (property/aggregation/…) cannot be resolved.

351.name: BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION
351.documentation:
<composition> must always be nested inside an aggregation member on Block definitions. On instances, open aggregations directly without a composition wrapper. Do not use <value> as a parallel wrapper on instance Properties — both are definition fields (doc:MemberAuthoring).
Emitted when <composition> appears outside an aggregation member element.

352.name: BML_SUBBLOCK_QUALIFIED_REFERENCE_REQUIRED
352.documentation:
Emitted when a Sub-Block shares the root Block name and a bare short tag is ambiguous. Remedy:
Prefer distinctive Sub-Block names. If names collide with the root, use Root.SubBlock / FQN
forms.
Emitted when a Sub-Block shares the root Block name and a bare short tag is ambiguous.

353.name: BML_SUBBLOCK_TYPE_MISMATCH
353.documentation:
Emitted when an explicit Sub-Block type does not equal resolve(parent.type) + "."
+ name. Remedy: The validator checks the full expected type from the immediate enclosing
block — not the last segment alone.
Emitted when an explicit Sub-Block type does not equal resolve(parent.type) + "." + name.

354.name: BML_SUGGESTION_TYPE_MISMATCH
354.documentation:
Emitted when a suggestion instance is incompatible with the property type. Remedy: Use compatible
ValueType/Entity instances; primitives need matching *Entity wrappers.
Emitted when a suggestion instance is incompatible with the property type.

355.name: BML_SUGGESTIONS_ON_ENUM
355.documentation:
Emitted when <suggestions> appears on an EnumType-typed property. Remedy: Enum values
come from the EnumType values aggregation — remove suggestions.
Emitted when <suggestions> appears on an EnumType-typed property.

356.name: BML_TOO_MANY_FUNCTION_PARAMETERS
356.documentation:
Emitted when a call supplies more positional arguments than the inputType arity allows. Remedy:
Trim excess arguments or adjust inputType / FunctionMapping.
Emitted when a call supplies more positional arguments than the inputType arity allows.

357.name: BML_TYPE_BOUND_NOT_SATISFIED
357.documentation:
Emitted when satisfiesTypeBound(T, G) fails for a generic/contract bound. Remedy: Ensure
T extends G via baseType chain or lists G in contracts[].
Emitted when satisfiesTypeBound(T, G) fails for a generic/contract bound.

358.name: BML_TYPE_CONFIGURATION_VIOLATION
358.documentation:
Emitted when a {...} configuration value does not satisfy the configuration Property's type.
Remedy: Configured instances are checked against the configured type — not bare ValueType
defaults.
Emitted when a {...} configuration value does not satisfy the configuration Property's type.

359.name: BML_TYPE_REFERENCE_CHILD_VALUE
359.documentation:
Emitted when TypeReferenceEntity sugar/children violate value authoring rules. Remedy: Empty
QName children expand to value=; do not mix illegal child shapes.
Emitted when TypeReferenceEntity sugar/children violate value authoring rules.

360.name: BML_TYPE_REFERENCE_CONSTRAINT
360.documentation:
Emitted when a TypeReference(B), PropertyReference(B) (or Aggregation / Association /
Capability Reference), or InstanceReference(T) bound is not satisfied by the resolved target.
Identifier sites have no branch bound and never emit this diagnostic. Remedy: Referenced type
or instance must satisfy the branch bound B / T (and the owning-Block bound B on member
References).
Emitted when a TypeReference(B) or InstanceReference(T) bound is not satisfied by the referenced type.

361.name: BML_TYPE_REFERENCE_MULTIPLICITY
361.documentation:
Emitted when multiplicity is applied illegally to a TypeReference site that forbids it. Remedy:
Check the site's type attribute rules — some TypeReference usages are singular only.
Emitted when multiplicity is applied illegally to a TypeReference site that forbids it.

362.name: BML_UNCLOSED_EMBEDDED_EXPRESSION
362.documentation:
Emitted when an implementation body has <$ without a matching $>. Remedy: Every opening
<$ must close with $>. Nested embeds are forbidden.
Emitted when an implementation body has <$ without a matching $>.

363.name: BML_UNEXPORTED_INSTANCE_REF
363.documentation:
Emitted when an instance id is referenced outside the aggregation visibility export rules.
Remedy: Use a public aggregation for cross-document ids, or reference from an allowed scope.
Emitted when an instance id is referenced outside the aggregation visibility export rules.

364.name: BML_UNKNOWN_BEAN
364.documentation:
Emitted when a bean name cannot be resolved (alias of expression bean errors in some pipelines).
Remedy: Declare bml:bean on the instance; prefer BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_BEAN for expression sites.
Emitted when a bean name cannot be resolved (alias of expression bean errors in some pipelines).

365.name: BML_UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY
365.documentation:
Emitted when a Capability reference cannot be resolved on the target Block. Remedy: Check
Capability name and inheritance/contract merge.
Emitted when a Capability reference cannot be resolved on the target Block.

366.name: BML_UNKNOWN_CONTRACT
366.documentation:
Emitted when a <contracts> entry does not resolve to a BlockDefinition. Remedy: Export
the contract Block and fix the FQN/QName.
Emitted when a <contracts> entry does not resolve to a BlockDefinition.

367.name: BML_UNKNOWN_DIRECTIVE
367.documentation:
Emitted when an unknown bml: directive name is used. Remedy: Use directives declared on org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation.
Emitted when an unknown bml: directive name is used.

368.name: BML_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION_PARAMETER
368.documentation:
Emitted when a named call argument is not a field of the Capability inputType. Remedy: Named
keys must match StructType / anonymous struct field names.
Emitted when a named call argument is not a field of the Capability inputType.

369.name: BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX
369.documentation:
Declare xmlns:prefix for Packages (type addressing) or Annotations (directives/facets). Prefixes are authoring aliases — BOM stores canonical FQNs/namespaces.
Emitted when a QName uses an xmlns prefix that is not declared on the document.

370.name: BML_UNKNOWN_NATURAL_LANGUAGE
370.documentation:
Emitted when a NaturalLanguage reference does not resolve. Remedy: Use org.blockml.bml.language.*
NaturalLanguage blocks (English, German, …).
Emitted when a NaturalLanguage reference does not resolve.

371.name: BML_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY
371.documentation:
The validator keys off the declared ValueType of the field, not the field name. Emitted when
a value whose type is PropertyReference (or AggregationReference / AssociationReference /
CapabilityReference) cannot be resolved
on the Block (non-expression). PropertyIdentifier and MemberIdentifier (and not a Reference
subtype) are syntax-only — an unknown but well-formed path is valid. Unresolved is an error,
not proof the document is ill-formed — the member may be missing from a not-yet-loaded
library. Remedy: Check member name, namespace, effective members after merge, and whether
the owning type's library is on the current classpath.
Emitted when a property name cannot be resolved on the Block (non-expression site).

372.name: BML_UNKNOWN_RELATION
372.documentation:
Emitted when see relation= does not resolve to org.blockml.bml.relation.*. Remedy: Use standard
Relation blocks (SeeAlso, ReadFirst, …).
Emitted when see relation= does not resolve to org.blockml.bml.relation.*.

373.name: BML_UNKNOWN_SERVICE
373.documentation:
Emitted when a #service builtin namespace is unknown. Remedy: Use registered services (#math,
#strings, #lists, #numbers, #bools).
Emitted when a #service builtin namespace is unknown.

374.name: BML_UNKNOWN_STATUS
374.documentation:
Emitted when status does not resolve to org.blockml.bml.status.*. Remedy: Use Draft, Stable,
Deprecated, Stub (or library Status blocks).
Emitted when status does not resolve to org.blockml.bml.status.*.

375.name: BML_UNKNOWN_TARGET
375.documentation:
Emitted when a configured render target name is not registered. Remedy: Register the target
package or fix targets[] configuration.
Emitted when a configured render target name is not registered.

376.name: BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE
376.documentation:
The validator keys off the declared ValueType of the field — not the property or attribute
name and not the XML site. Whether the field is authored as type=, baseType=, abc=, or any
other name is irrelevant. If the field's type is TypeReference or TypeReferenceEntity (or a
subtype), the authored name is expanded to a canonical FQN and looked up in TypeRegistry.
Failure to resolve emits this diagnostic.

If the field's type is TypeIdentifier (or a TypeIdentifier that is not a TypeReference),
existence is not checked — an unknown but well-formed FQN is valid. Ill-formed syntax on
either Identifier or Reference → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE. Unresolved PropertyReference /
AggregationReference / … → BML_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY (or this diagnostic when the owning type
cannot be resolved).
Unresolved InstanceReference → BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF.

This diagnostic is an error, but it does not mean the document is ill-formed or semantically
wrong. It is the same class of finding as Java "cannot find symbol" / class not found: the
name may be a typo, or a library may simply not be on the current classpath (for example a
Maven package not included). Which of those it is remains a question of interpretation.

Common causes: typo in FQN or xmlns prefix, missing Library blocks entry, unloaded dependency
library, or reference to a Sub-Block type without the full parent-qualified path where required.
Emitted when a value whose declared type is TypeReference (or TypeReferenceEntity)
cannot be resolved in the current TypeRegistry — including a missing dependency library.

377.name: BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE_CONFIGURATION
377.documentation:
Emitted when {...} instance configuration names a property that is not on the ValueType.
Remedy: Configuration keys must match effective Properties of the referenced ValueType.
Emitted when {...} instance configuration names a property that is not on the ValueType.

378.name: BML_UNKNOWN_VERSION
378.documentation:
Omitted bml:version resolves from TypeRegistry / library context. Present value is an exact-version assert — no match fails validation.
Emitted when bml:version pins a type/library reference to a version that is not available.

379.name: BML_UNQUALIFIED_BLOCK_REFERENCE
379.documentation:
Emitted when a composition/type site uses an unqualified Block name outside Sub-Block parent
context or a specialized implicit-namespace site. Remedy: Inside the declaring root's composition,
Sub-Blocks may use local names. Elsewhere require FQN / xmlns-qualified names.
Emitted when a composition/type site uses an unqualified Block name outside Sub-Block parent context or a specialized implicit-namespace site.

380.name: BML_UNQUALIFIED_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE
380.documentation:
Embedded type must be an FQN (or resolvable QName to a full FQN). Unqualified / relative Sub-Block forms are invalid for embeds.
Emitted when an embedded Block type is not fully qualified.

381.name: BML_UNREACHABLE_UNION_ALTERNATIVE
381.documentation:
Warning: a later union alternative cannot win under left-to-right first-hit matching. Prefer
narrower/sentinel alternatives on the left. Advisory like unreachable code — compile succeeds.
Warning: a later union alternative cannot win under left-to-right first-hit matching.

382.name: BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF
382.documentation:
The validator keys off the declared ValueType of the field, not the field name. Emitted when
a value whose type is InstanceReference cannot be resolved to an instance id in scope.
InstanceIdentifier (and not InstanceReference) is syntax-only — an unknown but well-formed
id is valid. Unresolved is an error, not proof the document is ill-formed — the instance
may live in a document or library that is not currently loaded. Remedy: Fix bml:id,
aggregation visibility, the reference path, or the load set.
Emitted when an InstanceReference cannot be resolved to an instance id in scope.

383.name: BML_VALIDATION_UNKNOWN
383.documentation:
Emitted when constraint validation= does not resolve to a Validation block. Remedy: Use Error,
Warning, or Information.
Emitted when constraint validation= does not resolve to a Validation block.

384.name: BML_VERSION_BELOW_LIBRARY
384.documentation:
Emitted when a Block version is below its exporting library.version policy. Remedy: Raise
the Block version or align with library versioning conventions.
Emitted when a Block version is below its exporting library.version policy.

385.name: BML_VERSION_MINOR_DRIFT
385.documentation:
Warning: Block version drifts from library.version in a minor/patch policy sense. Align versions
per library convention (framework often versions only Library.bml).
Warning: Block version drifts from library.version in a minor/patch policy sense.

386.name: BML_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH
386.documentation:
Optional visibility on members and Sub-Blocks must agree with public / _protected / __private naming. When omitted, visibility is derived from the name.
Emitted when an explicit visibility property does not match the naming-convention prefix on the name.

387.name: BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING
387.documentation:
Override matching uses normalizedLogicalName. Widening (protected → public) is allowed; narrowing is forbidden. Private members cannot be overridden at all.
Emitted when an override reduces visibility (e.g. public → protected, or protected → private).

388.name: BML_VISIBILITY_ON_ROOT_BLOCK
388.documentation:
Root Blocks must not declare <visibility>. Sub-Blocks inside <subBlocks> may declare optional visibility matching their name prefix.
Emitted when a document-root Block declares root-level visibility — only Sub-Blocks may do so.

389.name: BML_XML_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED
389.documentation:
Block-level <bml:xml> is for core:Block and Definition-branch types. Member bml:xml belongs on Definition-branch member declarations. Hybrid Stage 1/2 checks apply.
Emitted when bml:xml is authored where the grammar/branch does not allow it (e.g. block-level on ordinary ValueType).

390.name: BML_XML_RENDERING_INVALID
390.documentation:
In this context ${ … } forms are fixed tag recipes, not open Expression Language. Other roots, calls, or operators are invalid.
Emitted when a <bml:xml> body is not a literal local name, ${ bml:Self }, or ${ #this.name }.

391.name: AnnotationModel
391.documentation:
Annotations formalize directive namespaces. They are orthogonal to the Definition meta-model
(org.blockml.bml.definition.*) — they do not describe block structure, members, or constraints.
Naming overlap (Property, Aggregation, …) classifies directive form only;
Annotation.Property is not def:PropertyDefinition.

Every BML-semantic xmlns prefix resolves to either a Package (type addressing) or a concrete
Annotation (directives). preferredAlias is authoring convention only (bml, scad) — the BOM
stores the Annotation FQN, never the XML prefix. Document default xmlns remains
http://blockml.org/bml. xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — XSD is
not an officially supported standard feature (doc:DocumentFormat). Legacy schema URIs are
obsolete. BML-semantic xmlns:bml must target ann:BmlAnnotation — never a schema URL.

Branch shape (core:Annotation):
• preferredAlias : Text
• directives : Directive[]
• Directive — name = local name
  · Member (name="*") → Property | Aggregation | Association | Capability
  · Element → Document | Summary | Examples | Example | Value (fixed names)
  · Attribute — fixed names (id, each, with, …)

Concrete annotations:
• org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation (bml) — language directives; see doc:BmlDirectives
• Domain annotations (e.g. com.machineblocks.bml.annotation.ScadAnnotation, scad) — members,
  value facets, prose facets, example facets

Directive match:
• Attribute / Element (incl. fixed Document, Summary, Examples, Example, Value) —
  localName == directive.name
• Member subtypes — name="*"; any local name under the annotation; kind from the Member subtype

Parent context for *:value:
• Direct child of <properties> → Member (Annotation.Property) when declared
• Nested under a property element → Value facet (Annotation.Value) — same property identity,
  not member scad:myProp
Never means a renamed member QName.

Parent context for *:example:
• Prefixed child of <examples> → Annotation.Example (sibling of canonical <example>)
• Unprefixed <example> → StructuralDefinition.Example
Prefer sibling *:example for 1:1 BML↔target pairs; use *:examples for independent target-only
sets. Annotation facets never replace required canonical documentation / value / examples slots.

Property value facets multiply PropertyDefinition.value along the Annotation namespace axis
("" | Annotation FQN). Cross-namespace faceting is valid; same-namespace self-faceting is
forbidden. Duplicate namespace on one property → BML_DUPLICATE_PROPERTY_VALUE. Facets do not
satisfy or replace the canonical <value> for BML instance semantics unless a renderer
explicitly prefers an Annotation facet.
391.idea: A guide to Annotation namespaces and facets

392.name: BlockAndInstance
392.documentation:
The closest familiar model: a Block is a declarative semantic Class; a Block Instance is an
Object. This is a semantic analogy — not a mandate for runtime OOP. The compiler may represent
definitions and instances as plain data; the parser nonetheless distinguishes block documents
(classes) from composition children (objects).

Block (definition):
• .bml file · BlockDefinition
• Element tag is the type (root / embed) or the name (Sub-Block); legacy
  <block> wrappers remain valid (doc:DocumentFormat)
• FQN · members · composition schema
• Describes shape and behaviour
• No runtime · no address

Block Instance (in composition):
• Element such as ac:Wall with bml:id and member values
• typeFqn + bml:id + member values
• One concrete occurrence
• May become a Thing in Runtime (WOT vocabulary)

Composition:
• Aggregations hold Block Instances as children
• Instance identity uses bml:id (not the type FQN)
• Nested paths compose with :: (wall::bottom::inner)
• bml:version pins external references to exact library versions

Instance serialization (authoring) — definition fields are not instance wrappers:
• On Block definitions — Property default uses the value field (<value> preferred);
  Aggregation default uses <composition> nested inside the aggregation member
• On Block instances — NEVER wrap a Property in <value> and NEVER wrap Aggregation
  children in <composition>. The Property is a Block attribute or the Property element's
  direct content (myProperty="…" or <myProperty>…</myProperty>). Aggregation children
  sit directly inside the aggregation element (or bml:container for shared directives)
• Exception: a member whose name is value (PrimitiveEntity, TypeReferenceEntity, …) uses
  value="…" as ordinary instance syntax for that member — not as a PropertyDefinition wrapper
• readOnly effective members must not be authored on instances → BML_READONLY_MEMBER_WRITE
• Empty child meaning depends on aggregation type (instance vs TypeReferenceEntity sugar) —
  doc:MemberAuthoring / doc:CompositionModel / doc:SubBlockModel

Context-dependent interpretation:
• ValueTypes as type-classes for Property values and Capability input/output
• Languages as meta-classes for implementation contracts
• Sub-Blocks in the same .bml file as nested classes (derived types, inner scope)
• Presets as named default bindings on a class

Relationships: Library contains Blocks; Block has Members, Presets, Compositions; Catalog
contains top-level composite Blocks.
392.idea: A guide to Block vs instance

393.name: BlockNameConvention
393.documentation:
<name> is a class name — PascalCase, letters and digits only:

Format: [A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*
Valid: Wall, StandardBrick, Calibrator, NfcPlayer
Invalid: my-wall, wall_v2, 2Wall, My Wall
Error: BML_INVALID_BLOCK_NAME

PascalCase ensures composition instance tags with xmlns prefixes are unambiguous — no Property
or member name starts with an uppercase letter (members use camelCase; visibility prefixes _ /
__ do not change that rule for the logical name).

Relationship to type identity (doc:TypeIdentityDerivation / doc:DocumentFormat):
• Root Blocks — type is canonical (root tag preferred, or child <type>); name is
  optional and must equal lastSegment(resolve(type)) when present
  (BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH). On an unqualified type root, a redundant <name>
  is not recommended
• Sub-Blocks — name is required local identity, supplied by the element tag
  (<MyBlock> under <subBlocks>) or legacy child <name>; type is
  normally derived as parentType + "." + name (doc:DocumentFormat)
• Visibility prefixes on Sub-Block names (_Utils, __Helper) are allowed; the PascalCase rule
  applies to the logical name after stripping visibility prefixes for collision checks — authored
  names still follow the visibility naming convention (doc:MemberVisibility /
  doc:SubBlockModel)

Prefer distinctive Sub-Block names that differ from the enclosing root Block name to avoid
ambiguous short tags (doc:SubBlockModel — naming vs parent).
393.idea: A guide to Block name formatting

394.name: BmlDirectives
394.documentation:
BML Directives are attributes and elements in the bml: namespace, formalized by
org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation (preferredAlias bml). Bind with
xmlns:bml="org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation". Directives are not Block properties and not
Definition members. Flow-control directives structure composition; serialization directives
(bml:xml) declare how Definition blocks map to canonical BML XML.

Flow-control follows the Thymeleaf model — attributes on the element they apply to. Whether a
directive is pre-processed at compile time or translated into target constructs is the
BlockProcessor's decision.

Placement:
• bml:id — Block instances; composition identity (literal or ${ expr }); required when
  referenced or on bml:each
• bml:version — Block instances; external type version pin
• bml:bean — Block instances; service bean name for @bean expressions
• bml:scope — Block instances; bean visibility "local" (default) or "context"
• bml:generics — Block instances only; binds open genericTypes. Value is the parenthesized
  argument list from a baseType generic application (parentheses required). Attribute
  bml:generics="(type:Integer)" or child
  <bml:generics>(type:String, myns:MyBlock)</bml:generics>. Open generic
  aggregated without it → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE. Elsewhere →
  BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED. Incompatible args → BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH
• bml:with — composition, bml:container, Block instances; local variable scope
• bml:each — bml:container, Block instances; loop
• bml:if / bml:unless — bml:container, Block instances; conditional include / exclude
• <bml:xml>…</bml:xml> — core:Block and Definition-branch blocks; root XML element recipe
• bml:xml="…" on members — Definition-branch member serialization shape
Bare id= / version= on instances are ordinary member values — use bml:id / bml:version for
composition meta. Do not bind xmlns:bml to a Package or use bml: as a member Annotation prefix.

bml:each — expands the element once per iteration (numeric or collection). Forms:
i : ${ n } · i, stat : ${ n } · item, stat : ${ collection }. Stat fields: index, count, size,
first, last, even, odd (0-based index/even/odd). For numeric loops i equals stat.index.

bml:if / bml:unless — include when expression is true / false respectively.

bml:container — virtual element; produces no Block output; groups children for shared directives
(each, if, with).

bml:with — defines local variables on the element and descendants. Comma-separated assignments;
evaluated left-to-right; later variables may reference earlier ones; shadows outer names of the
same name; may reference Properties of the current Block and override Properties within local
scope. Primary mechanism for sharing values between sibling composition children.

Dynamic instance IDs: combine bml:each with bml:id="${ 'prefix_' + i }" (or equivalent).

bml:generics — instance-only binding of open genericTypes (doc:GenericsModel). Same TypeExpression
grammar as the (…) of a baseType application; the type name is the instance tag, so only the
parenthesized list is authored. Parentheses are required. Not allowed on definitions,
composition wrappers, bml:container, or member declarations. Abstract Blocks remain uninstantiable
even with bml:generics.

bml:xml (serialization — orthogonal to flow control):
• Element form on core:Block / Definition branch: literal local name, ${ bml:Self }, or
  ${ #this.name } only — other recipes → BML_XML_RENDERING_INVALID
• Ordinary composable / ValueType blocks must not redeclare block-level <bml:xml> →
  BML_XML_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED (Stage 2)
• Member attribute form selects node kind (element | attribute | text | cdata, including
  element|attribute alternatives). May change on override="true"
Shared XML grammar metadata for serializer, FatBlock, the optional XSD compiler, and
similar targets — not a serializer-private detail. XSD is not a standard feature
(doc:DocumentFormat). Meta-driven emit is WIP; Definition blocks already declare shapes.

Catalogue of directive Sub-Blocks: ann:BmlAnnotation.Id, Version, Bean, Scope, Status, Generics,
Each, If, Unless, With, Xml, Container. Composition usage: doc:CompositionModel.
394.idea: A guide to BML language directives

395.name: BmlNamespace
395.documentation:
Every BML definition — Blocks, Libraries, Types, Languages, Services, Capabilities, and all
other BlockML definitions — must reside below the owning domain's bml package.

General form:
• <domain>.bml.*

Examples:
• org.blockml.bml.*
• com.machineblocks.bml.*
• com.example.bml.*

No BML Block, Library, or other BlockML definition may exist outside the domain's bml
namespace (BML_OUTSIDE_BML_NAMESPACE). Physical source layout mirrors the FQN:
blocks/org/blockml/bml/core/Block.bml defines org.blockml.bml.core.Block.

Typical BlockML branches (all under org.blockml.bml.*):
• org.blockml.bml.core.* — framework base types (Block, Annotation, ValueType, Status, Capability, Exception, Library, …)
• org.blockml.bml.annotation.* — concrete Annotations (BmlAnnotation)
• org.blockml.bml.type.* — bootstrap ValueTypes
• org.blockml.bml.service.* — built-in expression services (#math, #strings, …)
• org.blockml.bml.language.* — implementation language types
• org.blockml.bml.capability.* — Capability type branches
• org.blockml.bml.definition.* — Definition meta-model (orthogonal to Annotations)
• org.blockml.bml.documentation.* — bootstrap documentation blocks
• org.blockml.bml.status.* / constraint.* / validation.* / relation.* / unit.* — matching branches

xmlns prefixes are BML-semantic only when they target a Package or an Annotation:
• Package — type addressing (xmlns:core="org.blockml.bml.core")
• Annotation — directives (xmlns:bml="org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation")
Other URI bindings (schemaLocation keys) are not BML-semantic type namespaces.
xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — XSD is not a standard
feature (doc:DocumentFormat). Undeclared
prefix → BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX; non-Package/Annotation target →
BML_INVALID_NAMESPACE_TARGET; colliding prefixes across a bundle →
BML_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_COLLISION.

XML prefix convention (required authoring practice — BOM stores FQNs; compiler does not
rewrite aliases). Rule of thumb: a bare short prefix always means BlockML. Domain mirrors of
the same segment use a domain token in front (MachineBlocks → mb):
• core → org.blockml.bml.core · type → org.blockml.bml.type · unit → org.blockml.bml.unit
• lang → org.blockml.bml.language · status / def / constraint / validation / … → matching
  org.blockml.bml.*
• mbcore → com.machineblocks.bml.core · mbt → …type · mbunit → …unit
• bricks / cal / scad — collective or annotation packages (descriptive OK when no collision)
Do not steal framework aliases (xmlns:core="com.machineblocks.bml.core" is wrong). Do not use
legacy bcore / btype. Other domains use their own short token (ac → acore / atype / aunit).

Member and facet QNames: optional XML prefix on member element names supplies the member
namespace (resolved via xmlns; unprefixed → default empty namespace). Prefixed member QNames
that are Annotation Member directives (name="*") resolve to that Annotation — see
doc:AnnotationModel. There is no namespace= attribute on members.

Domain libraries follow the same <domain>.bml.* rule
(com.machineblocks.bml.core / bricks / type / annotation.*, …).

npm workspace packages (@blockml/core, @blockml/parser, …) are deployment units — not
identical to FQN namespaces. TypeScript toolchain code ships in package src/ directories;
it is not a BML definition and does not receive a domain.bml FQN.
395.idea: A guide to the BML namespace

396.name: BootstrapModel
396.documentation:
Self-hosting bootstrap: the compiler loads framework BML from @blockml/core (and domain
packages) before user content — TypeRegistry bootstrap, not special-cased type semantics
in code.

Bootstrap order (summary):
1. Core branches — Block, ValueType, Language, Status, Relation, Constraint, Capability, Definition
2. Concrete types — Integer, Decimal, languages, services, constraints, relations
3. BlockLibrary — library descriptor base (readMe, bootstrap, dependencies, subLibraries,
   schemas, blocks)
4. org.blockml.bml.Library — published catalog via blocks; readMe → README
5. Domain framework BML (e.g. com.machineblocks.bml.core.*)

Two library entry roles (do not conflate):
• org.blockml.bml.core.ReadMe — human/LLM reading entry. Required on every Library via
  readMe (exactly one TypeReferenceEntity(ReadMe)). org.blockml.bml.README is the standard
  core-library ReadMe.
• org.blockml.bml.core.Bootstrap — optional automation SPOE (tasks, agents, CI). At most one
  per Library via bootstrap (0..1). Empty abstract branch; concrete subtypes supply process logic.

Concrete Library.bml <references> — at most two <see> entries on the catalog
descriptor (not on documentation blocks):
1. Required relation=ReadFirst → the ReadMe named in readMe
2. Optional relation=ThenContinueWith → the Bootstrap named in bootstrap (only when present)
Signals: after reading, continue by executing the automation SPOE. No AuthoringGuide /
DeepDive / Extends / SeeAlso on concrete Libraries.

Curated reading order lives in <references> on the ReadMe block — each entry uses
relation=ReadFirst with a context note. Available tasks use relation=TaskIndex on the same
references container. One mechanism for all cross-links; tooling filters by relation. No
separate reading-order aggregation on ReadMe itself.

Task-oriented paths:
• org.blockml.bml.core.TaskGuide — procedural org.blockml.bml.task.* blocks
• relation=TaskStep — ordered steps inside a TaskGuide (document order)
• relation=Prerequisite — before starting a task
• org.blockml.bml.core.Diagnostic — org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* validator codes
• relation=Resolves — Diagnostic → TaskGuide fix procedure

Interpretation context:
• Framework BML defines what types ARE — TypeRegistry SSOT
• Renderers interpret what types MEAN for their target — free manifestation
• Hosts may also evaluate deterministic Capability implementations (doc:CapabilitySemantics)
• README references with ReadFirst establish shared vocabulary before diving into definitions
• After the first ten ReadFirst documentation blocks, most of the core library can be derived
  directly from Block definitions themselves

Each registered BlockDefinition from TypeRegistry bootstrap is an immutable BomDocument parse
result.

397.name: CapabilitySemantics
397.documentation:
There are no special language concepts for constructor, getter, setter, or render — all
behaviour is expressed as ordinary Capabilities: init(), getValue(), setValue(), render(),
parseValue(), and domain-specific operations. Package: org.blockml.bml.capability.* (base
org.blockml.bml.core.Capability).

A Capability implementation is a language-tagged body. It may serve one or more of these
readings — no ranking, no model restriction to a single use:

• Intent — PseudoCode or a natural language (English, German, …). Humans and LLMs read the
  contract; no host is required to execute the body.
• Companion template — a target-language body (TypeScript, Java, OpenSCAD, …) that a
  renderer or companion transpiles or emits. org.blockml.bml.service.Math TypeScript
  implementations are this reading.
• Host-evaluable function — a deterministic body a toolchain (validator, parser, runtime)
  may execute. The host chooses which language it evaluates; BlockML does not require
  TypeScript or any other language.

The compiler/renderer reading — map init() to a constructor, ignore a body, emit a method —
remains valid. It is one interpretation in a compiler pipeline, not a rule that the BOM
must not contain executable behaviour.

Capability kinds describe payload shape — they are not compiler rules or runtime objects:
• Inbound — receives input from outside (setValue, configure); requires inputType; no outputType
• Outbound — produces output to outside (getValue, emit); requires outputType; no inputType
• Transformation — maps input to output (compute, format, parse); requires both
• Action — performs a side effect or command (trigger, reset, refresh); no inputType, no outputType
Async reply via replyTo is a runtime/message pattern — not modeled on the Capability.

inputType and outputType are ValueTypes. Host encodings (TypeScript number, Java int, …)
are FunctionMapping / host concerns — not the BML signature (doc:FunctionMappingModel).

throws lists Exception types the Capability may raise — the BlockML equivalent of a Java
method throws clause. The aggregation type is type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]
(def:CapabilityDefinition). Children are type references, not Exception instances — empty-QName
sugar such as <io:FileNotFound /> names a type that must extend
org.blockml.bml.core.Exception. Omitted or empty throws means no declared exceptions. Exception
instances carry message:Text; domain libraries define concrete exception types. Distinct from
org.blockml.bml.core.Diagnostic (validator and parser codes). A host that evaluates a body
maps a thrown Exception to a Diagnostic when it reports a validate/parse failure.

Unqualified Capability type resolves to org.blockml.bml.capability.*; unqualified inputType /
outputType resolve to org.blockml.bml.type.* (doc:ImplicitNamespaceResolution). General block
references (aggregation type, association type, baseType) have no implicit namespace.

Authoring: declare under <capabilities> with a camelCase name (visibility prefixes apply —
doc:MemberVisibility). In a Composition the Capability value is the address or binding —
attribute on the child Block instance, like a Property value. Private Capabilities (__name)
cannot be bound from outside the declaring Block; protected (_name) follow the formal access
rule including derived Blocks and the direct composition owner.

Each Capability may carry an implementation whose language attribute references a Language FQN
(org.blockml.bml.language.*). utility Sub-Blocks (baseType Entity) commonly host Transformation
implementations — doc:SubBlockModel. Preferred dialect for intent: PseudoCode
(doc:PseudoCode). A compiler renderer may still map names to target constructs:

init()     → Java constructor · UI5 onInit() · React useEffect()
getValue() → direct field access · generated getter · reflection
setValue() → direct field assignment · generated setter
render()   → SCAD module · JSX component · may be ignored
parseValue() → host-evaluable parse of authored text (doc:ValueTypeParsing)

A Block's public surface is Capabilities — internal structure (Properties, Aggregations)
is not the outward API.

398.name: CompilerArchitecture
398.documentation:
Overview only — normative Urmodell / Pragmatic / BomBuilder rules live in docs/01_bom_core.md;
pipeline stages and packages in docs/06_compiler.md; system layout in docs/00_system.md.

Sketch: BML → Parser → Urmodell (immutable Canonical BOM) → Validator pragmatic fork /
Framework Utilities / Render Target pipeline → target output. Serializer reads the Urmodell only.
Validation Stages 1–3 (Parser / Validator / Renderer) — glossary in 06_compiler.md.
Semantic validation is the validator and the LSP. XSD is not a standard check; the XSD
compiler remains available but is not used by default (doc:DocumentFormat).
Self-hosting: CLI bootstraps TypeRegistry from framework BML before user projects.

In this compiler pipeline a Capability body is often a companion template the renderer
emits, or a name the renderer maps to a target construct. That is one interpretation
(doc:CapabilitySemantics). Hosts — including a future validator that evaluates
PrimitiveType.parseValue — may execute a deterministic implementation body. The model
does not forbid executable Capability implementations.
398.idea: A guide to the compiler pipeline

399.name: CompositionModel
399.documentation:
A Composition fills an Aggregation with concrete child Block instances. On Block definitions,
<composition> is nested inside the aggregation member. On Block instances, aggregations are
filled directly by member name — no <composition> wrapper. Do not treat composition as a
general-purpose container; the parallel Property mistake is wrapping instance values in
<value> — both are definition fields, not instance wrappers (doc:MemberAuthoring). The
composition aggregation="…" attribute is removed.

Unified container concept — one idea, two forms:
• composition — initial fill of an aggregation inside a Block definition only
• bml:container — general virtual container everywhere else (Block instances)
Both support the same flow-control directives: bml:if, bml:each, bml:with (and future container
directives). See doc:BmlDirectives.

Placement rules:
• <composition> must always be nested inside an aggregation member — never standalone →
  BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION
• New aggregation declaration → type required
• Inherited aggregation override → override="true" required; type may be omitted (identical
  restated type → BML_REDUNDANT_AGGREGATION_TYPE)
• Block instances open aggregations directly — recursive nested structure is first-class

Child elements inside composition (or instance aggregation content) are Block instances:
• Tag name — Block type (FQN / xmlns QName)
• bml:id — composition instance identity; required when referenced or on bml:each (literal or
  Expression). Omitted on anonymous static children → auto-ID after directive expansion
• bml:version — optional exact-version assert on external type references; omitted → TypeRegistry
  / library context; no match → BML_UNKNOWN_VERSION. Same-document Sub-Block refs omit version
• bml:bean / bml:scope — optional service bean registration (local | context; default local)
• bml:generics — required when the instance type still has open genericTypes; parenthesized
  TypeExpression list matching a baseType application (parentheses required). Attribute or
  child element. Missing → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE. Not on an instance →
  BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED. Incompatible args → BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH
  (doc:GenericsModel)
• Member attributes / child elements — property and nested aggregation values (literals or
  ${ … } expressions)

Instance ID reachability is controlled by the aggregation member's visibility — not by flags on
composition or bml:container. Public aggregations export ids for cross-document
{EnclosingBlockFQN}::{id}; protected and private narrow reach as in doc:MemberVisibility.
Qualified cross-document references require a public target aggregation and a literal static
bml:id.

Recursive composition: every Block instance may contain aggregation members directly — complex
object structures nest wherever instances appear.

Sibling value sharing: use bml:with on a common ancestor (composition or bml:container). Variables
are visible to the element and all descendants — no separate registry. Full expression grammar
lives in doc:Expressions; V1 implements property references, #built-in calls, and bml: directives
(including bml:with). @bean / @model: / capability linking are specified but not V1-implemented.

Meta-model: AggregationDefinition.composition (Sub-Block Composition) maps to BOM
CompositionTemplate. Service binding uses bml:bean and bml:scope on instances — not aggregation
member fields.
399.idea: A guide to composition and aggregation fill

400.name: ConstantValueType
400.documentation:
Constant provides singleton (constant) value domains in type expressions without a dedicated
literal-type language feature. Branch: ConstantType. Standard implementation:
org.blockml.bml.type.Constant.

Surface syntax — Constant(T){value: …}:
• (…) binds generic T to any ValueType (mandatory — bare Constant or Constant{value: …}
  without (T) is invalid)
• {value: …} configures the single allowed literal on the internal ValueType instance

External representation equals the representation of T — Constant(Text){value: "auto"} accepts
the external value "auto", not { value: "auto" }. Validation: first against bound type T, then
equality with the configured constant. No type inference — T is always authored explicitly.

Primary use — union alternatives:
Boolean | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}
Float | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}

Future literal shorthand Boolean | "auto" desugars to the Constant form; until enabled, author
Constant explicitly. Legacy literal unions remain parseable; normalize to Constant at map time.

Boolean.True / Boolean.False — Sub-Blocks of org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean; prefer these shortcuts
over spelling Constant(Boolean){value: true/false} in type expressions.

Obsolete wrappers migrate to Constant unions (doc:TypeExpressions): AutoOr<T> →
Constant(Text){value: "auto"} | T, FalseOr<T> → Boolean.False | T, etc.

Orthogonal mechanisms on one reference: Constant(SizeXY){value: {x: 1, y: 2}} — generic bind +
instance configuration (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). value is required (ValuePresent).
400.idea: A guide to Constant singleton types

401.name: ConstraintsModel
401.documentation:
Constraints are reusable validation rules attached via a single <constraints> container on
ConstrainableDefinition elements (Blocks and members). There is no target= property — the
embedding context binds the constraint automatically. Constraint branches declare genericTypes;
the compiler binds T from context (never authored):
• ValueConstraint on Property → T = effective ValueType
• PropertyConstraint → T = PropertyDefinition
• AggregationConstraint / AssociationConstraint / CapabilityConstraint → corresponding Definition
• BlockConstraint → BlockDefinition (incl. Sub-/Root-)
Wrong branch for context → BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH. Unknown constraint type →
BML_CONSTRAINT_UNKNOWN. Generic T incompatible → BML_CONSTRAINT_TYPE_MISMATCH. Instance property
incompatible with T → BML_CONSTRAINT_VALUE_MISMATCH.

Validation property (optional) references org.blockml.bml.validation.*:
• Error → BML_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION (fail compile)
• Warning → BML_CONSTRAINT_WARNING
• Information → BML_CONSTRAINT_INFORMATION
Omitted validation → constraint is metadata only (not value-enforced by the BlockML validator).

Standard value constraints include Min, Max, MinLength, MaxLength, MinItems, MaxItems, Pattern,
ValuePresent. Structural examples: RequiresMember, AllowedChildType, NoSelfReference,
MustBeReadOnly, RequiresImplementation.     Prefer ValueType instance configuration for
type-intrinsic thresholds (Text{maxLength: 100}); keep Constraints for contextual/composable
rules (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). Both run after PrimitiveType.parseValue accepts the
authored text (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

Suggestions — Property-only metadata: Block instances compatible with the property type for
editors/renderers. Not validation. Forbidden on EnumType properties → BML_SUGGESTIONS_ON_ENUM.
Incompatible suggestion instance → BML_SUGGESTION_TYPE_MISMATCH (PrimitiveType properties use
matching *Entity wrappers).

Procedure: task:AddConstraint.
401.idea: A guide to constraints and suggestions

402.name: ContractsModel
402.documentation:
Blocks may declare <contracts> at root level to compose one or more contract Blocks —
reusable partial definitions whose member fragments merge into the effective Block definition.
Declared only on the document root (not on nested Sub-Blocks). Child elements are direct Block
references (TypeReferenceEntity sugar — empty element is not an instance of the named Block).

baseType vs contracts:
• baseType — framework taxonomy and branch detection (extends); single inheritance; inBranch()
  uses the baseType chain only
• contracts — domain cross-cutting member mixins and type-bound identifiers (implements) via
  satisfiesTypeBound
Framework core branch types (ValueType, Entity, Language, Constraint, …) remain baseType markers
only — not duplicated as interface contracts in org.blockml.bml.*.

Semantics:
• Role — reusable partial Block definition (replaces interfaces / traits / mixins) plus type-bound
  identifier
• Scope — Properties, Aggregations, Associations, Capabilities, Constraints, Suggestions,
  documentation, examples, references, optional Capability defaults
• Ignored on contract types — subBlocks, embeddedBlocks, and compositions
• Partial members — contracts may declare incomplete members; the concrete Block completes them
  with override="true" (same rule as baseType refinement) → omission BML_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED
• Merge order — baseType chain → contracts (declaration order) → local Block declarations
• Conflict — later contract wins; Block overrides all contracts
• Override — only explicitly specified attributes replace merged values; final members from any
  layer cannot be overridden → BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE
• Validation — resolveEffectiveMembers() and satisfiesTypeBound() at Stage 2

Type bounds — satisfiesTypeBound(T, G) is true when G is on T's baseType chain OR G appears
directly in T.contracts[] (V1: no transitive closure through a contract's own contracts[]).
Used for generic bounds and polymorphic reference checks. Branch rules (inBranch) ignore
contracts.

Authoring tip: keep contract Blocks abstract with focused member fragments; complete defaults,
constraints, and documentation on the concrete Block with override="true". See
doc:PartialMemberOverrides for merge details and doc:ModelingGuidelines for when to prefer
baseType vs contracts.
402.idea: A guide to contracts and type bounds

403.name: CoreUseCases
403.documentation:
BlockML is designed around three core use cases. They build on the same principle:
**information is represented as a structured, semantic model instead of unstructured text or
implementation-specific data.**

## 1. Structured Project Documentation

BlockML can be used as a structured alternative to Markdown for project documentation.

Traditional documentation is primarily written for humans. Markdown improves readability and
portability, but its structure remains largely implicit. BlockML makes that structure explicit
while preserving human-readable content such as Markdown inside documentation blocks.

A BlockML document can therefore serve simultaneously as:

• documentation for humans,
• context for AI systems,
• structured input for software tools,
• and a machine-processable source for generated documentation.

Because BlockML has a defined object model and can be processed by parsers, validators,
compilers, and renderers, documentation is no longer merely text attached to a project. It
becomes part of the project's structured model.

    BML Documentation
          │
          ├──→ Human / AI
          ├──→ Markdown
          ├──→ HTML
          ├──→ BlockDoc
          └──→ other representations

The important distinction is that the generated documentation is not the source of truth.
**The BlockML model is.**

## 2. General-Purpose Domain Modeling

BlockML can describe arbitrary domains.

A domain defines its vocabulary as Blocks, types, properties, relationships, capabilities,
constraints, and compositions. Concrete models can then be expressed using that vocabulary.

BlockML itself does not prescribe what these models represent. They may describe software
systems, infrastructure, IAM configurations, physical objects, user interfaces, business
processes, documentation structures, or entirely new domains.

Renderers interpret these semantic models for a particular target. The same BlockML model may
therefore have multiple manifestations.

    Domain Model
         │
         ▼
        BML
         │
         ├──→ Renderer A → Code
         ├──→ Renderer B → Configuration
         ├──→ Renderer C → Documentation
         ├──→ Renderer D → UI
         └──→ Renderer E → Domain-specific output

The renderer determines the output format and interpretation; the model remains independent of
any particular target. This separation is fundamental to BlockML's renderer architecture.

**BlockML describes what something is. Renderers decide how that description manifests in a
particular environment.**

## 3. AI Workspaces

BlockML can serve as the persistent model of an AI workspace.

Instead of giving an AI a collection of documents and repeatedly asking it to produce new text,
the AI works directly on a structured BlockML model.

The model represents the current state of the work. The AI can inspect it, validate it, extend
it, and transform it while preserving explicit structure and semantics.

This makes it possible to represent not only the final result, but also intermediate states of a
process:

    Initial Model
         │
         ▼
      Analysis
         │
         ▼
    Planning Model
         │
         ▼
    Transformation
         │
         ▼
    Refined Model
         │
         ▼
     Validation
         │
         ▼
     Final Model
         │
         ├──→ Renderer
         ├──→ Compiler
         └──→ further AI transformation

Stages, tasks, decisions, constraints, intermediate results, and final artifacts can all become
explicit parts of the workspace rather than disappearing into prompts and conversation history.

The AI is therefore no longer primarily generating isolated outputs. **It is operating on and
evolving a persistent model.**

This turns BlockML from a representation format into a foundation for model-driven AI workflows:

> **The model is the workspace. The AI works on the model. Renderers manifest its current
> state.**
The three core use cases BlockML is designed around — structured project documentation,
general-purpose domain modeling, and AI workspaces — all built on one principle: information is
represented as a structured semantic model instead of unstructured text.
403.idea: A guide to the three core BlockML use cases

404.name: DefinitionModel
404.documentation:
Block definitions describe types. The Definition branch (org.blockml.bml.core.Definition) is the
meta-model for describing block structure in BlockML's own language — definitions are normal
Blocks that inherit from org.blockml.bml.core.Block like everything else.

Definition branch hierarchy:
• org.blockml.bml.core.Definition — abstract base of the Definition branch
• org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition — shared documentation model for structural definitions
• org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition — shape of every block document
• org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition — abstract base for block member declarations;
  override and boolean implementation; CapabilityDefinition overrides implementation
• AssociationDefinition — instance-to-instance model links (not documentation References)
• PropertyDefinition, AggregationDefinition, CapabilityDefinition
  (CapabilityDefinition.throws lists Exception types the Capability may raise —
  type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[], analogous to a Java method throws clause)
• GenericTypeDefinition

org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition declares:
• Properties: documentation, since, status, abstract, final
• Aggregations: changelog, examples, references
  (References connect types to types or types to instances for documentation —
  distinct from Associations)

Definition addressing uses canonical structural paths within the Block FQN:
com.foo.Bar.properties.width → PropertyDefinition
com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render → CapabilityDefinition
com.foo.Bar.references → Reference entries

Reflection resolves these paths via structural containers at query time — no special
definition-reference syntax. Definition blocks may declare bml:xml for how instances
serialize to canonical BML XML.

Definitions as Blocks means the same parser, TypeRegistry, and validation rules apply.
Domain-specific definition types can extend the branch with additional Capabilities
(validateDefinition(), generateDocumentation()) without core changes.
404.idea: A guide to the Definition branch

405.name: DocumentationModel
405.documentation:
Every root block definition carries a documentation model at the definition site — single
source of truth inside BML files:

Definition identity first (required at top of every Block document):
name / type / baseType — FQN identity before prose (baseType omitted only on org.blockml.bml.core.Block).
Preferred: the element tag supplies type on the document root and on embeds, and name
on Sub-Blocks (doc:DocumentFormat); <type> / <name> remain valid in the legacy
<block> form.

is (always required, after identity) — names the Idea (Urbild): what this Block semantically
  represents. Noun phrase; several words when name/type alone is too thin — not purpose and not
  full technical detail. Urbild is a fixed BlockML term (keep German explicit in meta-prose):
  English/French gloss + (Urbild); German docs may use Urbild alone. WOT: the Block itself is
  the Idea (Urbild); <is> names it in prose. Reflection: bml:Self.is. Omitted →
  BML_MISSING_IS. Motto: as simple as Lego at the designation; as powerful as SAP beneath.
summary (required when documentation is too long) — short prose expansion between is and
  documentation; inherited from StructuralDefinition on blocks and members. Missing when
  required → BML_MISSING_SUMMARY.
keywords aggregation (optional) — core.Keyword[]; domain FixedKeyword catalogue blocks, meta.FreeTextKeyword; shorthand → FreeTextKeyword only.
language (optional Definition meta — def:BlockDefinition.language) — natural language for
  documentation prose; inherits enclosing Library document language, then the English default
  authored on org.blockml.bml.core.Block.
documentation (always required on every Block definition) — technical description of the Block
  definition itself; Markdown(English) by default, with an optional language attribute
  (Markdown(NaturalLanguage) or a bare NaturalLanguage) when prose deviates from the effective
  block language. Omitted → BML_MISSING_DOCUMENTATION.
isNot (required when confusion risk exists, blocks only) — what this Block is not; block-level
  disambiguation. Reflection: bml:Self.isNot. Missing when required → BML_MISSING_IS_NOT.
aliases aggregation (optional, blocks only) — core.Alias[]; domain FixedAlias catalogue blocks, meta.FreeTextAlias; shorthand → FreeTextAlias only.
Member elements carry their own summary, keywords, and documentation for individual Properties, Aggregations, etc.

Optional extensions (wherever documentation is permitted):
since — version from which the element is available
changelog — container of change entries (oldest first)
examples — container of example entries (title in block natural language + CDATA body)
references — container of see entries (type, instance, file, url, or member path + relationship text)

Natural language inheritance (documentation prose and example titles) — Definition meta only,
not a core:Block / BlockLibrary member:
Library document <language> → Block document <language> → documentation / change / see
language attribute. Unqualified names inside <language> and on documentation, change, and
see language= resolve via org.blockml.bml.language.*. On documentation the natural language is
either the generic argument of Markdown (Markdown(German)) or the bare shorthand (German); on
change and see language= it is always the NaturalLanguage itself, since those bodies carry no
markup. Authors declare language only when deviating from the effective inherited language. Example title language always follows the
enclosing block — example language attribute applies to CDATA content only (implementation
dialect: OpenSCAD, TypeScript, …) and also resolves via org.blockml.bml.language.*.

## Documentation, Summary, Markdown and CDATA

`summary` and `documentation` serve different purposes and therefore use different content
models:

    summary         → plain text
    documentation   → Markdown(English) by default

### Summary

`summary` is a short, presentation-independent description for contexts such as lists, search
results, explorers, tooltips, and IDE tooling. It is **plain text** and does not support
Markdown:

    <summary>A generic block for describing a reusable component.</summary>

### Documentation

`documentation` is rich textual content and uses Markdown by default. The default is declared by
the documentation definition itself as `Markdown(English)`
(def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation.language), so authors normally **do not** write the
`language` attribute:

    <documentation>
    A **Block** is the fundamental unit of BlockML.
    </documentation>

is semantically equivalent to:

    <documentation language="Markdown(English)">
    A **Block** is the fundamental unit of BlockML.
    </documentation>

The explicit `language` attribute is only necessary when overriding the default. It is bound to
`Markdown(NaturalLanguage) | NaturalLanguage`: `Markdown` forwards `MarkupLanguage.L`
(NaturalLanguage, default English), so the natural language travels as the generic argument —
`language="Markdown(German)"` for German prose, `language="Markdown"` being the same as
`Markdown(English)`. A bare natural language stays valid as shorthand: `language="German"` means
`Markdown(German)`. Both forms denote the same i18n entry, so do not author them side by side on
one definition element.

### CDATA usage

Markdown itself does **not** require CDATA. CDATA is purely an XML serialization mechanism and
has no semantic meaning for documentation. The serialization rule is:

    no XML escaping required   → ordinary XML text
    XML escaping required      → prefer CDATA over entity escaping

Documentation should be ordinary XML text when nothing needs escaping. When the content contains
characters that would require escaping — especially `<` and `&` — the body is wrapped in a
`<![CDATA[` … section, because that keeps the authored Markdown readable. Preferred payload:

    Returns `true` when `value < maximum && enabled`.

Avoid entity escaping when CDATA can preserve the original content verbatim — the same payload
written as `value < maximum && enabled` is the form to avoid. This block itself is
serialized as CDATA for exactly that reason.

### CDATA terminators inside CDATA

XML CDATA sections cannot be nested: the sequence `]]` followed by `>` terminates the current
section. This occurs when Markdown documentation contains XML or BML examples that themselves
contain CDATA. A serializer must therefore split the CDATA section around such a sequence so
that the original text is preserved losslessly.

This is purely a serialization concern. Ordinary XML text, a single CDATA section, and split
CDATA sections all represent the same documentation content after parsing.

**Principle:** `Markdown(English)` is the default semantics of `documentation`; CDATA is only an
XML representation detail, used when necessary to keep BML readable.

### Human-friendly formatting

Block documentation is Markdown and should be written as such — in particular the main
documentation of a Block, and in particular for longer texts. Use paragraphs, headings, lists,
and inline code to make the structure visible. Long block documentation without paragraph breaks
is to be avoided; readable formatting for humans and LLMs is a central part of BlockML, not
decoration. `summary` stays a single plain-text paragraph — when documentation grows long enough
to need structure, that is exactly when summary becomes required.

Authoring split:
• documentation carries technical prose only
• references carries all documentation cross-links — types to types, types to packages, or types to instances
  (also Definition members, repository markdown files, and external URLs) — each with an
  explicit relationship note
• Associations connect instances to instances (model links); References do not form the
  instance graph — use associations for that
• Do not repeat cross-links in documentation prose

see target attributes — exactly one target kind:
type="core:ValueType" — Block or Definition type via xmlns prefix (TypeReference)
package="org.blockml.bml.type" — package string without a type segment (PackageReference)
instance="myId" / instance="foo:Bar::myId" — Block instance pointer (InstanceReference)
file="guide.md" — optional companion markdown in the consuming repository (not Core SSOT)
url="https://…" — external URL
property="com.foo.Bar.properties.width" — PropertyDefinition canonical path
aggregation="com.foo.Bar.aggregations.parts" — AggregationDefinition canonical path
association="com.foo.Bar.associations.parent" — AssociationDefinition canonical path
capability="com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render" — CapabilityDefinition canonical path
Split forms (still one target): type="com.foo.Bar" property="width" →
com.foo.Bar.properties.width in BOM; type="com.foo.Bar" instance="myId" → com.foo.Bar::myId.
(Retired attribute name: block= — use type=.)

relation attribute (optional) — Block reference to org.blockml.bml.relation.*; unqualified
names resolve via implicit namespace org.blockml.bml.relation.*. Omitted =
org.blockml.bml.relation.SeeAlso. Standard blocks: SeeAlso, ReadFirst, ReadNext,
ThenContinueWith, Extends, Requires, ContrastsWith, AuthoringGuide, Defines, DeepDive,
TaskIndex, TaskStep, Prerequisite, Resolves. README curates with ReadFirst; documentation
blocks chain with ReadNext.

README / ReadMe blocks (baseType org.blockml.bml.core.ReadMe) are library reading entry points
for humans and LLMs (Library.readMe). Curated reading order is expressed via references with
relation=ReadFirst; available tasks via relation=TaskIndex — not via separate aggregations on
ReadMe. Documentation blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.*) inherit from
org.blockml.bml.core.Documentation. TaskGuide blocks (org.blockml.bml.task.*) inherit from
org.blockml.bml.core.TaskGuide. Diagnostic blocks (org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.*) inherit from
org.blockml.bml.core.Diagnostic.

406.name: DocumentFormat
406.documentation:
Every Block definition wrapper is identified by its element tag: the document root, each
Sub-Block under `<subBlocks>`, and each embedded Block under `<embeddedBlocks>`. Two
authoring formats are valid during a long transition. The type-or-name-as-tag form is the
intended long-term format; the legacy `<block>` wrapper remains valid until it is withdrawn.

Existing sources in this library stay in the legacy form until they are migrated.

Member containers (`<properties>`, `<aggregations>`, …) and instance children are unchanged.
Instance serialization already uses the declared type tag (`<core:Block>`, `<myns:Wall>`).

## Qualified Blocks — document root and embedded Blocks

Legacy:

    <block>
      <name>MyBlock</name>  <!-- optional -->
      <type>acme:MyBlock</type>
      …
    </block>

Preferred:

    <acme:MyBlock>
      <name>MyBlock</name>  <!-- optional -->
      …
    </acme:MyBlock>

The element QName is the type. Prefixes resolve via xmlns Package bindings
(doc:BmlNamespace). Child `<type>` is omitted when the tag already supplies the type.
Optional `<name>` must still equal `lastSegment(resolve(type))` when present
(BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH).

Embedded Blocks use this same authoring as the document root. Their identity is still an
independent FQN — `resolve(type)`, not nested under the root (doc:SubBlockModel).

## Unqualified Blocks — document root, Sub-Blocks, and optional embeds

Legacy:

    <block>
      <name>MyBlock</name>
      …
    </block>

Preferred:

    <MyBlock>
      <name>MyBlock</name>  <!-- optional, not recommended -->
      …
    </MyBlock>

The local name of the element is the type (and the effective name). A redundant `<name>`
is allowed but not recommended. Unqualified roots and embeds follow the same identity rules
as unqualified type references (doc:TypeIdentityDerivation / doc:ImplicitNamespaceResolution).
Embeds still require a fully qualified resolved FQN
(BML_UNQUALIFIED_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE) — prefer the qualified tag.

## Sub-Blocks — unqualified name as the element

Sub-Blocks always use the unqualified form. The element local name *is* the Sub-Block name.
Type stays derived as `resolve(parent.type) + "." + name` (doc:TypeIdentityDerivation).

Legacy:

    <subBlocks>
      <block>
        <name>MyBlock</name>
        …
      </block>
    </subBlocks>

Preferred:

    <subBlocks>
      <MyBlock>
        <!-- <name>MyBlock</name> is optional and not recommended -->
        …
      </MyBlock>
    </subBlocks>

Child `<name>` may still be authored and must equal the element local name when present
(BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH). BML_MISSING_SUBBLOCK_NAME when neither the element tag nor
`<name>` supplies the name (legacy `<block>` without `<name>`). Visibility prefixes stay on
the logical name and therefore on the tag (`<_Utils>`, `<__Helper>`). Nested Sub-Blocks use
the same rule at every depth.

## Dual format

Parser, validator, and LSP accept both forms on the root, on Sub-Blocks, and on embeds.
New documents should use the type-or-name-as-tag form. Both remain valid until the legacy
form is withdrawn.

Identity rules (doc:TypeIdentityDerivation):

• Root and embed — type is required as canonical identity: the element tag and/or child
  `<type>`. BML_MISSING_BLOCK_TYPE / BML_MISSING_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE when neither supplies
  a type. When both supply a type, they must resolve to the same FQN.
• Sub-Block — name is required as local identity: the element tag and/or child `<name>`.
  Type is normally omitted and derived. When `<type>` is present it must equal
  `parentType + "." + name`.
• A generic `<block>` wrapper is not itself a type or name. In the legacy form, identity
  comes from `<type>` / `<name>`. In the preferred form the element tag *is* that identity.

## XSD is not a standard feature

`xmlns:xsi` and `xsi:schemaLocation` are omitted by default. XML Schema is not an officially
supported standard feature. The XSD compiler remains available; it is not used by default.
Semantic validation is the validator and the LSP.

Default `xmlns="http://blockml.org/bml"` and BML-semantic prefixes stay. Other URI bindings
(schemaLocation keys) are not BML-semantic type namespaces (doc:BmlNamespace).
`Library.schemas` remains an optional legacy catalog of XSD paths during migration
(doc:LibrarySystem).
Every Block definition wrapper — document root, Sub-Block, and embedded Block — uses
the type or name as its element tag. Legacy <block> remains valid during a long
transition. xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — validation is the
validator and LSP, not XSD.
406.idea: A guide to the BML Block authoring format

407.name: EmbeddedExpressions
407.documentation:
BML Embedded Expressions are language-neutral Capability references inside a Capability
<implementation> body. Delimiters: opening <$ · closing $>.

The implementation CDATA is source text of the language named by language= (OpenSCAD,
TypeScript, …). Regions wrapped in <$ … $> are BlockML Expression Language fragments. The
renderer replaces each embedded region (including delimiters) with equivalent target-language
syntax; surrounding text is copied unchanged. Embedded Expressions are not a separate
implementation language and not a replacement for <implementation>.

Supported call forms inside embeds (at least):
• #this.someCapability(...) — own Block Capability (required for self-refs; bare foo(...) not
  supported here)
• #math.max(...) / #strings.concat(...) — built-in services (same registry as ${ })
• @bean.someCapability(...) — Transformation Capability on a bound bean

Property access, operators, literals, and nested calls follow the same rules as ${ }
expressions unless noted otherwise. #this is the outer Block instance — the same binding as
${ }; it does not rebind in nested compositions. Bare this is a member (#this.this), not the
instance. Own-Capability calls in embeds still require #this.foo() (doc:Expressions).

Delimiter rules:
• Zero, one, or many regions per implementation body; multiline OK
• Whitespace immediately after <$ and before $> is ignored
• Nested delimiters forbidden
• Unclosed <$ → BML_UNCLOSED_EMBEDDED_EXPRESSION
• Invalid embed content → BML_INVALID_EMBEDDED_EXPRESSION
• Literal <$ or $> in implementation source must not appear outside a valid pair

Contrast with ${ } (member values):
• Host: BML attributes / <value> / directives vs implementation CDATA
• Own Capability: myCapa(...) or link vs #this.myCapa(...) only
• BOM: ExpressionValue.raw on members vs EmbeddedExpression { raw, start, end } on
  ImplementationBlock

See doc:Expressions for ${ } language, layers, V1 scope, and scope rules; doc:SubBlockModel
for utility Sub-Block implementations that commonly host embeds.
407.idea: A guide to embedded expressions in implementations

408.name: EverythingIsABlock
408.documentation:
BlockML describes everything that belongs to a World's grammar as Blocks. There is one root
(org.blockml.bml.core.Block), one parser, and one TypeRegistry bootstrap path — branch-specific
rules come from the baseType chain, not from parallel ontologies.

Everything is a Block means:
• Composable domain types (Wall, StandardBrick, Set) are Blocks
• ValueTypes (Integer, Size3D, Decimal) are Blocks — type definitions, not runtime values
• Languages (TypeScript, OpenSCAD, PseudoCode) are Blocks — capability implementation contracts
• Definition meta-model types (PropertyDefinition, StructuralDefinition sub-blocks) are Blocks
• Documentation blocks (this branch) are Blocks
• Libraries, Services, Constraints, Capabilities, Exceptions — all Blocks

Two layers must be distinguished:
• Authoring ontology (BML / WOT): Block = named definable unit with FQN and baseType chain
• Compiler internals: free representation — plain data, split indexes; no mandatory uniform
  runtime Block class hierarchy

One root · one registry · one parser. ValueTypes never store data — Properties own all concrete
values. The type describes nature; the Property owns the value.

409.name: Expressions
409.documentation:
The BML Expression Language is extended JSON inside ${ } delimiters. It appears wherever a
Block member value needs to be dynamic — derived, computed, or bound to a service. Capability
<implementation> bodies use the same language inside <$ $> embeds
(doc:EmbeddedExpressions). On type:Text, restricted ${ } holes may also appear in running
text — interpolation, not a whole expression value.

Four additions beyond JSON:
• Property references — myProp, myProp.x (StructType members by name only; no size[0] on structs)
• Model bindings — @model:/path, @model:relativeAttr
• Bean calls — @bean.capa(...) (call) · @bean.capa (capability linking, no parentheses)
• Built-in calls — #math.min(a, b), #strings.trim(s)

Everything else follows a JSON subset: double-quoted strings, numbers, booleans (true/True/TRUE
accepted; BOM stores lowercase), arrays [...], objects {...}. null is not a BML literal —
absent/empty is not typed as null.

Expression vs BOM data layer (separate):
• BOM stores LiteralValue, ExpressionValue.raw, and InterpolatedTextValue.raw — immutable
  authored form
• parseExpression() / parseInterpolatedText() → AST + type inference — utility output, not
  BOM mutation. Interpolation AST is Stage-2 only — not stored in the Canonical BOM
• evaluateExpression() / evaluateInterpolatedText() — renderer working model only (Stage 3);
  evaluateInterpolatedText runs at read time; the Canonical BOM is not rewritten
Validator checks correctness (members, visibility, types, capabilities) but never executes.

#this — one lookup everywhere:
• #this is the magic bean of the outer Block instance. The binding does not change inside
  nested compositions.
• this without # is not a keyword and not an alias for the instance. It is a member name
  (#this.this); a Property named this is allowed.
• Same rule in whole ${ } values and in interpolation holes:
  size ≡ #this.size · this ≡ #this.this · this.x ≡ #this.this.x · params.z ≡ #this.params.z
• #this.foo() inside <$ $> remains the required form for own-Capability calls
  (doc:EmbeddedExpressions).

Text interpolation (authored surface on type:Text — not a whole expression value, not
desugared to 'Hello ' + label):
myText="Hello this is ${ #this.label } bla bla"
Classification is on the entire member value:
• "${ expr }" (whole value) → ExpressionValue — full expression language
• "Hello ${ expr } world" → InterpolatedTextValue — Restricted Profile
• "Hello world" → LiteralValue
• \${ → literal ${ (not a hole)
• JSON that starts with [ or { stays LiteralValue even when string leaves contain ${
InterpolatedTextValue.raw is the entire authored text including holes. The serializer emits
raw 1:1, with no extra ${ } wrapper.
Top-level interpolation only on type:Text. On type:Text[] the member stays a LiteralValue
array; string leaves with unescaped ${ are checked and evaluated as interpolated text.

Restricted Profile (holes only — same as value-expression property/builtin subset):
Allowed: property access (size, #this.size, this, this.x, params.z); literals; + (Text /
Number); #strings.*; #math.*.
Forbidden → BML_EXPR_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_INTERPOLATION: @model, @bean, Capability linking /
own-calls, bml:each / bml:with variables.
Unclosed ${ → BML_EXPR_SYNTAX_ERROR. Interpolation on a non-Text member →
BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH. Nested ${ inside a hole is out of scope.

Scope rules:
• Property access — outer Block instance via #this (no parent/sibling climb); top-down
• @bean — walk composition hierarchy; bml:scope=context visible to descendants; local = declaring
  Block only
• #built-ins — always available; cannot be overridden
• @model: relative paths need binding context from nearest parent Model-bound Aggregation
• bml:each / bml:with variables — element + descendants; shadow outer same names
  (doc:BmlDirectives). Not visible in interpolation holes.
• <value> expressions — own Properties and #built-ins; topological resolve; cycles →
  BML_PROPERTY_CYCLE

FunctionMapping maps call arguments to Capability inputType (doc:FunctionMappingModel). Named
and positional must not be mixed under default mapping.

V1 supported: literals; operators + - * / % == != < > <= >= && || ! ?:;
property access myProp / myProp.x / myProp[i] (index only where valid — not StructType fields);
#math.min/max/abs/floor/ceil/round/pow/sqrt/clamp; #numbers.formatDecimal; #strings.concat/length;
#lists.size/get/first/last/sequence; bml:each/if/unless/container/with; interpolated Text holes
(Restricted Profile).
V1 deferred: @bean execution, model bindings, capability linking, most #strings/#bools,
TypeScript service transpilation.

Diagnostics (selection): BML_EXPR_SYNTAX_ERROR, BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY,
BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_BEAN, BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN, BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH,
BML_EXPR_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_INTERPOLATION, BML_EXPR_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH, BML_EXPR_LINK_*,
BML_EXPR_MODEL_NO_CONTEXT, BML_EXPR_BUILTIN_NOT_V1, BML_EXPR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO — plus
FunctionMapping codes.
Formal EBNF / AST shapes remain DeepDive in 10_expression_language.md (parser utility contract).
Expression language, #this lookup, and interpolated Text holes — authored surface
and BOM classification, not a toolchain pipeline.

410.name: FunctionMappingModel
410.documentation:
FunctionMapping translates between function-parameter lists and Capability inputType /
outputType. Concrete Mapping: org.blockml.bml.mapping.FunctionMapping.

Two application sites (opposite directions):
1. Expression calls — function syntax → FunctionMapping → Capability inputType
2. Capability implementation — inputType → FunctionMapping → target-language parameters
   (and reverse for returns)

Capabilities have no separate parameter list — only inputType / outputType. FunctionMapping
matters when a Capability is invoked as a function (built-ins, utility Sub-Blocks, expression
calls). Messaging transport ignores struct shape. Declared exception types live on
CapabilityDefinition.throws (type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]) and are not part of
FunctionMapping.

Host-language return types in an implementation body (TypeScript number, string, boolean) are
FunctionMapping / host encodings of the BML outputType — not a second type system.
PrimitiveType.parseValue has outputType bml:Self; a TypeScript number for Integer is mapping,
not the Capability signature (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

inputType shapes:
• Primitive → single positional or named argument
• Named StructType / anonymous struct { a: Float, b: Float } → arity = field count; names =
  declaration order
• Collection field { values: T[0..n] } → exactly one positional sequence argument — not
  fixed-arity multi-arg expansion
Anonymous struct field types are full TypeExpressions — qualified references, multiplicity,
unions, and nested anonymous structs included ({ list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer }). Arity
