and named keys come from the field list; the field types themselves do not change the mapping
(doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes).

Nested collection inputType — for a grouped, nested multiplicity such as (core:ValueType[])[]
(doc:TypeExpressions — Nested multiplicities) the collection rule above applies to the outermost
collection. A positional/variadic function representation may therefore map each function
argument to one element of the outer collection:

  inputType="(core:ValueType[])[]"
  #lists.concat([1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"])  →  [[1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]]

The inner collections stay ordinary typed values and are validated recursively against
core:ValueType[] — nesting changes the shape of the logical input value, not the mapping rules.

Canonical call forms normalize to the same logical input value (positional, named name=expr,
or object literal). Default FunctionMapping (when no explicit mapping is declared):
• Positional-only — arg i → field i in declaration order
• Named-only / object literal — keys = field names
• Mixed positional + named → BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS
• Too few / too many / unknown / duplicate → BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
  BML_TOO_MANY_FUNCTION_PARAMETERS, BML_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
  BML_DUPLICATE_FUNCTION_PARAMETER

Declaration order — same contract as StructType positional literals and ValueType instance
configuration {…} positional args (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). Member access in expressions
remains by name (point.x) — not numeric index on StructTypes.

Custom FunctionMapping on an implementation may reorder/rename parameters or reject forms.
Required custom mapping absent → BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_MAPPING (reserved until custom mappings
ship). Ambiguous custom mapping → BML_AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_MAPPING.

Default mapping properties on mapping:FunctionMapping: supportsPositional=true,
supportsNamed=true, supportsMixed=false.

411.name: GenericsModel
411.documentation:
Generic parameters belong exclusively to the Block that declares them — never inherited
implicitly. When a generic Block is used as baseType, the derived Block must account for every
base parameter by either binding it to a concrete TypeExpression in baseType or forwarding it
to a parameter declared on the derived Block. All bound → concrete; any forwarded → remains
generic. Resolution runs during inheritance: bound parameters are substituted throughout the
inherited definition. Validator checks: every base parameter accounted for, argument count
matches, each bound argument satisfies the parameter baseType (satisfiesTypeBound), forwarded
parameters are declared locally.

Type-level binding uses baseType application: a derived Block must bind or forward every base
parameter (PrimitiveEntity(T) → IntegerEntity with baseType PrimitiveEntity(Integer), etc.).
Instance-level binding uses bml:generics. A type whose genericTypes remain open after inheritance
cannot appear as an aggregation child unless bml:generics binds those parameters. Abstract
Blocks remain uninstantiable even with bml:generics.

Declaration — on the Block via <genericTypes> (meta-model GenericTypeDefinition). Parameter
name = XML element local name (<T baseType="…"/>). Optional defaultType when an application
omits the argument:
1. Concrete TypeExpression (e.g. type:Decimal)
2. Earlier sibling parameter name only (declaration-order DAG; no forward refs/cycles)
Resolution: authored args win → unbound params get defaults in declaration order → every
parameter must ground to a concrete TypeExpression → each binding satisfies baseType.
Diagnostics: BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_FORWARD_REF, BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_CYCLE,
BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_UNRESOLVED, BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.

BML attribute syntax — round parentheses: Box(Integer), TypeReference(core:Block),
InstanceReference(core:Block), SelectiveGrid(Boolean | type:HoleType). Each (…) argument is a
TypeExpression. With multiple parameters, labels match generic parameter names. At validate
time placeholders (T) are substituted; mismatch → BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.

Instance syntax — bml:generics on the Block instance (attribute or child element). The value is
only the parenthesized argument list; the type name is the instance tag. Parentheses are
required. Same TypeExpression grammar as baseType arguments. Authored args win; remaining
parameters take defaultType in declaration order. After resolution every parameter must be
concrete. Incorrect: <MyBlock someProp="Value"/> when MyBlock still has open T. Correct:
<MyBlock bml:generics="(type:Integer)"/> or
<TestBlock><bml:generics>(type:String, myns:MyBlock)</bml:generics></TestBlock>.
Open generic aggregated without the directive → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE. bml:generics
anywhere other than a Block instance → BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED. Argument list
incompatible with the instance's open genericTypes → BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH. Missing
required argument with no defaultType → BML_MISSING_GENERIC_TYPE_ARGUMENT. Ill-formed
TypeExpression → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE.

Orthogonal to {…} ValueType instance configuration (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration) and to
multiplicity brackets (doc:TypeExpressions).

Sub-Blocks / embeds may declare own genericTypes (Java static nested class model) — they do not
see enclosing generics; forward explicitly (Item(T)). Name collisions on the same declaring
Block with Block name or direct Sub-Block → BML_GENERIC_BLOCK_NAME_COLLISION /
BML_GENERIC_SUBBLOCK_NAME_COLLISION.

Constraint generics — Constraint branches declare genericTypes but arguments are never authored;
the compiler binds T from the <constraints> embedding context (Property → ValueType,
Aggregation → AggregationDefinition, Block → BlockDefinition, …). Branch ↔ context mismatch →
BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH. Validation property (Error/Warning/Information) controls
enforcement; omitted → metadata only.

412.name: ImplicitNamespaceResolution
412.documentation:
Unqualified block references are supported only at specialized, semantically unambiguous
reference sites. Each site defines exactly one implicit namespace. The name expands directly:

<Name> → <implicitNamespace>.<Name>

There is no multi-stage search, no global TypeRegistry fallback, and no document-scope
heuristics. If the expanded FQN does not exist or the Block does not satisfy the expected
base type for that site, the compiler emits an error.

Reference sites and implicit namespaces:
• Property type → org.blockml.bml.type.*
• Capability inputType / outputType → org.blockml.bml.type.*
• Implementation language attribute → org.blockml.bml.language.*
• language element child → org.blockml.bml.language.* (NaturalLanguage)
• language attribute on documentation → org.blockml.bml.language.*
  (Markdown(NaturalLanguage) | NaturalLanguage — the generic argument resolves in the same
  namespace)
• language attribute on change → org.blockml.bml.language.* (NaturalLanguage)
• language attribute on see → org.blockml.bml.language.* (NaturalLanguage)
• relation attribute on see → org.blockml.bml.relation.* (Relation)
• language attribute on example → org.blockml.bml.language.* (Language)
• status element content · bml:status attribute → org.blockml.bml.status.*
• Capability type → org.blockml.bml.capability.*
• Constraint validation attribute → org.blockml.bml.validation.*

Examples:
• <width type="Integer" /> → org.blockml.bml.type.Integer
• <implementation language="TypeScript"> → org.blockml.bml.language.TypeScript
• <language><English /></language> → org.blockml.bml.language.English
• <documentation language="Markdown(German)"> → org.blockml.bml.language.Markdown with
  L = org.blockml.bml.language.German (shorthand <documentation language="German"> resolves
  to the same entry)
• <change version="2.0.0" language="German"> → org.blockml.bml.language.German
• <see file="guide.md" language="English"> → org.blockml.bml.language.English
• <see type="core:Block" relation="Extends"> → org.blockml.bml.relation.Extends
• <example language="OpenSCAD"> → org.blockml.bml.language.OpenSCAD
• <status>Draft</status> → org.blockml.bml.status.Draft
• type="Transformation" on Capability → org.blockml.bml.capability.Transformation
• validation="Error" on constraint → org.blockml.bml.validation.Error

Resolution applies per type reference, including inside composed type expressions. In an
anonymous StructType on inputType / outputType, every field type is resolved on its own —
{ list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } resolves list via the xmlns prefix core and index via
the site's implicit namespace to org.blockml.bml.type.Integer. A qualified field type is never
ambiguous with the field-name separator (doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes).

General block references have no implicit namespace — baseType, aggregation type,
InstanceReference type arguments, and composition instance tags require a full FQN or xmlns prefix.
Explicit FQNs and xmlns prefixes remain valid everywhere, including at specialized sites.

413.name: Introduction
413.documentation:
BlockML is a universal declarative language for describing parametric, composable semantic
units called Blocks. BML (Block Markup Language) is the human- and editor-friendly authoring
format; the BOM (Block Object Model) is its canonical, immutable, lossless representation.

The BOM Compiler is domain-agnostic. It understands BML and the BOM object model. Domain-specific
knowledge lives exclusively in Render Targets — MachineBlocks (SCAD) is the reference
implementation, not the only possible World.

Key goals:
• One grammar for types, domain blocks, languages, services, and documentation
• Semantics in BML — behaviour as Capabilities, not compiler special cases
• Lossless BML ↔ BOM — the parser makes no semantic decisions
• Renderer freedom — each target decides how to manifest Blocks in its output
• Self-hosting bootstrap — the compiler loads framework BML before user content

BML file extension is .bml. XML is the sole BML serialization for V1 and V2 — a JSON
authoring form is not planned as an equivalent format. Every Block definition wrapper —
document root, Sub-Block, and embedded Block — identifies the Block by its element tag:
preferred type tag (<acme:MyBlock>) or unqualified name tag (<MyBlock>);
the legacy <block> form remains valid during a long transition (doc:DocumentFormat).
xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — XSD is not a standard
validation feature. Withdrawn roots such as device / sign / game stay withdrawn.

414.name: LibrarySystem
414.documentation:
A Library groups related Block and ValueType definitions into a publishable unit. Concrete
libraries use name Library, filename Library.bml, baseType org.blockml.bml.core.BlockLibrary.
FQN = {package}.Library from the file's package path.

Membership is defined exclusively by Library.bml blocks — not by directory layout. A .bml
file is a library member only if listed in that library's blocks. Without a Library block,
all .bml source files in the directory are public.

Structure (catalog aggregations are public and readOnly — inspectable from foreign Blocks;
authored only on the Library definition):
• readMe — required human/LLM reading entry (ReadMe, 1..1; typically README)
• bootstrap — optional automation SPOE (Bootstrap, 0..1)
• dependencies — other Library blocks (typical: inner library depends on outer)
• subLibraries — nested child Library blocks grouped under this library
• blocks — exported Block and ValueType definitions
• schemas — optional legacy XSD paths as FilePathEntity instances; XSD is not a
  standard feature (doc:DocumentFormat)
• version on Library.bml — framework convention: version only on Library for org.blockml.bml.*

Concrete Library.bml <references> — at most two <see> entries:
1. Required relation=ReadFirst → the ReadMe named in readMe
2. Optional relation=ThenContinueWith → the Bootstrap named in bootstrap (only when present)
No other relations on the catalog descriptor; deep links belong on documentation blocks.

Nested libraries may coexist at different package levels (org.blockml.bml.Library and
org.blockml.bml.compiler.Library are separate units). Typical pattern: inner library lists
outer in dependencies; outer lists inner in subLibraries. Violation: outer blocks
referencing a Block exported by an inner library → BML_LIBRARY_NESTING_VIOLATION.

Namespaces: xmlns prefixes map to FQN package prefixes. BOM stores canonical FQNs only —
prefixes are authoring convenience. Every BML definition must reside under
<domain>.bml.* — no Block, Library, or other BlockML definition may exist outside
the domain's bml namespace. See doc:BmlNamespace.

Version resolution:
effectiveBlockVersion = own version if present, else library.version if exported via blocks,
else error BML_MISSING_VERSION. bml:version on TypeReferenceEntity sugar (readMe, bootstrap,
dependencies, subLibraries, blocks) is an optional exact-version assert against the referenced
type (value); omitted → TypeRegistry / library context; no match → BML_UNKNOWN_VERSION.
414.idea: A guide to libraries and packages

415.name: MemberAuthoring
415.documentation:
LLMs repeatedly confuse member-declaration syntax with the syntax used when assigning members
on Block instances. The two most common mistakes are wrapping an instance Property in
<value> and wrapping instance Aggregation children in <composition>.

Incorrect on a Block instance:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty><value>Hello!</value></myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
<myns:MyBlock><content><composition>…</composition></content></myns:MyBlock>

Two contexts, never mixed:

1. Definition context — a Property or Aggregation is being declared inside <properties>
   or <aggregations> (or an inherited member is filled on a Block definition).
2. Instance context — a concrete Block instance receives Property values or Aggregation
   children.

<value> is the value field of def:PropertyDefinition. <composition> is the
composition field of def:AggregationDefinition. Both are definition-context fields. They are
not general-purpose wrappers around instance payloads.

Critical authoring rule — inside a Block instance:
• NEVER introduce <value> as a wrapper around a Property assignment
• NEVER introduce <composition> as a wrapper around Aggregation children
Instead: the Property element (or Block attribute) contains the value; the Aggregation element
contains the child Blocks. Group instance children with bml:container, not composition.

PROPERTIES — definition. Inside <properties> the child element is a PropertyDefinition.
Its default value is the value field of that declaration. Element form is preferred when
serializing definitions:
<properties><description><value>BlockML core library</value></description></properties>
Compact attribute form on the declaration is also valid:
<properties><description value="BlockML core library"/></properties>
Do not specify both forms on the same declaration (conflicting payloads). Other declaration
fields (type, readOnly, override, constraints, suggestions) stay on this PropertyDefinition
element — they are not authored on domain instances.

PROPERTIES — Block instance. The instance is not a PropertyDefinition. It only supplies the
payload. Attribute form is preferred:
<myns:MyBlock myProperty="Hello!"/>
Element form is the Property element with direct character content — the element itself is
already the value container:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty>Hello!</myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
Incorrect — definition value field used as an instance wrapper:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty><value>Hello!</value></myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
Also incorrect as a wrapper (same category error):
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty value="Hello!"/></myns:MyBlock>
unless myProperty is actually named value (see exception below).

Exception — member whose name is value. PrimitiveEntity, TypeReferenceEntity, FilePathEntity
and similar types declare a Property named value. Then value="…" or <value>…</value>
on the Block instance is ordinary instance syntax for that member, not a PropertyDefinition
wrapper:
<type:FilePathEntity value="blockml-library.xsd"/>
Annotation value facets (e.g. <scad:value> under a property declaration) are a separate
namespace axis on PropertyDefinition.value — not instance wrappers. See doc:AnnotationModel.

AGGREGATIONS — definition. Inside <aggregations> the child element is an
AggregationDefinition. Its initial/default child structure is the composition field:
<aggregations><content><composition><myns:Child/></composition></content></aggregations>
<composition> is allowed only as that definition field, nested inside the aggregation
member — never standalone (BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION).

AGGREGATIONS — Block instance. Child Block instances are placed directly inside the
Aggregation element. There is no composition wrapper:
<myns:MyBlock><content><myns:Child/></content></myns:MyBlock>
Incorrect:
<myns:MyBlock><content><composition><myns:Child/></composition></content></myns:MyBlock>
The same rule applies recursively — a Block instance nested inside a definition composition
still fills its own aggregations without a composition wrapper:
<aggregations><myAggr><composition>
  <myns:MyBlock><content><myns:Child/></content></myns:MyBlock>
</composition></myAggr></aggregations>
Outer <composition> is valid (myAggr is an Aggregation definition). Inner
<composition> under content is invalid (content is populated on a Block instance).

On instances, the virtual grouping element is bml:container — not composition. Both
composition (definitions) and bml:container (instances) host bml:if, bml:each, and bml:with.

Unified pattern:
Definition Property → value attribute or <value> wrapper on the PropertyDefinition
Definition Aggregation → <composition> wrapper on the AggregationDefinition
Instance Property → attribute on the Block, or direct Property element content
Instance Aggregation → direct child Block instances (bml:container for grouping)

Capabilities on instances follow the Property pattern: attribute or child element, no extra
wrapper. readOnly effective members must not be authored on instances
(BML_READONLY_MEMBER_WRITE). Declared exception types are the throws aggregation on the Capability
declaration — TypeReferenceEntity children (empty-QName sugar), not instance wrappers
(doc:CapabilitySemantics).
<value> and <composition> belong only to member declarations. On a Block instance
the Property element or attribute is already the value; the Aggregation element already holds
the child Blocks. Do not wrap instance payloads in those definition fields.
415.idea: A guide to definition versus instance member syntax

416.name: MemberVisibility
416.documentation:
Member and Sub-Block visibility controls BlockML access only — which definitions may reference,
read, or set a member or Sub-Block. It does not prescribe how a renderer manifests visibility.
Renderers always see the entire Canonical BOM (public, protected, and private). Visibility
restricts authoring access, not technical BOM access.

Naming convention (primary signal):
• myVar — public
• _myVar — protected
• __myVar — private

The prefix is BlockML visibility, not logical member identity. Collision checking uses the
normalizedLogicalName with visibility prefixes stripped (myVar / _myVar / __myVar → myVar).
Members that differ only by visibility prefix must not coexist in the same Block →
BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_VISIBILITY_VARIANT. A logical member exists exactly once with exactly one
visibility.

Override matching uses normalizedLogicalName. A child may redeclare with a different visibility
prefix only when the change widens access:
• protected → public — allowed
• private → any — forbidden (BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE)
• public → protected/private, or protected → private — forbidden (BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING)
Effective visibility and authored name come from the child declaration. Member-level bml:xml may
change on the same override.

Formal access (D = declaring Block, C = Block whose definition contains the access, I = instance
type, O = immediate composition owner of that instance):
• public — always
• private — only when C = D (owning composite does not gain access to private members of
  contained Sub-Block instances)
• protected — when C = D, or C inherits from D, or C = O, or C inherits from I.
  Only the immediate composition owner grants protected configuration access on children — not
  the entire outer composition hierarchy.

Aggregation members: visibility also controls which bml:id values may be referenced
(basePresets, Step.part, {BlockFQN}::{id}, …):
• public — cross-document {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{id}; unqualified ids within permitted access
• protected — declaring Block and its child Blocks (derived / Sub-Blocks in the same tree)
• private — declaring Block definition only
No separate export flag on composition or bml:container — reachability follows the aggregation
member's visibility. Qualified cross-document references require a public target aggregation and
a literal static bml:id.

Optional visibility property on members (and optional root-level visibility on Sub-Blocks) must
match the naming convention → mismatch BML_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH. Root Blocks must not declare
root-level visibility.

Validator diagnostics (access checks do not alter the Canonical BOM):
BML_PRIVATE_MEMBER_ACCESS, BML_PROTECTED_MEMBER_ACCESS,
BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_VISIBILITY_VARIANT, BML_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH, BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING,
BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE (private cannot be overridden).

Declared on org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition as visibility (and related override
rules). Sub-Block visibility uses the same naming convention — see also Sub-Block authoring
rules on org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition.
416.idea: A guide to member and Sub-Block visibility

417.name: ModelingGuidelines
417.documentation:
Inheritance (baseType):
• Single inheritance — each Block has exactly one baseType (mandatory except org.blockml.bml.core.Block)
• Use for branch membership (ValueType, Language, domain base) and shared member fragments
• Framework branches inherit via org.blockml.bml.core.ValueType, Language, or domain bases
• final on Block or member prevents further override → BML_FINAL_BASE_TYPE / BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE

Contracts:
• Reusable partial Block definitions — not pure interfaces; may include default implementations
• Use when multiple Blocks share a member fragment without sharing a common baseType ancestor
• Declared on root block only via contracts aggregation — direct Block references
• Merge order: baseType chain → contracts (declaration order) → local declarations
• Contract may supply partial members (e.g. id type only); concrete Block completes defaults,
  constraints, and documentation
• subBlocks and compositions on contract types are ignored

Capabilities:
• All behaviour — init, get/set, render, parse, domain operations — express as Capabilities
• An implementation may be intent (PseudoCode / natural language), a companion template,
  or a host-evaluable function — no ranking (doc:CapabilitySemantics)
• Prefer PseudoCode or natural language when the body is intent for humans and LLMs
• Use Inbound/Outbound/Transformation/Action kinds to describe payload shape
• Public surface of a Block is Capabilities — Properties are internal configuration
• Declare throws for Exception types the Capability may raise
  (type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[] — Java-style method throws; omit when none)

Constraints:
• Declare on Properties via constraints aggregation — Constraint Block instances
• Generic binding is automatic: Min/Max bind T from property type; MinItems/MaxItems from
  collection element type; MinLength/MaxLength from Text element type
• Use for validation rules expressible as reusable Constraint blocks (Min, Max, Pattern, …)
• Suggestions (optional Block instances of property type) guide editors — not validation

General: keep <is> stable; put cross-links in references; prefer explicit baseType over
implicit defaults; document partial members in contracts clearly.

Documentation formatting: block documentation is Markdown(English) by default — structure longer
prose with paragraphs, headings, lists, and inline code instead of one unbroken text; keep
summary plain text. Human-friendly formatting is a central part of BlockML
(doc:DocumentationModel).

418.name: PartialMemberOverrides
418.documentation:
Child Blocks override inherited members with override="true", or satisfy abstract implementation
obligations with a locally complete override. The flag is required whenever a local member
redeclaration merges with an existing member from the baseType chain or from contracts[] —
contract completion uses the same rule as baseType refinement.

Local declaration properties (never inherited; only effects propagate):
• abstract="true" — incomplete declaration; creates an implementation obligation
• final="true" — seals the declaration; descendants cannot override
• override="true" — confirms deliberate redefinition of an inherited member
Boolean properties require an explicit true or false — empty elements and bare attributes are
invalid. Preferred literals: lowercase true / false.

Modes:
• new — introduces a member; must not set override="true" → else BML_OVERRIDE_WITHOUT_PARENT
• override — refines an inherited member; omit override when merging → BML_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED
Each redeclaration layer must set override="true" again — override is not inherited.

Partial authoring: only the member name, override mode, and changed attributes need to be
specified — all other attributes are inherited from the parent definition. Omit unchanged type
(and other unchanged attributes such as bml:xml or defaults). On aggregations, restating an
identical type when only filling an inherited member → BML_REDUNDANT_AGGREGATION_TYPE (warning
V1). Declare type on an override only when refining or replacing the inherited type.

Abstract → implementation:
• Parent may omit required parts (e.g. property without type or value) when abstract="true"
• Child implements with override="true" and a locally complete declaration (abstract defaults
  to false → locally concrete)
• To keep a member abstract in a child, redeclare with override="true" abstract="true"
• Abstract member left unimplemented on a concrete block → BML_ABSTRACT_MEMBER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
Capability overrides supply a full implementation child element (not a boolean attribute).

Merge rules (resolveEffectiveMembers — baseType chain → contracts declaration order → local):
• Same member kind required (property overrides property, …)
• Only specified attrs replaced; unspecified attrs inherited
• Override matching key: (resolvedNamespace, normalizedLogicalName) — visibility prefixes
  stripped; xmlns prefix aliases may differ if they resolve to the same namespace
• Visibility may widen (protected → public); narrowing → BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING
• Member-level bml:xml may change on the same override
• Private members cannot be overridden → BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE
• final="true" on parent prevents override → BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE

readOnly is orthogonal to final / abstract / override: it controls instance authoring only.
• Block definition — may declare and set readOnly members via value, composition, or partial
  override
• Child Block definition — may override an inherited readOnly member (value/composition only;
  cannot override a final member at all)
• Block instance — must not set a member whose effective definition has readOnly=true →
  BML_READONLY_MEMBER_WRITE (after resolveEffectiveMembers on every BlockInstance)
• Expressions — may read readOnly members subject to visibility; renderers may read the BOM
A public readOnly member remains publicly readable. final blocks value overrides entirely;
readOnly does not.

Declared on org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition (abstract, final, override, readOnly,
visibility) and specialized on PropertyDefinition, AggregationDefinition, AssociationDefinition,
and CapabilityDefinition.
418.idea: A guide to partial member overrides

419.name: PseudoCode
419.documentation:
PseudoCode (org.blockml.bml.language.PseudoCode) is a ProgrammingLanguage for free-form
pseudocode Capability implementations. The code must be internally consistent but is
otherwise unconstrained — an LLM may interpret it. Content/text language follows
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) — declare L only when the prose
is not English.

Why PseudoCode exists:
• Capability implementations need a stable intent form that humans and LLMs can read
• PseudoCode avoids premature binding to Java, TypeScript, SCAD, or Python syntax
• Intent descriptions in PseudoCode stay stable across Worlds and hosts

When to use PseudoCode:
• Documenting intended behaviour on Capabilities during design (intent reading)
• Framework and domain blocks where the semantic contract matters more than a host body
• Blocks read by LLMs for code generation — PseudoCode is the preferred intent layer

When to use concrete languages:
• org.blockml.bml.language.TypeScript, OpenSCAD, Python, … as a companion template a
  renderer transpiles or emits, or as a host-evaluable function a toolchain runs
• Block definitions may restrict permitted languages via the languages aggregation

PseudoCode is the preferred intent dialect — not the only allowed implementation form.
A Capability may also carry a companion template or a deterministic host-evaluable body
(doc:CapabilitySemantics). A compiler renderer mapping names to target constructs remains
one valid interpretation, not a model restriction.

420.name: RendererFreedom
420.documentation:
The Render Target is free in what it produces and how it maps BML to output. No global rule
requires output to be blocks in the target language, 1:1 mapping input Block → one output
artifact, or any files at all (side-effects-only targets are valid).

Cardinality, format, and semantics are target-defined. The framework provides utilities;
each renderer decides which to use and in what sequence:

SCAD Renderer: resolveInheritance → evaluateExpression → expandComposition → renderSCAD
Java Renderer: resolveInheritance → resolveContracts → renderJava
Documentation Renderer: renderRawBOM() → Markdown / HTML

Each renderer owns an internal working model — optimised, cacheable, freely mutable:
SCAD: Modules, Parameters, GeometryGraph
Java: Classes, Fields, Methods
React: Components, Props, JSX Tree

The working model belongs exclusively to the renderer. The Canonical BOM remains unchanged.

MachineBlocks SCAD re-creates Blocks in the target language via mb_block() — a common pattern,
not a platform obligation. ScreenMachine may emit React JSX; EBOM may emit KiCad symbols.
The renderer reads BML Blocks; it does not need to preserve Block as a runtime concept in
its internal pipeline — only to emit correct target output.

Platonic mapping: BML holds the Idea (Urbild) stable. The compiler is Manifestor tooling —
it may represent the Idea internally as it chooses. Full Manifestation is the renderer's and
runtime's job in a specific World.

Treating Capability implementations as emit templates (or ignoring them) is the compiler
reading of doc:CapabilitySemantics — not a rule that Capability bodies cannot be
host-evaluable functions. A renderer or other host may execute a deterministic body.

421.name: SubBlockModel
421.documentation:
Sub-Blocks are Block definitions nested inside a parent Block — Java static nested classes: they
share the parent's FQN prefix, may declare own genericTypes, and have no enclosing-instance /
outer-generic scope (forward type parameters explicitly). Declared in <subBlocks> on a root
block, parent Sub-Block, or embedded block; may nest to arbitrary depth. Identity and FQN
derivation: doc:TypeIdentityDerivation. Unqualified nested names: innermost scope first.

Format: same fields as root Blocks; prefer omitting <type> (derived). baseType is required.
Preferred authoring uses the unqualified name as the element tag under <subBlocks>
(<MyBlock>…</MyBlock>); child <name> is then optional and not recommended.
Legacy <block><name>MyBlock</name>… remains valid (doc:DocumentFormat).
Must not declare embeddedBlocks → BML_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS_ON_SUBBLOCK.

Visibility — same naming convention and access model as members (doc:MemberVisibility):
• SubBlock — public (inside and outside enclosing definition)
• _SubBlock — protected (enclosing definition and derived Blocks)
• __SubBlock — private (immediately declaring Block only)
Differing only by visibility prefix → BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_VISIBILITY_VARIANT. Optional
root-level <visibility> on Sub-Blocks must match the name → else BML_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH;
when omitted, derive from name. Root Blocks must not declare <visibility> →
BML_VISIBILITY_ON_ROOT_BLOCK. Access diagnostics: BML_PRIVATE_SUBBLOCK_ACCESS,
BML_PROTECTED_SUBBLOCK_ACCESS.

Embedded Blocks (Inline Library) — virtual .bml files under root <embeddedBlocks>. Meta-model
EmbeddedBlockDefinition. Each embed is a full Block document; FQN = resolve(type), not nested
under the root. Authoring is the same as the document root: preferred type tag
(<acme:MyBlock>), legacy <block> plus <type> (doc:DocumentFormat). Root-only:
forbidden on Sub-Blocks and on embeds themselves (BML_NESTED_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS). type required
and fully qualified (BML_MISSING_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE / BML_UNQUALIFIED_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE).
Within the document, embed FQNs shadow library/file definitions; duplicates →
BML_DUPLICATE_EMBEDDED_BLOCK; externally invisible. Composition refs to embeds must use
fully qualified Block types.

Central distinction:
• SubBlockDefinition — semantically nested type
• EmbeddedBlockDefinition — virtual .bml in root embeddedBlocks
• RootBlockDefinition — document root; sole owner of embeddedBlocks

Composition Block references: empty child meaning depends on aggregation type (instance vs
TypeReferenceEntity sugar). Domain types need FQN or xmlns. Sub-Blocks of the enclosing root may
use unqualified local name inside that Block's composition; outside → qualified name / FQN else
BML_UNQUALIFIED_BLOCK_REFERENCE.

Naming vs parent: a Sub-Block should not share the root Block's name (…Calibrator.Calibrator);
bare short tags become ambiguous → BML_SUBBLOCK_QUALIFIED_REFERENCE_REQUIRED.

utility Sub-Blocks — baseType org.blockml.bml.core.Entity bind Transformation Capability
implementations (language = org.blockml.bml.language.*). V1: OpenSCAD (main function name =
Capability name; helpers allowed; compiler prefixes with block FQN) and TypeScript (compile-time
literal eval when args are literals). One implementation child per Capability; language required.
CDATA may use BML Embedded Expression (<$ … $>).
421.idea: A guide to Sub-Blocks and embedded blocks

422.name: TaskGuideModel
422.documentation:
Task-oriented paths complement ReadFirst learning paths on ReadMe entry points:

ReadFirst (relation)     — mental learning order on ReadMe / README blocks
TaskIndex (relation)   — catalog of accomplishable tasks on ReadMe
TaskGuide (branch)     — org.blockml.bml.task.* procedural how-to blocks
TaskStep (relation)    — ordered steps inside a TaskGuide (document order = step order)
Prerequisite (relation)— understand before starting a TaskGuide
Diagnostic (branch)    — org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* validator code documentation
Resolves (relation)    — Diagnostic → TaskGuide fix procedure

One mechanism: all navigation uses <references> and <see> with typed relation
attributes — no separate task aggregation on ReadMe. Automated process SPOE uses
Library.bootstrap (core:Bootstrap), separate from reading/task catalog on ReadMe.

Tooling (future):
• filter relation=ReadFirst → learn context bundle
• filter relation=TaskIndex → task menu
• load Diagnostic by code → follow Resolves → TaskStep chain

org.blockml.bml.README lists TaskIndex entries after ReadFirst entries. Future Bootstrap
subtypes (AgentBootstrap, CIBootstrap) supply automation SPOE members — not reading paths.

423.name: TypeExpressions
423.documentation:
Everything beyond the four ValueType kinds is a type expression — a use or combination of named
types, not a new BlockML type class.

ValueType = named semantic meaning (Primitive · Enum · Struct · Constant)
TypeExpression = usage or combination (multiplicity · union · generic application · instance
configuration · anonymous StructType · bml:Self · T)

Examples: Integer[] · Integer[3] · Integer[0..n] · Boolean | Integer · Box(Integer) ·
InstanceReference(core:Block) · SelectiveGrid(Boolean | HoleType) · Text{maxLength: 100} ·
{ x: Integer, y: Integer } · bml:Self · T

In type="…" XML attributes, generic applications use round parentheses (not angle brackets) so
values stay valid XML. Generic type arguments may be full type expressions — unions,
multiplicity, nested generics, and {…} configuration. Parentheses bind the argument:
SelectiveGrid(Boolean | HoleType) means T = Boolean | HoleType, not SelectiveGrid(Boolean) | HoleType.
When a parameter constrains baseType to ValueType (or another branch), every union alternative
must satisfy satisfiesTypeBound → else BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION. The same parenthesized
argument list is authored on Block instances as bml:generics (type name omitted; parentheses
required) — see doc:GenericsModel.

Obsolete wrappers → write unions directly:
• AutoOr<T> → Constant(Text){value: "auto"} | T
• FalseOr<T> → Boolean.False | T
• NoneOr<T> → Constant(Text){value: "none"} | T
• BooleanOr<T> → Boolean | T
• Array<T> → T[]
Boolean.True / Boolean.False are Sub-Block shortcuts for Constant(Boolean){value: true/false}.

Multiplicity — no separate Array type. Bracket notation is a postfix operation on a
TypeExpression, not an intrinsic property of a named ValueType; it is metadata on the type
reference and the FQN is unchanged. Prefer Collection / Multiplicity terminology (not Array).
Semantics only — ordered vs unordered and concrete storage are renderer-defined.
• Integer → exactly one
• Integer[] ≡ Integer[0..n]
• Integer[3] · Integer[1..5] · Integer[1..]
Applies commonly on aggregation/association types and capability input fields; bare properties
are usually exactly one value.

Nested multiplicities — multiplicity may be applied to any TypeExpression, including one that
already carries a multiplicity. Parentheses group the inner TypeExpression before the outer
multiplicity is applied, so nested collections need no separate Array or collection type:
• Integer[] → collection of Integer
• (Integer[])[] → collection of collections of Integer
• (Integer[3])[] → collection of fixed-size Integer collections
• (Integer[])[2] → fixed-size collection containing two Integer collections
Integer[][] is intentionally not supported — nested multiplicities must use explicit grouping
((Integer[])[]), which keeps the binding of each multiplicity unambiguous. Ungrouped stacked
brackets are ill-formed → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE.

Nested collections nest their rules too: compatibility, element-wise validation, and
multiplicity bounds are applied recursively, outer collection first. (core:ValueType[])[]
accepts [[1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]] — three elements against the outer multiplicity, each element
validated against core:ValueType[]; (Integer[])[2] rejects [[1], [2], [3]] with
BML_CARDINALITY_VIOLATION on the outer collection. For Capability inputs the ordinary collection
FunctionMapping rule applies to the outermost collection, so service:Lists concat with
inputType="(core:ValueType[])[]" maps #lists.concat([1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]) to
[[1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]] — one function argument per outer element, inner collections remaining
ordinary typed values (doc:FunctionMappingModel).

Collection compatibility — for a type reference with multiplicity, compatibility is evaluated
against the referenced element type. If S is assignable to T (S <: T), then a collection of S
values is assignable to a collection of T values, provided the source multiplicity is compatible
with the target multiplicity — collections are covariant in their element type:

  S <: T
  ---------------
  S[] <: T[]

With Integer <: Number <: PrimitiveType <: ValueType:
• Integer[] <: Number[] · Integer[] <: PrimitiveType[] · Integer[] <: ValueType[]
• Text[] <: ValueType[] · SomeStruct[] <: ValueType[]
• Integer[3] <: Number[] — but Integer[] is not assignable to Number[1..2] (bounds do not fit)
• Date[] <: Temporal[] · DateTime[] <: Temporal[] — Duration[] is not assignable to Temporal[]

A value assigned to a collection type is validated element by element against the referenced
element type. core:ValueType[] accepts zero or more values where every element's concrete
ValueType is assignable to ValueType — therefore:
• [1, 2, 3] → valid as Integer[], as Number[], and as ValueType[]
• ["a", "b"] → valid as Text[] and as ValueType[]

Heterogeneous collections — a collection type does not require all elements to have the same
concrete subtype. Each element is validated independently against the declared element type:
• ValueType[] : [1, "text", true] is valid, because Integer <: ValueType, Text <: ValueType,
  and Boolean <: ValueType
• Integer[] : [1, 2, 3] is valid — [1, "text", 3] is invalid, because Text is not assignable to
  Integer
An element whose type is not assignable to the declared element type is rejected
(BML_INVALID_PROPERTY on authored member values, BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH on expression payloads);
an element count outside the multiplicity bounds → BML_CARDINALITY_VIOLATION.

Unions — alternatives with |. Match order is left to right, first hit wins (no best-match).
Prefer narrower / sentinel alternatives on the left (Boolean | Text, not Text | Boolean).
Later alternatives that can never win → BML_UNREACHABLE_UNION_ALTERNATIVE (warning). Singleton
alternatives use Constant(T){value: …} (doc:ConstantValueType). Future literal shorthand
Boolean | "auto" desugars to Constant form.

Anonymous StructTypes — { field: Type, … } is the type-expression form of a StructType without a
declared name, and the mechanism for structured Capability inputs. An empty anonymous StructType
{} is type-equivalent to the named instantiable type:EmptyStruct. The grammar is recursive:

  AnonymousStruct := "{" StructField ("," StructField)* "}"
  StructField     := Identifier ":" TypeExpression

Because the right side of a field is a full TypeExpression — not merely an unqualified type name
— qualified type references, multiplicity, generic applications, unions, instance configuration,
and nested anonymous StructTypes are all valid field types:
• { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } — qualified reference with multiplicity
• { values: foo:Thing[1..n] } · { value: Integer | Text } · { nested: { x: Integer, y: Integer } }
• { lists: (core:ValueType[])[] } — nested multiplicity as a field type

The colon separating a field name from its type and the colon inside a qualified type reference
belong to different grammar levels and are unambiguous:

  list : core:ValueType[]
       ^     ^
       |     +-- prefix colon of a qualified TypeReference (xmlns prefix + local name)
       +-- field name / type separator

So { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } is one anonymous StructType with field list of type
core:ValueType[] and field index of type Integer. Field declaration order is significant — same
contract as named StructTypes (doc:FunctionMappingModel).

Braces are disambiguated by position: a { opening a type expression starts an anonymous
StructType whose field values are TypeExpressions; a { directly following a type reference is
ValueType instance configuration whose field values are literals — Text{maxLength: 100}
(doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). Each field type resolves like any other type reference at that
site: unqualified names via the site's implicit namespace (Integer → org.blockml.bml.type.Integer
on inputType / outputType), prefixed names via xmlns, full FQNs always
(doc:ImplicitNamespaceResolution).

Conformance note — an implementation that accepts { list: Integer[], index: Integer } but rejects
{ list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } is missing support for qualified type references
inside anonymous StructType fields. That is a parser / mapper limitation, not a semantic
ambiguity in the type expression.

Bare type name sites (Property type, Capability inputType/outputType) require ValueTypes (plus
type expressions over them). Aggregation type may be any Block FQN (plain composition or
TypeReferenceEntity application). Association type must be InstanceReference(T) or
InstanceReference(T)[] with T extending core:Block — bare Block FQNs are invalid.
Non-ValueType on a property → BML_INVALID_PROPERTY_TYPE.

Compiler-internal descriptors (UnionTypeDescriptor, …) are not BML Block classes.

424.name: TypeIdentityDerivation
424.documentation:
Every type name in BML — composition tags, identity type / baseType on definitions, member type
attributes — may be written in one of four forms. All normalize to a canonical FQN during
resolution:
1. Fully qualified name — com.foo.Bar
2. QName (xmlns prefix) — foo:Bar with xmlns:foo="com.foo"
3. Unqualified fallback — Integer at a context-bound site (doc:ImplicitNamespaceResolution)
4. Sub-Block-relative name — MySubBlock or foo:Bar.MySubBlock

Validator — declared ValueType wins, never the field name. type=, baseType=, abc=, or any
other name is irrelevant; only whether the field's type is-a TypeReference / TypeIdentifier /
PropertyReference / … matters:
• TypeReference / TypeReferenceEntity — FQN must resolve in TypeRegistry → else BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE
• TypeIdentifier (and not TypeReference) — syntax only; unknown FQN is valid
• PropertyReference / AggregationReference / … — path must resolve → else BML_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY
  (or BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE if the owning type cannot be resolved)
• MemberIdentifier / PropertyIdentifier / … — path syntax only
• InstanceReference — instance must resolve → else BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF
• InstanceIdentifier — id / path syntax only
Ill-formed syntax on any of these → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE (and, when a host evaluates
parseValue, BML_INVALID_VALUE). Syntax is PrimitiveType.parseValue; existence stays a
validator step on Reference types (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

An unresolved Reference is an error, but it does not mean the document is ill-formed. Like
Java class-not-found, it may be a typo or a missing dependency (library not on the current
classpath). Interpretation is left open.

Unqualified names on TypeReference fields require an explicit FQN or xmlns prefix — no
implicit fallback. Unresolvable → BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE. Ambiguous unqualified → BML_AMBIGUOUS_TYPE.
Undeclared QName prefix → BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX.

Sub-Block type references — Java static nested classes: own FQN prefix, optional own
genericTypes, no enclosing-instance and no outer type-parameter scope (forward explicitly, e.g.
Item(T)). Reference unqualified when in scope, as FQN, or as QName. The local part of a QName may
include a relative Sub-Block path (foo:Bar.MySubBlock).

Unqualified nested type resolution (innermost scope first, then enclosing chain):
On the current Block, in order: (1) own Block name, (2) own genericTypes, (3) own direct
Sub-Blocks. Then repeat for the immediate enclosing Block up to the document root. Grandchildren
are never unqualified — from Grid, Range does not resolve to Grid.Selector.Range; write
Selector.Range or Grid.Selector.Range. After the nested walk fails, context-bound implicit
namespace / FQN / xmlns rules apply. Generic / Sub-Block name collisions on the same declaring
Block remain errors (BML_GENERIC_*_COLLISION).

Root Block identity:
• type — required (BML_MISSING_BLOCK_TYPE); canonical identity. Preferred authoring: the
  document root tag is the type (<acme:MyBlock> / <MyBlock>). Legacy: child
  <type> under a <block> root. Both forms are valid during the transition
  (doc:DocumentFormat). When both the root tag and <type> supply a type, they must
  resolve to the same FQN
• name — optional; when omitted effectiveName = lastSegment(resolve(type)); when present must
  equal lastSegment(resolve(type)) → else BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH. On the preferred
  unqualified root, a redundant <name> is not recommended
• definition — optional; default RootBlockDefinition; unqualified via org.blockml.bml.definition.*

Sub-Block identity (opposite convention — unqualified name-as-tag, doc:DocumentFormat):
• name — required (BML_MISSING_SUBBLOCK_NAME). Preferred authoring: the element local name
  is the Sub-Block name (<MyBlock> under <subBlocks>). Legacy: child <name>
  under a <block> wrapper. When both are present they must match
• type — normally omitted; expectedType = resolve(parent.type) + "." + name; when present must
  equal expectedType (full parent path check, not last segment alone) →
  BML_SUBBLOCK_TYPE_MISMATCH
• definition — default SubBlockDefinition
• genericTypes / subBlocks — allowed; embeddedBlocks — forbidden
  (BML_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS_ON_SUBBLOCK)

Embedded Block identity (same authoring as the document root, doc:DocumentFormat):
• type — required and fully qualified (BML_MISSING_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE /
  BML_UNQUALIFIED_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE); preferred: the element tag is the type
  (<acme:MyBlock>). Legacy: child <type> under a <block> wrapper. FQN =
  resolve(type), not nested under the root
• name — optional; same matching rule as the document root
• definition — default EmbeddedBlockDefinition

Canonical derivation summary:
• Root / embed: canonicalType = resolve(type); effectiveName = name ?? lastSegment(canonicalType);
  if name present → name == lastSegment(canonicalType)
• Sub-Block: effectiveName = name (element tag or child <name>);
  expectedType = canonicalParentType + "." + name;
  canonicalType = type ? resolve(type) : expectedType; canonicalType == expectedType

See also doc:SubBlockModel (visibility, embeds, reference scope) and doc:BlockNameConvention.
424.idea: A guide to type references and Block identity

425.name: TypeSystemOverview
425.documentation:
BlockML knows four ValueType kinds at language level — each names a semantic meaning.
They are sibling branches under ValueType (not subtypes of each other):

PrimitiveType — atomic scalar semantics; no stored values on the type itself.
Examples: Boolean, Integer, Decimal, Float, Text, Color (Text subtype), URL, UUID, Version,
TypeIdentifier / TypeReference, PackageIdentifier / PackageReference, InstanceIdentifier /
InstanceReference, MemberIdentifier / PropertyIdentifier / …, Date, Time, DateTime, Duration.
PrimitiveType declares parseValue (Text → bml:Self). The TypeScript return is a host encoding;
outputType is always bml:Self (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

StructType — custom value objects; structure via properties.
Examples: EmptyStruct (no fields; only {}), Size3D, Address, Transform. Parameterized
types (Box(T)) are StructTypes with genericTypes — not a separate branch.

EnumType — closed set of named members; own ValueType branch (not a StructType). Allowed
members live in the values aggregation; BOM stores id + typeFqn only.
Examples: Direction, Face, StudType.

ConstantType — singleton value domain; one configured literal.
Example: Constant(Text){value: "auto"} for union alternatives.

Type expressions combine named types — they are not new BlockML type classes:
• Multiplicity: Integer[], Integer[3], Text[0..n] — postfix on a TypeExpression, so it nests via
  explicit grouping: (Integer[])[] (never Integer[][])
• Unions: Boolean | Integer, Constant(Text){value: "auto"} | Float
• Generic application: Box(Integer) · InstanceReference(core:Block) — round parentheses in type
  attributes; open generic instances bind the same (…) list via bml:generics (doc:GenericsModel)
• Instance configuration: Text{maxLength: 100}, Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2}
• bml:Self — resolves to effective current Block type after inheritance
• T — generic parameter reference from declaring Block's genericTypes

Assignability follows the branch hierarchy — a value of a subtype is accepted wherever a
supertype is required, with ValueType as the top of the value hierarchy:
Integer <: Number <: PrimitiveType <: ValueType. Date <: Temporal <:
PrimitiveType. Duration is a sibling of Temporal under PrimitiveType — not a Temporal subtype.
A type reference with multiplicity is compatible per element type: Integer[] <: Number[]
<: ValueType[], and each element of a collection is validated independently, so ValueType[]
also accepts mixed element types (doc:TypeExpressions — Collection compatibility · Heterogeneous
collections).

Only ValueTypes may appear where a bare type name is required (Property type,
Capability inputType/outputType). Aggregation type may be any Block FQN. Association type
must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[] — bare Block FQNs are invalid.
ValueTypes never store data — Properties own all concrete values.

Identifier vs Reference — parseValue on Identifier types checks syntax only. Existence is a
later validator step on Reference types (doc:ValueTypeParsing). The validator keys off the
declared ValueType of the field, never the property or attribute name (type= vs abc= is
irrelevant):
• TypeReference, PropertyReference / AggregationReference / …, and
  InstanceReference — the target must resolve in the current corpus. Unknown TypeReference
  → BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE; unknown PropertyReference → BML_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY (or BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE
  if the owning type cannot be resolved); unknown InstanceReference →
  BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF. Unresolved is an error, not proof the document is
  ill-formed — like Java class-not-found, it may be a typo or a missing library.
• TypeIdentifier, MemberIdentifier (PropertyIdentifier / …), and InstanceIdentifier —
  syntax only. Ill-formed → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE. An unknown but well-formed name is
  valid.
425.idea: A guide to the type system

426.name: ValueTypeConfiguration
426.documentation:
Curly braces configure the Property's owned ValueType instance — orthogonal to generic (...)
binding. The configuration applies to the type instance associated with a Property, not to
the ValueType definition block itself. Both may coexist: Box(Integer){minItems: 1}.
Multiplicity brackets apply after configuration: Text{maxLength: 50}[0..n].

Syntax examples:
• Text{maxLength: 100} — named configuration property (JSON-like key: value)
• Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2} — named precision and scale
• Decimal{10, 2} — positional by ValueType property declaration order (precision, scale)
• Constant(SizeXY){value: {x: 1, y: 2}} — nested object literals for StructType config values

Rules:
• Named and positional configuration must not be mixed in one {...} block →
  BML_MIXED_TYPE_CONFIGURATION
• Positional mapping follows declaration order — same principle as FunctionMapping
• Do not use key=value inside {...} (that is expression call syntax, not type configuration)
• Unknown config property → BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE_CONFIGURATION; value mismatch →
  BML_TYPE_CONFIGURATION_VIOLATION
• Generic application uses round parentheses: Box(Integer), TypeReference(core:Block)
• Constant(T){value: …} — generic (...) binds T; {value: …} supplies the singleton literal

Prefer multiplicity on the type reference for collection bounds (Text[1..10]) over List{…}
wrappers. Prefer inline configuration for type-intrinsic thresholds (Text{maxLength: 100});
keep Constraints for contextual/composable/business rules (Pattern, cross-property, …).

Configuration runs after PrimitiveType.parseValue accepts the authored text
(doc:ValueTypeParsing). parseValue does not read min / max / maxLength — those stay on the
Property's owned type instance.

ValueType definitions declare configuration Properties on the type block (e.g. precision and
scale on Decimal). Values live on Properties of Block instances — never on the ValueType
definition. There is no new Integer(5) in BlockML; the Property owns value 5 with type Integer.

Decimal is the default for non-integer numerics (3.5, 12.75). Float is special-purpose only
when binary floating-point semantics are explicitly required.

427.name: ValueTypeParsing
427.documentation:
PrimitiveType declares parseValue — a Transformation from authored Text to bml:Self that
throws exception:InvalidValueException. Concrete primitives implement a deterministic
TypeScript body (host-evaluable reading of doc:CapabilitySemantics). The BML outputType is
always bml:Self — the TypeScript return (number, string, boolean) is FunctionMapping / host
encoding, not the Capability signature.

parseValue is lexical only:
• Input is XML attribute or element text, already tokenized by the parser as Text
• Success means the text is a value of this PrimitiveType
• Failure throws InvalidValueException; a validating host reports diag:BML_INVALID_VALUE
• The body sees the type definition, not the Property's configured type instance — no
  this.min / this.max

After a successful parse, in this order:
1. Type instance configuration — Integer{min: 0, max: 100}, Text{maxLength: 50}
   (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration)
2. Property constraints — Pattern, Min, Max, … (doc:ConstraintsModel)
3. Existence checks on Reference types — TypeReference, InstanceReference, PropertyReference /
   … (doc:TypeSystemOverview). parseValue does not consult the TypeRegistry.

Inheritance: Text implements identity (every string is Text). Number implements a numeric
literal; Integer, Decimal, and Float refine. Temporal leaves parseValue abstract; Date, Time,
and DateTime implement ISO forms. Identifier types implement syntax; Reference subtypes inherit
that syntax and add existence in the validator.

parseValue does not cover multiplicity or unions (TypeExpression on the reference, element-wise),
StructType field walks, EnumType membership, or Constant(T){value} equality. Those stay
validator-side.

Bootstrap: the compiler still tokenizes framework BML as text. parseValue runs on loaded
property values after TypeRegistry bootstrap. Hard-coded bootstrap parsers for Text, Integer,
Boolean, and TypeIdentifier remain until a host evaluates these bodies.

428.name: WOTFoundation
428.documentation:
The Web of Things (WOT) provides the philosophical foundation for BlockML. Optional reading
for context — not required to use the compiler or author BML.

Idea (Plato):
The only true constant. Exists independently of Universes, Worlds, Technologies, and
Manifestations. An Idea does not change. In BlockML: Block, ValueType, Language, FQN —
describable without any render target. BML holds the Idea stable. The Block definition
itself is the Idea; the authoring field <is> (BOM block.is, reflection bml:Self.is)
names that Idea in an ultra-short noun phrase for humans and LLMs — it is not the Idea.

Manifestation:
The entire process from Idea to Thing — not a single step. Manifestor (compiler) produces
preconditions; Runtime completes Manifestation in a World the Manifestor cannot fully know.
In BlockML: renderer working model, target output, runtime behaviour. The renderer decides
interpretation — SCAD mb_block(), React components, KiCad symbols are different Manifestations
of the same Ideas.

Grammar (BlockML / BOM):
How Things are structured. Blocks are the grammar of a World. Types, Languages, Services,
and Capabilities are part of that grammar — not implementation detail. stud:// is how Things
communicate; BOM Core is how Things are structured.

World:
Delivers interpretation. An Idea carries no properties of its own — no substance, material,
or weight. The World assigns meaning. MachineBlocks is one World (physical geometry → SCAD);
other Worlds (ScreenMachine → React, EBOM → electronics) share type FQNs with different
render mappings.

WOT alignment at language layer: ontological unity in BML; engineering freedom in compiler
internals and renderer output. Without adoption, there is no WOT — and without internal
freedom, there is no maintainable compiler.
428.idea: A guide to the WOT foundation

429.name: InvalidValueException
429.documentation:
Thrown by PrimitiveType.parseValue when authored text is not a lexical value of this
ValueType. Inherits message:Text from core:Exception — the instance carries the reason;
the type is listed on the Capability throws clause.

A host that evaluates parseValue maps this Exception to diag:BML_INVALID_VALUE. Existence
failures (unknown TypeReference, missing instance) stay validator Diagnostics — they are
not this Exception. Type instance configuration and Property constraints run after a
successful parse (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

430.name: BlockGroup
430.documentation:
Abstract Group branch for block groups — named categories that organize Blocks
for editors and tooling. Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks.
Concrete group kinds extend this branch. BlockDefinition.groups overrides
StructuralDefinition.groups to TypeReferenceEntity(group:BlockGroup)[].

431.name: MemberGroup
431.documentation:
Abstract Group branch for member groups — named categories that organize Block
members (properties, aggregations, associations, capabilities) for editors and tooling.
A member may reference several groups via MemberDefinition.groups (e.g. UI category and usage
facet). Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks. Concrete group kinds
extend this branch. MemberDefinition.groups overrides StructuralDefinition.groups to
TypeReferenceEntity(group:MemberGroup)[].

432.name: BML
432.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for BlockML (BML) document implementations on Capabilities — block
definitions, library catalogs, and other structured BML markup. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L
(NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content/text language inside the BML body — bare BML
is BML(English).

433.name: C
433.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for C function implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare C is C(English).

434.name: Chinese
434.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and Chinese
natural-language capability implementations.

435.name: CPP
435.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for C++ function implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare CPP is CPP(English).

436.name: CSharp
436.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for C# method implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare CSharp is CSharp(English).

437.name: English
437.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and English
natural-language capability implementations.

438.name: French
438.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and French
natural-language capability implementations.

439.name: German
439.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and German
natural-language capability implementations.

440.name: Japanese
440.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and Japanese
natural-language capability implementations.

441.name: Java
441.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for Java method implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare Java is Java(English).

442.name: JavaScript
442.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for JavaScript function implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare JavaScript is JavaScript(English).

443.name: JSON
443.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for JSON document implementations on Capabilities — configuration,
structured data, or templates. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for
the content/text language inside the document — bare JSON is JSON(English).

444.name: Markdown
444.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for Markdown prose — documentation bodies and Markdown document
implementations on Capabilities — with lightweight structure (headings, lists, links, code
fences).

Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) is forwarded from MarkupLanguage and names
the content language of the Markdown body: Markdown = Markdown(English), Markdown(German) for
German prose. Because L is forwarded rather than bound, Markdown(NaturalLanguage) is a usable
type bound — def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation.language binds
Markdown(NaturalLanguage) | NaturalLanguage, where the bare-language alternative is shorthand for
Markdown in that language.

Also the default content language of documentation prose: Markdown(English) is the default value
of language on def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation, so every <documentation> body is
Markdown unless it declares otherwise. summary is plain text and never Markdown. CDATA is an XML
serialization detail — Markdown itself never requires it. See doc:DocumentationModel —
Documentation, Summary, Markdown and CDATA.

445.name: MarkupLanguage
445.documentation:
Abstract branch for markup languages — XML and other structured document formats
used as capability implementation bodies and, for Markdown, as documentation prose. Generic
parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) names the content/text language inside the markup
(element text, comments, human-facing labels, prose).

Concrete sub-types forward L via baseType MarkupLanguage(L) and redeclare it locally, so the
parameter stays open on the sub-type — Markdown(German) is authorable and Markdown(NaturalLanguage)
is usable as a type bound. Because L defaults to English, a bare sub-type name needs no argument:
Markdown ≡ Markdown(English). Binding L in baseType instead (MarkupLanguage(lang:German)) fixes
the content language for that sub-type and closes the parameter.

446.name: NaturalLanguage
446.documentation:
Abstract branch for natural languages used in documentation text, example
titles, and natural-language capability implementations. All locale-specific language blocks
(English, German, French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, …) must extend this branch —
not org.blockml.bml.core.Language directly. Distinct from implementation languages
(ProgrammingLanguage, MarkupLanguage) used in capability bodies and example content. Those
formal branches reuse NaturalLanguage as optional generic L (default English) when their
content/text language must be named.

447.name: OpenSCAD
447.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for OpenSCAD function implementations on Capabilities.
Emitted by the MachineBlocks SCAD renderer with FQN-prefixed function names. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare OpenSCAD is OpenSCAD(English).

448.name: ProgrammingLanguage
448.documentation:
Abstract branch for programming languages — TypeScript, OpenSCAD, PseudoCode, and
other languages with defined or interpretable syntax. Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage,
default English) names the content/text language of the formal code — for example pseudocode
prose, identifiers, or LLM-oriented wording.

Concrete sub-types forward L via baseType ProgrammingLanguage(L) and redeclare it locally, so the
parameter stays open on the sub-type — PseudoCode(German) is authorable and
PseudoCode(NaturalLanguage) is usable as a type bound. Because L defaults to English, a bare
sub-type name needs no argument: TypeScript ≡ TypeScript(English). Binding L in baseType instead
(ProgrammingLanguage(lang:German)) fixes the content language for that sub-type and closes the
parameter.

449.name: PseudoCode
449.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for free-form pseudocode implementations. The code must be
internally consistent but is otherwise unconstrained — an LLM may interpret it. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) — declare a content language only when
the pseudocode prose is not English, directly on this language (PseudoCode(German)); bare
PseudoCode is PseudoCode(English).

450.name: Python
450.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for Python function implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare Python is Python(English).

451.name: Russian
451.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and Russian
natural-language capability implementations.

452.name: Spanish
452.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and Spanish
natural-language capability implementations.

453.name: TypeScript
453.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for TypeScript arrow-function implementations on Capabilities.
V1: compile-time execution when all arguments are literals. Forwards ProgrammingLanguage.L
(NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers and comments — bare
TypeScript is TypeScript(English).

454.name: Unity
454.documentation:
C# dialect for Unity script implementations on Capabilities — MonoBehaviour methods,
UnityEngine APIs, and game-logic code. Forwards L on through CSharp (NaturalLanguage, default
English) for the content language of identifiers and comments — bare Unity is
Unity(English).

455.name: XML
455.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for XML document implementations on Capabilities — templates,
configuration, or structured markup. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English)
for the content/text language inside the markup — bare XML is XML(English).

456.name: YML
456.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for YAML document implementations on Capabilities — configuration,
structured data, or templates. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for
the content/text language inside the document — bare YML is YML(English).

457.name: Library
457.documentation:
Publishable BlockML core library (org.blockml.bml.Library). Exports the framework grammar:
core branches (Block, Annotation, ValueType, Language, Status, Relation, Constraint, Validation, Capability, Exception, Definition, Group),
group branch (org.blockml.bml.group.MemberGroup, org.blockml.bml.group.BlockGroup),
concrete value types and constraints, implementation languages, built-in services, lifecycle
status blocks, the Definition meta-model branch (org.blockml.bml.definition.*), the language
annotation (org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation), bootstrap
documentation blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.*), task guides (org.blockml.bml.task.*),
diagnostic blocks (org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.*), and definition metadata entities
(org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword, org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedAlias,
org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextKeyword, org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextAlias). FreeText* extends
Fixed* and widens protected members to public attributes. Domain libraries extend FixedKeyword
and FixedAlias for catalogue-controlled tags and alternative names.

Membership is defined exclusively by this file's blocks list — not by directory layout.
Version 3.0.0 applies to all exported blocks (framework convention: version only on
Library.bml).

458.name: FunctionMapping
458.documentation:
Concrete Mapping for function-like call syntax. Describes translation between a
function-parameter list and a Capability inputType or outputType.

Two application sites (opposite directions):
1. Expression calls — function syntax → FunctionMapping → Capability inputType
2. Capability implementation — Capability inputType → FunctionMapping → target-language
   function parameters (and reverse for return values)

Canonical call form passes a value matching inputType directly, using JSON-like syntax:
• Primitive → primitive literal
• StructType → object literal
• Collection → array literal

Helper syntax (when supported by this mapping):
• Named parameters — mapped by StructType property names; order irrelevant
• Positional parameters — mapped by property declaration order (mapping config only;
  does not create general StructType index semantics)

Default FunctionMapping (used when no explicit mapping is declared on an implementation):
• Primitive inputType — exactly one positional or named parameter
• StructType inputType — object literal (canonical), named parameters, or positional
  parameters by declaration order
• Primitive collection — positional parameters → array literal
• StructType collection — one outer parameter per struct instance → array literal
• Mixed positional and named arguments — not supported (BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS)

Capability implementations that require a target-language function signature must declare an
explicit FunctionMapping child when the default rules are insufficient.

Validation errors: BML_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION_PARAMETER, BML_DUPLICATE_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_PARAMETER, BML_TOO_MANY_FUNCTION_PARAMETERS,
BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS, BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_MAPPING,     BML_AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_MAPPING.

459.name: FixedAlias
459.documentation:
Protected base for domain catalogue Alias blocks. Extends org.blockml.bml.core.Alias
for controlled alternative names whose payload is authored once on the alias Block definition —
not at each <aliases> reference site. Domain libraries declare concrete alias blocks
extending FixedAlias and set protected members in <properties> (for example
<_name>Sub-Block</_name>). References in <aliases> are empty fixed blocks
(for example <vocab:SubBlockAlias />) — type FQN is the catalogue identity; name,
language, and legacy resolve from the alias definition.

org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextAlias extends FixedAlias and widens the same members to public
attributes (`_name` → `name`, …) for ad-hoc names configured per <aliases> reference —
visibility widening on override; see doc:MemberVisibility.
FixedAlias members use the protected naming convention (_*) and are set only on derived alias
block definitions — not on composition instances in <aliases>. Comma-separated shorthand on
<aliases> does not expand to FixedAlias instances.

460.name: FixedKeyword
460.documentation:
Protected base for domain catalogue Keyword blocks. Extends org.blockml.bml.core.Keyword
for controlled vocabulary tags whose payload is authored once on the keyword Block definition —
not at each <keywords> reference site. Domain libraries declare concrete keyword blocks
extending FixedKeyword and set protected members in <properties> (for example
<_term>inheritance</_term>). References in <keywords> are empty fixed blocks
(for example <vocab:Inheritance />) — type FQN is the catalogue identity; term, language,
and weight resolve from the keyword definition.

org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextKeyword extends FixedKeyword and widens the same members to public
attributes (`_term` → `term`, …) for ad-hoc tags configured per <keywords> reference —
visibility widening on override; see doc:MemberVisibility.
FixedKeyword members use the protected naming convention (_*) and are set only on derived keyword
block definitions — not on composition instances in <keywords>. Comma-separated shorthand on
<keywords> does not expand to FixedKeyword instances.

461.name: FreeTextAlias
461.documentation:
Standard free-text specialization of org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedAlias for colloquial or
legacy alternative names on Block definitions. Extends FixedAlias and widens protected catalogue
members to public attributes via visibility widening (`_name` → `name`, same for language and
legacy) — see doc:MemberVisibility. Types are inherited from
FixedAlias and omitted on these overrides. Rendered as a direct child inside <aliases> (for
example <meta:FreeTextAlias name="Sub-Block" />). Comma-separated plain text on
<aliases> is shorthand that expands to FreeTextAlias instances only. For catalogue-controlled
alternative names, domain libraries define concrete Alias blocks extending FixedAlias (members
stay protected on the definition) or org.blockml.bml.core.Alias directly for empty identity-only
aliases.

Instance configuration: FreeTextAlias{name: "Sub-Block"}. Block-level only — members do not carry
aliases. Not XML namespace prefix aliases.

462.name: FreeTextKeyword
462.documentation:
Standard free-text specialization of org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword for ad-hoc RAG
and discovery tags. Extends FixedKeyword and widens protected catalogue members to public
attributes via visibility widening (`_term` → `term`, same for language and weight) — see
doc:MemberVisibility. Types are inherited from FixedKeyword
and omitted on these overrides. Rendered as a direct child inside <keywords> (for example
<meta:FreeTextKeyword term="inheritance" />). Comma-separated plain text on <keywords>
is shorthand that expands to FreeTextKeyword instances — one term per trimmed token. For
controlled vocabulary tags, domain libraries define concrete Keyword blocks extending
FixedKeyword (members stay protected on the definition) or org.blockml.bml.core.Keyword directly
for empty identity-only tags.

Instance configuration at type reference sites: FreeTextKeyword{term: "inheritance"}. Not to be
confused with XML namespace prefix aliases.

463.name: README
463.documentation:
README block for the BlockML core library. Start with references marked relation=ReadFirst —
thirty-six documentation blocks in mental learning order. The early entries form the BlockML
conceptual core — the core use cases, the type system, and the expression language
(${ } and <$ $>).
Later entries cover conventions, authoring rules (visibility, overrides, member authoring,
composition, annotations, directives, type identity, Sub-Blocks, contracts, constraints),
organisation, and background knowledge.

Library.bml points here via the required readMe aggregation (<blockml:README />).
Tooling filters references where relation=ReadFirst to build a curated learning context bundle;
relation=TaskIndex lists accomplishable procedural tasks for humans, agents, and CI. Automated
process SPOE uses Library.bootstrap (core:Bootstrap) — not this ReadMe.

464.name: AuthoringGuide
464.documentation:
Typical file= targets — repository markdown with authoring rules, examples, or
migration notes. Use when the link is procedural ("how to write…") rather than structural
(Extends) or optional background (SeeAlso).

465.name: ContrastsWith
465.documentation:
Use to disambiguate easily confused concepts — for example Sub-Block vs embedded Block,
contract vs baseType, Inbound vs Outbound capability. The context text body must explain the
difference explicitly.

466.name: DeepDive
466.documentation:
Use for file= or url= targets with long-form prose the reader may skip on first
pass. Distinct from Requires (mandatory) and AuthoringGuide (procedural). Typical for architecture
documents, WOT foundation, or specification deep-dives.

467.name: Defines
467.documentation:
Use when the referenced Block or Definition element is the formal specification
the current type conforms to — for example def:PropertyDefinition on a property member, or
core:Bootstrap on a README block.

468.name: Extends
468.documentation:
Use when the referenced Block is in the baseType chain or represents a branch the
current type belongs to. Typical type= targets only — not for file or url references.

469.name: Prerequisite
469.documentation:
Use on <see> entries at the start of a TaskGuide <references> container
— before TaskStep entries. Distinct from Requires (dependency of the current definition) and
ReadFirst (library-wide learning path). Prerequisite scopes to one task procedure.

470.name: ReadFirst
470.documentation:
Two uses:
1. Concrete Library.bml — required single ReadFirst <see> targeting the ReadMe named in
